children.translated_text: Oṃ, salutations to <s>Śiva</s>, whose body is pure consciousness.
Now begins the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñāvimarśinī</s> (Examination of the Recognition of the Lord).
and then wills to divide His own power into two branches,
He who, from the fullness beyond all manifestation, first illumines as 'I',
I worship that non-dual totality, whose essence is the supreme <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>.
whose nature consists in the states of opening forth, expansion, and closing back into His own essence,
Of the one established in the midst of the noble lineage of the <s>Śrotriya-Tryambaka</s> tradition, like a pearl,
a reflection of the wisdom of the venerable <s>Somānandanātha</s>,
who taught the means concerning the supreme subject, witnessed by nothing other than the Absolute,
the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) named <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition of the Lord), which is supremely pure—
I, <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, being a disciple of that lineage, compose this concise commentary on those <s>sūtras</s> (aphorisms),
having learned from the illustrious <s>Lakṣmaṇagupta</s>.

children.text: vṛttyā tātparyaṃ ṭīkayā tadvicāraḥ sūtreṣveteṣu granthakāreṇa dṛbdham /
children.translated_text: Through the <s>vṛtti</s> (gloss) the intended meaning, through the <s>ṭīkā</s> (commentary) the detailed examination—this was firmly established by the author in these <s>sūtras</s>.
Therefore, I shall properly explain the meaning of the <s>sūtras</s> for those of limited intellect, for the elucidation of the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition).
Whether for one of little understanding everywhere, or for one of great intellect in some matter,
or even for none other—this may be beneficial to oneself.

children.text: granthakāraḥ aparokṣamātmadṛṣṭaśaktikāṃ parameśvaratanmayatāṃ paratra saṃcikramayiṣuḥ, svatādātmyasamarpaṇapūrvam avighnena tatsampattiṃ manyamānaḥ, parameśvarotkarṣaprahvatāparāmarśaśeṣatayā parameśvaratādātmyayogyatāpādanabuddhyāprayojanam āsūtrayatiḥ ----
children.translated_text: The author, wishing to transmit to others the identity with the Supreme Lord, the power directly perceived by himself, by first offering his own identity, considering that the attainment of that will proceed without obstacles, and with the intention of establishing fitness for identity with the Supreme Lord through the remainder of the reflection on the excellence and devotion to the Supreme Lord, introduces the opening aphorism—
Having somehow attained the servitude of <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord), and wishing to benefit the people as well,
I shall demonstrate the recognition of Him, which is the cause of the attainment of all perfections.

children.text: iha prameśvaraṃ prati yā iyaṃ kāyavāṅmanasāṃ tadekaviṣayatāniyojanālakṣaṇā prahvatā sā namaskārasya arthaḥ / sā ca tathā kartum ucitā prāmāṇikasya bhavati , yadi sarvato namaskaraṇīyasya utkarṣaṃ paśyet / anyathā yuktim aparāmṛśataḥ aparamārthe 'pi namaskārodyatasya sāṃsārikajanamadhyapātitvameva / yathoktam
children.translated_text: Here, the meaning of salutation is the devotion characterized by the directing of body, speech, and mind exclusively toward the Supreme Lord. And such devotion is proper for one who is authoritative, if one sees the supreme excellence of Him who is worthy of salutation in every respect. Otherwise, for one who does not reflect upon reason, even if one is inclined toward salutation to an inferior object, one merely falls among worldly people. As it is said:
{Those tainted by attachment to limited knowledge do not find the Supreme Lord.}

children.text: iti / tāvati hi māyīyāśuddhavidyārāgakalāsaṃcāryamāṇasya paśutvameva / itarāpekṣayā tu katipayādhvottīrṇatayā samutkarṣo 'pi syāt / taduktam
children.translated_text: Thus. For to that extent, one who is impelled by <s>Māyā</s>'s impure <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), and <s>kalā</s> (limited agency) remains merely a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>). But in relation to others, there may be a relative superiority by having transcended some stages of the path. As it is said:
{For whom, seeing with genuine faculties Your unblemished glory,
does there not arise, even involuntarily, a desire for praising You as the boon-granter, setting aside all else?}

children.text: iti śrīmadvidyādhipatinā / etaśca āgamakāṇḍe nirūpayiṣyāmaḥ / tasmāt nikhilotkarṣaparāmarśanamapi tatra svīkāryam / yadyapi āyātadṛḍheśvaraśaktipātasya svayameveyamiyatī paramaśivabhūmirabhyeti hṛdayagocaram, na tu atra svātmīyaḥ puruṣakāraḥ ko 'pi nirvahati, sarvasya tasya māyāmayatvenāndhatamasaprakhyasyāmāyīyaṃ śuddhaprakāśaṃ svapratidvandvinaṃ prati upāyat|anupapatteḥ, vajigamiṣayā niḥśeṣotkarṣaviśeṣābhidhīyi-jayatyādiśabdānuvedhena parāmarśanīyam, iti namaskāre ākṣepyaḥ / jayapadodīraṇe 'pi tādṛśasamutkarṣātiśayaśālini svātmānamaprahvīkurvāṇasya taṭasthasya paramanātmopakāritvam iti samutkarṣaviśeṣākṣipta eva namaskāro 'vaśyamabhyantarīkāryaḥ, ityanayā yuktyā jaya-namaskāraikataraprakrame anyatarasya arthākṣiptatā avaśyamaṅgīkartavyā / vandana-namana-smaraṇa-pradhyānaprabhṛtīnāmapi namaskāra-jayatyarthamātraparamārthatvād iyameva vartanī / atrāyaṃ punargranthakṛtā tādṛk prakrama āśritaḥ, yatra dvayamapi idaṃ svaśabdaparāmṛṣṭameva / etacca padārthavyākhyānāvasara eva prakaṭībhaviṣyati / svaśabdaparāmarśaśca sarvajanahitatvādyuktiyuktaḥ, sa hi sarvasyaiva jhaṭiti hṛdayaṃgamaḥ, arthākṣiptastu katicideva prati svapratibhoditavāktattvāvamarśāsaṃbhavāt, vāktattvāvamarśaśūnyasya ca prakāśasyāprakāśakalpatvāt / etacca sphuṭībhaviṣyati / abhiprāyeṇa prasiddhajaya-namaḥ prabhṛtiśabdaśaṭyānāśleṣeṇa imāṃ saraṇim anusarasi sma granthakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus by the illustrious Lord of Knowledge (<s>Vidyādhipati</s>). And this we shall establish in the <s>Āgama</s> section. Therefore, the reflection on the totality of supreme excellence must also be accepted there. Although for one upon whom the firm descent of <s>Śiva</s>'s power has already come, this very ground of supreme <s>Śiva</s> itself approaches the field of the heart—and no personal effort whatsoever avails here, since all such effort, being of the nature of <s>Māyā</s> and resembling utter darkness, cannot serve as a means toward the non-<s>Māyic</s> pure light which is its very opposite—still, with the desire to express this, through the reflection employing words such as 'jayati' (he is victorious) which convey the eminence of particular supreme excellence, this is to be implied in the salutation. Even in the utterance of the word 'jaya' (victory), one who does not bow down before such an extraordinary eminence but remains a mere bystander cannot truly benefit the supreme Self—thus the salutation, which is necessarily implied by the particular supreme excellence, must be internalized. By this reasoning, when either 'jaya' or 'namaskāra' is employed, the other is necessarily implied. Since vandana (reverence), namana (bowing), smaraṇa (remembering), pradhyāna (meditation) and such also have their ultimate meaning in the sense of namaskāra and jayati alone, this is the proper path. Here, moreover, the author has adopted such an arrangement wherein both of these are explicitly referred to by their own words. And this will become evident at the appropriate occasion of explaining the terms. The explicit self-reference is justified by its being beneficial to all people, for it immediately reaches the heart of everyone, whereas what is merely implied reaches only a few, since the impossibility of reflecting on the truth of speech for those lacking such reflection, and since consciousness devoid of reflection on the truth of speech is as good as non-consciousness. This too will be made clear. With this intention, the author followed this path by not clinging to well-known conventional words such as 'jaya' and 'namaḥ'.

children.text: iha yadyatkiṃ cana(KSS: kiṃcit) sphurati tattadvakṣyamāṇeśvararūpasvātmaprathāmātram, tatra tu upāyopeyabhāvaprabhṛtiḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'pi yathāprakāśaṃ paramārthabhūta eva, prakāśasya anapahnavanīyatvāt / yadāha bhaṭṭativākaravatso vivekāñjane
children.translated_text: Here, whatever appears in any form is nothing but the self-manifestation in the form of the Lord to be described; and therein, even the relation of cause and effect, such as that of means and end, is ultimately real in accordance with its manifestation, since manifestation cannot be denied. As stated by the son of <s>Bhaṭṭa Tīvakara</s> in the <s>Vivekāñjana</s>:
{Of things, light itself... /}
and so forth,
{...is not destroyed by mere denial. /}

children.text:
ityantam / tatra tu kāryakāraṇabhāve 'pi kvacit paripūrṇasvātantryalakṣaṇamāheśvaryanāntarīyakatākroḍīkṛtānantaśakticakracumbitabhāvabhāvitaprathāntaravyacadhānaṃ cakāsti ; sa tu māyīyatvena sthāpayiṣyate , jaḍacetanādyavāntarabhedaśatasaṃbhinnaśca asau , tatkṛtaśca sarvo 'yaṃ niṣpādya ---- niṣpādakabhāvajñāpya-jñāpakabhāvāṃvabhāso lokavyavahārarūpaḥ / yatra tu śuddhasvātmarūpaprathātmakānuttaraśaktiśālinirargalasvātmaprakāśa eva māyīyaprathāntaravyavadhānavandhyo nibandhanam, tatra tasyaiva bhagavataḥ kāraṇatvam / eṣa ca anugrahalakṣaṇo 'ntyaḥ pañcamaḥ pārameśvaraḥ kṛtyaviśeṣaḥ parapuruṣārthaprāpakaḥ,
tannibandhanatvāt paramārthamokṣasya / anyatratyo hi apavargaḥ kutaścinmuktiḥ, na sarvata iti niḥśreyasābhāsa iti vakṣyāmaḥ / sa cāyaṃ dvitīyaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvo laukikānvayavyatirekasiddhaprasiddhakāryakāraṇabhāvavilakṣaṇatvāt sphuṭena rūpeṇāsaṃcetyamānaḥ kādācitkavastusadbhāvonneyaparamārthaḥ atidurghaṭakāritvalakṣaṇaiśvaryavijṛmbhābhāvitādbhutabhāvaḥ prathamakoṭisaṃbhāvanāśūnyakālikākārasvaprakāśāvaraṇanirākaraṇamanorathaśataduṣprāpa ityevaṃprakāraḥ kathamā dyotakanipātasahitena nirūpitaḥ 'kathaṃcit'; iti, kenacicca prakāreṇa parameśvarābhinnagurucaraṇasamārādhanena parameśvaraghaṭitenaiva / yathoktam
children.translated_text:
up to that point. Therein, however, even in the relation of cause and effect, there shines a certain expansion of an alternative manifestation, embraced by the circle of infinite powers that is inseparable from sovereignty characterized by complete and absolute freedom; but that will be established as being of the nature of <s>Māyā</s>, and it is divided into hundreds of sub-divisions such as insentient and sentient, and all this manifold appearance of the produced and the producer, the made-known and the maker-known, constitutes worldly transaction. But where the unobstructed self-luminosity endowed with the supreme <s>Anuttara-Śakti</s> (absolute power) whose nature is the manifestation of pure self-essence—where that alone is the ground, free from the veil of <s>Māyic</s> alternative manifestation—there, causality belongs to that Blessed One alone. And this is the fifth and final divine function characterized by <s>anugraha</s> (grace), which bestows the supreme goal of human existence,
since ultimate liberation is grounded in that alone. For liberation found elsewhere is freedom from some particular thing, not from everything—thus it is merely an appearance of the highest good, as we shall state. And this second type of causality, being different from the well-known cause-effect relation established through common worldly co-presence and co-absence, not being apprehended in a manifest form, having its ultimate truth to be inferred from the occurrence of occasional realities, being of a wondrous nature brought about by the display of sovereignty characterized by accomplishing the extremely difficult, being unattainable even by hundreds of aspirations for removing the self-concealment that has the form of beginningless self-luminous obscuration empty of even the initial stage of possibility—being of such a nature, it is described with the word 'kathaṃcit' (somehow) accompanied by the emphatic particle 'katham'; and by some means, through the worship of the guru's feet who are non-different from the Supreme Lord, accomplished by the Supreme Lord Himself. As it is said:
{The connection is extremely difficult to establish... /}

children.text: iti / ‘āsādya'; iti ā samantāt paripūrṇarūpatayā sādayitvā , svātmopabhogayogyatāṃ nirargalāṃ gamayitvā ; iyatā viditavedyatvena parārthe śāstrakaraṇe adhikāro darśitaḥ ; anyathā pratārakatāmātrameva syāt / paurvakālyena sāmanantaryam atra vivakṣitam / anyathā tu āsādanatāratamyaprāptau māyīyamalakalāpasaṃskāraprakṣaye kathaṃ paropadeśaḥ śakyakriyaḥ / saṃbhavanti hi māyāgarbhādhikāriṇo viṣṇuviriṃcādyāḥ , taduttīrṇā api mahāmāyādhikṛtāḥ śuddhāśuddhā mantra-tadīśa-tanmaheśātmānaḥ ; śuddhā api śrīsadāśivaprabhṛtayaḥ / te tu yadīyaiśvaryavipruḍbhirīśvarībhūtāḥ sa bhagavān anavacchinnaprakāśānandarūpasvātantryaparamārtho maheśvaraḥ , tasya 'dāsyam'; ityanena tatpratyabhijñopapādanasya mahāphalatvam āsūtrayati / dīyate asmai svāminā sarvaṃ yathābhilaṣitam iti dāsaḥ , tasya bhāva ityanena parameśvararūpasvātantryapātratā uktā / ‘janasya'; iti , yaḥ kaścit jāyamānaḥ tasya , ityanena adhikāriviṣayo nātra kaścinniyama iti darśayati , yasya yasya hi idaṃ svarūpaprathanaṃ tasya tasya mahāphalam , prathanasyaiva paramārthaphalatvāt , tasya ca pratibandhakasaṃmatairapratibandhanīyatvāt , na hi prathitamaprathitamiti nyāyāt / taduktam
children.translated_text: Thus. 'Āsādya' (having attained): having accomplished fully and completely in every respect, having brought about an unrestricted fitness for one's own enjoyment; by this, the authority for composing a treatise for the benefit of others is shown through the state of having known all that is to be known; otherwise it would be mere deception. Immediate succession with the prior state is intended here. For otherwise, when gradations in attainment are possible, and the accumulated impressions of <s>Māyic</s> impurities have not been dissolved, how could instruction of others be accomplished? For there exist authorities within <s>Māyā</s> such as <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Viriñca</s> (Brahmā) and others; and even those who have transcended that, the authorities of <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, the pure-impure ones—<s>Mantra</s>, <s>Mantreśvara</s>, and <s>Mantramaheśvara</s>; and even the pure ones such as <s>Sadāśiva</s> and others. But they have become lords through mere drops of His sovereignty—He, the Blessed One, <s>Maheśvara</s>, whose ultimate reality is the freedom whose nature is unlimited light and bliss. By the word 'dāsyam' (servitude) to Him, the author indicates the great fruitfulness of demonstrating the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition). 'Dāsa' (servant) means one to whom everything desired is given by the master—by this word, fitness as a vessel for the freedom that is the very nature of the Supreme Lord is stated. By 'janasya' (of the people), meaning 'of whoever is born,' he shows that there is no restriction here regarding who is qualified, for indeed, for whomever this self-manifestation occurs, for that person it bears great fruit, since manifestation itself is the ultimate fruit, and since it cannot be obstructed by what are considered to be obstructions—for what has been manifested cannot be made unmanifested. As it is said:
{Here there is no loss of effort, nor is there any adverse result;
even a little of this <s>dharma</s> (practice) protects from great fear.}
Thus. And by the supreme guru in the <s>Śivadṛṣṭi</s>:
{Once the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, which abides in all things, is known through a valid means of knowledge, through scripture, or through the guru's word,
with firm conviction and a steadfast mind,

children.text: karaṇena nāsti kṛtyaṃ kvāpi bhāvanayāpi vā /
children.translated_text: there is nothing further to be accomplished through any instrument or through meditation;
once gold is recognized, what use is there for testing and such?
The ascertainment should always be as firm as one's certainty regarding one's own father, mother, and such.}
'Janasya' (of the people):

children.text: anavaratajananamaraṇapīḍitasya ityanena kṛpāspadatayā upakaraṇīyatvamāha / apiśabdaḥ svātmanaḥ tadabhinnatām āviṣkurvan pūrṇatvena svātmani parārthasaṃpattyatiriktaprayojanāntarāvakāśaṃ parākaroti / parārthaśca prayojanaṃ bhavatyeva tallakṣaṇatvāt , na hi ayaṃ daivaśāpaḥ svārtha eva prayojanaṃ na parārtha iti ; tasyāpi atallakṣaṇatve sati aprayojanatvāt ; saṃpādyatvena abhisaṃhitaṃ yat mukhyatayā tata eva kriyāsu prayojakaṃ tatprayojanam / ata eva bhedāde 'pi īśvarasya sṛṣṭyādikaraṇe parārtha eva prayojanam iti darśayituṃ nyāyanirmāṇavedhasā nirūpitam
children.translated_text: By saying 'one who is constantly afflicted by birth and death,' he states that they are worthy of assistance as objects of compassion. The word 'api' (also), revealing the non-difference of others from one's own self, with completeness removes any room for a purpose other than the accomplishment of others' welfare in oneself.
Thus.
{That purpose with regard to which a person engages in action is called <s>prayojana</s> (motivation).}
'Icchan' (wishing):

children.text: iti icchāviṣayīkṛtasya phalasya pravṛtto hetutvaṃ śatrā darśayati / icchāśaktiśca uttarottaram ucchūnasvabhāvatayā kriyāśaktiparyantībhavati ---- iti darśayiṣyāmaḥ / upaśabdaḥ samīpārthaḥ , tena janasya parameśvaradharmasamīpatākaraṇam atra phalam / ata evāha
children.translated_text: By the present participle, he shows that the fruit, which has been made the object of desire, is the cause of activity. And the <s>icchā-śakti</s> (power of will) progressively swells in nature until it culminates in <s>kriyā-śakti</s> (power of action)—this we shall demonstrate. The prefix 'upa' means 'near'; by that, bringing the people into proximity with the nature of the Supreme Lord is the fruit here. Therefore he says:
'Samasta' (all):

children.text: iti / parameśvaratālābhe hi samastāḥ saṃpadaḥ tanniḥṣyandamayyaḥ saṃpannā eva , rohaṇalābhe ratnasaṃpada iva / pramuṣitasvātmaparamārthasya hi kim anyena labdhena , labdhatatparamārthasyāpi tadanyat nāsti yad vāñchanīyam / yaduktaṃ granthakṛtaivaḥ
children.translated_text: For upon attaining the nature of the Supreme Lord, all perfections (<s>saṃpadas</s>), being flowing emanations of that, are already accomplished—just as upon obtaining the <s>Rohaṇa</s> mountain, the wealth of gems is already obtained. For one who has been robbed of the ultimate reality of one's own Self, what use is anything else obtained? And for one who has obtained that ultimate reality, there is nothing else to be desired. As stated by the author himself:
Thus.
{For those enriched with the wealth of devotion, what else is to be sought?
And for those impoverished of it, what else is to be sought?}

children.text: ityevaṃ ṣaṣṭhīsamāsena prayojanamuktam , bahubrīhiṇā tu upāyaḥ sūcyate /

children.translated_text: 'Samastasya' (of all):
Of all that is of the nature of existence and non-existence, external and internal, such as blue, pleasure, and the like—
'saṃpat' (perfection):
<s>saṃpatti</s> (attainment), <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment), the manifestation of its true nature—of that,
'avāpti' (full attainment):
the establishment in reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>)—that itself is the
'hetu' (cause):

children.text: yasyāṃ tatpratyabhijñāyām , tathā hi ---- sphuṭatarabhāsasamānanīlasukhādipramānveṣaṇadvāreṇaiva pāramārthikapramātṛlābha iha upadiśyate / yadāha anyatraḥ
children.translated_text: of that <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition). For thus—through the investigation of the perceiver (<s>pramātṛ</s>) that is equivalent to the most vivid manifestation of blue, pleasure, and such objects of experience—the attainment of the ultimate perceiver is taught here. As stated elsewhere:
Thus, through the genitive compound (<s>ṣaṣṭhī-samāsa</s>), the purpose is stated; while through the possessive compound (<s>bahuvrīhi</s>), the means is indicated.
{The fulfillment of the reflective awareness that has been severed as 'this',
that resting in one's own essential nature which is the reflective awareness 'I am'—}
Thus. And likewise in the same text:
{The self-repose of <s>Prakāśa</s> (luminous consciousness) is indeed declared to be the <s>ahaṃbhāva</s> (I-sense);
and that very repose is said [to consist] in the non-obstruction of all dependence.
<s>Svātantrya</s> (absolute freedom), then <s>kartṛtva</s> (agency), the primary <s>Īśvaratā</s> (lordship) as well.}

children.text: iti / iyatā ca upāye atidurghaṭatvāśaṅkā parākṛtā / yadante nirūpayiṣyati
children.translated_text: Thus. And by this much, the apprehension that the method is exceedingly difficult to accomplish has been set aside. As he will establish at the end:
{This new path is easy to accomplish} (Ipv_4,1.16)
Of him,
of <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord),
<s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition),

children.text: pratīpamātmābhimukhyena jñānaṃ prakāśaḥ pratyabhijñā / pratīpam iti ---- svātmāvabhāso hi na ananubhūtapūrvo'vicchinnaprakāśatvāt tasya , sa tu tacchaktyaiva vicchinna iva vikalpita iva lakṣyate ---- iti vakṣyate / pratyabhijñā ca ---- bhātabhāsamānarūpānusaṃdhānātmikā , sa evāyaṃ caitra ---- iti pratisaṃdhānena abhimukhībhūte vastuni jñānam ; loke'pi etatputra evaṃguṇa evaṃrūpaka ityevaṃ vā , antato'pi sāmānyātmanā vā jñātasya punarabhimukhībhāvāvasare pratisaṃdhiprāṇitameva jñānaṃ pratyabhijñā ---- iti vyavahriyate ; nṛpaṃ prati pratyabhijñāpito'yam ---- ityādau / ihāpi prasiddhapurāṇasiddhāntāgamānumānādividitapūrṇaśaktisvabhāve īśvare sati svātmanyabhimukhībhūte tatpratisaṃdhānena jñānam udeti , nūnaṃ sa eva īśvaro'ham ---- iti / tāmenām
children.translated_text: <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition) is knowledge, illumination, directed inversely — that is, turned toward oneself. 'Inversely' means — for the self-luminosity [of consciousness] is not something never previously experienced, since its <s>prakāśa</s> (luminosity) is uninterrupted; but by its own power (<s>śakti</s>), it appears as if interrupted, as if conceptually constructed — as will be stated. And <s>pratyabhijñā</s> — having the nature of reconnecting what has appeared and is appearing, is knowledge of an object that has been brought face-to-face through reconnection, as in 'This is indeed that same <s>Caitra</s>'; in ordinary life too, when something known — whether as 'this is his son, of such qualities, of such form' or at the very least in a general way — when the occasion of its coming face-to-face again arises, the knowledge animated by reconnection is called <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition); as in 'This one has been made to recognize the king' and so on. Here too, when <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), whose essential nature is full power, already known through well-established <s>Purāṇas</s>, <s>Siddhāntas</s>, <s>Āgamas</s>, inference and other [means], comes face-to-face as one's own self, knowledge arises through that reconnection: 'Surely I myself am that very <s>Īśvara</s>.' That very [recognition]
I shall establish

children.text: iti / upapattiḥ saṃbhavaḥ , tāṃ saṃbhavantīṃ tatsamarthācaraṇena prayojakavyāpāreṇa saṃpādayāmi / tathā hi ---- saṃbhavati tāvad asau , avicchinnaprakāśatvāt ; nirodhakābhimatamāyāśaktisamapasāraṇamātrameva tu tatra upapādanam / pratyabhijñopapattau svaparavibhāgābhāve tadapekṣaṃ kartrabhiprāyādi asaṃbhāvyam iti parasmaipadaprayogaḥ / itthaṃ ca atra śloke yojanā , ---- maheśvarasya dāsyaṃ samastasaṃpallābhahetuṃ kathaṃcit āsādya , janasyāpi kathaṃcit tatpratyabhijñām āsādya prāpayya , upakāraṃ samastasaṃpallābhahetubhūtaṃ maheśvaradāsyātmakam icchan , tāmeva samastasaṃpatsamavāptihetukāṃ tatpratyabhijñām upapādayāmi /
children.translated_text: thus. <s>Upapatti</s> (establishment) means possibility; I shall bring about that possibility through the activity of a motivator, through a course of action capable of it. For — that [recognition] is indeed possible, since [consciousness's] luminosity is uninterrupted; the establishment there consists merely in the removal of the so-called <s>Māyā-śakti</s> (power of illusion) that is held to be the obstruction. Since in the establishment of recognition, in the absence of the distinction of self and other, the intention of an agent and such [attributions] dependent on that [distinction] are impossible — therefore the <s>parasmaipada</s> (active voice) construction [is used]. And thus the construction of this verse [is]: having somehow attained the servitude of <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord), which is the cause of obtaining all prosperity, and having somehow brought about for the people their recognition of Him — having led them to it — desiring to render them the benefit consisting of servitude to <s>Maheśvara</s> which is the cause of obtaining all prosperity, I establish that very recognition of Him which is the cause of attaining all prosperity.
Having attained —

children.text: iti āvṛttiyojane dvau ṇicau / iyati ca vyākhyāne vṛttikṛtā bharo na kṛtaḥ , tātparyavyākhyānāt / yaduktam
children.translated_text: in this, with the repeated construction, there are two causatives. And in this explanation, the <s>vṛttikṛt</s> (author of the <s>vṛtti</s>) has not exerted effort, since it is a commentary on the essential meaning. As he has said:
Thus.
{[The <s>vṛtti</s>] is occupied merely with elucidating the condensed <s>sūtra</s>-style exposition.}

children.text: iti / ṭīkākāreṇāpi vṛttimātraṃ vyākhyātumudyatena nedaṃ spṛṣṭam , asmākaṃ tu sūtravyākhyāna eva udyama -- iti vibhajya vyākhyātam / evaṃ sarvatra / evamanena ślokena abhidheyam , prayojanam , tatprayojanam , tatprayojanam , adhikārinirūpaṇam , guruparvakramaḥ saṃbandha -- iti darśitam / tathā hi ---- samastasaṃpallakṣaṇo vyākhyāto yo'rthaḥ pūrvaṃ puṇyapāpādau saṃsāramūlakāraṇe hetuḥ , sa eva pratyabhijñāyate anayā ---- iti karaṇavyutpattyā upāyaḥ iha lokottaramārgaṃ prati nirṇītaḥ , iti atidurghaṭakāritvalakṣaṇamaiśvaryam
children.translated_text: Thus. Even the commentator (<s>ṭīkākāra</s>), who undertook merely to explain the <s>vṛtti</s>, did not touch upon this; but our endeavor is to explain the <s>sūtras</s> themselves — thus it has been explained by making a distinction. So everywhere. Thus by this verse, the subject matter, the purpose, the purpose of the purpose, the purpose of that [purpose], the determination of the qualified student, the lineage through the great teachers, and the connection — have been shown. For — the meaning previously explained, characterized as all prosperity, which is the cause in the root-cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) such as merit and sin, that very [meaning] is recognized through this [work] — thus through etymological derivation of the instrumental case, the means toward the supramundane path has been determined here; thus the means has been indicated as the subject matter, pointing toward the sovereignty characterized by accomplishing what is supremely difficult,
{a new path} (Ipv_4,1.16),

children.text: iti śākhānte nirūpayiṣyamāṇaṃ sūcayatā upāyaḥ darśitaḥ abhidheyatvena / ata eva
children.translated_text: which will be established at the end of the branch. Therefore,
{For inert entities...} (Ipv_1,1.4)

children.text: ityupakramapūrvakaṃ ślokāntaraṃ bhaviṣyati / prayojanaṃ ca pratyabhijñopāyajñānam , tasya prayojanam pratyabhijñānam , tasyāpi prayojanaṃ samastasaṃpallakṣaṇapāramaiśvaryaikarūparathanam , tataḥ paraṃ nāstyeva , tasya sarvaparyantaphalatvādaṃśāṃśikayāpi / yaduktaṃ mayaiva stotre
children.translated_text: — thus, beginning with this introduction, another verse will follow. And the purpose is knowledge of the means of recognition; the purpose of that is the [actual] recognition; the purpose of that too is the attainment of supreme sovereignty characterized as all prosperity and identity with it; beyond that there is nothing further, since it is the ultimate fruit even in its partial aspects. As I myself have said in a hymn:
{The fruit of actions, or else of injunctions, is ultimately identity with You alone, O Lord;

children.text: pahlepsavo ye punaratra teṣāṃ mūḍhā sthitiḥ syādanavasthayaiva //}
children.translated_text: those who desire further fruit here — their state would be one of confusion, due to infinite regress.}
Thus. This he will state:
{Placing his foot therein} (Ipv_4,1.16)
Of the people —
by this word the qualified student is indicated. As he will conclude:
— with these two quarter-verses.
{Constantly entering} (Ipv_4,1.16)
Somehow —
by this word the lineage through great teachers [is indicated]. He will state:
thus.
{As was declared by the great teachers in the <s>Śivadṛṣṭiśāstra</s>} (Ipv_4,1.16)

children.text: iti / evaṃ pratyabhijñātavyasamastavastusaṃgrahaṇena idaṃ vākyamuddeśarūpaṃ pratijñāpiṇḍātmakaṃ ca , madhyagranthastu hetvādinirūpakaḥ ,
children.translated_text: thus. In this way, by encompassing all things to be recognized, this statement constitutes the <s>uddeśa</s> (enunciation) and the summary of the thesis; the middle portion of the treatise establishes the reasons and so forth;
{Thus demonstrated by me} (Ipv_4,1.16)

children.text: iti ca antyaśloko nigamanagranthaḥ -- ityevaṃ pañcāvayavātmakamidaṃ śāstraṃ paravyutpattiphalam / naiyāyikakramasyaiva māyāpade pāramārthikatvam ---- iti granthakārābhiprāyaḥ
children.translated_text: — and thus the final verse is the concluding passage — in this way, this <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) consisting of five members has its fruit in the instruction of others. The intention of the author of the treatise, that the very procedure of the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> has its ultimate validity in the <s>Māyā</s> level,
{The generality of the relation of action} (Ipv_2,2.1)

children.text:
ityādiṣu uddeśeṣu prakaṭībhaviṣyati -- iti tāvad granthasya tātparyam sujanaśca laukikeśvaraparicita īśvaraviṣaye janam anujīviguṇasaṃpannaṃ prakāśayati ,
janaviṣaye ca abhigāmikādiguṇasaṃpannam īśvaraṃ prakāśayati - iti
iyānarthaḥ sāmānyena ṣaṣṭhosamāsena darśitaḥ

children.translated_text: His recognition —

children.text: iti / etacchlokākarṇanasamaye ca śiṣyāṇām etadarthasaṃkramaṇakrameṇa parameśvaratādātmyameva upajāyate tāvat / tathā hi ----
children.translated_text: thus. And at the time of hearing this verse, through the process of transference of this meaning, identity with <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) indeed arises for the students. For —
Of the people —

children.text: ityākarṇanāt vayaṃ te jananamaraṇapīḍitā aparyupastavṛttayaśca , asmākamayam upakāram icchan , maheśvarasya dāsyam āsādya , samastasaṃpatsamavāptihetuṃ tatpratyabhijñām upapādayati ; tataśca tatpratyabhijñāmevaṃbhūtāṃ vayaṃ prāptā eva , itītthameva hi adhikāriṇi śāstrārthasya bimbapratibimbavat saṃkrāntiḥ loḍliṅādīnāṃ viṣayībhavati prathamapuruṣārtha uttamapuruṣārthe paryasyati , na tu tāṭasthyena ; adhikāryanadhikāriṇoḥ pratipattau viśeṣābhāvaprasaṅgāt / ārogyakāmāḥ śivāṃ sevantāṃ sevadhvam ---- iti vā vākyārthasya sevāmahai -- ityevaṃrūpeṇa adhikāriṇi dvitīyā kakṣyā saṃkrāntau , tṛṭīyakakṣyāmeva bhāvikoṭipatitāmapi puruṣārthasaṃpattim akālakalitasvarūpānupraveśena svātmīkṛtām abhimanyamāne , tata eva vitatasaṃvitsundaraparāmarśo pūrṇatābhimānapratilambhāt , anyasya tu anevaṃrūpatvenaiva anadhikāritā tāṭasthyaprāṇā ---- iti / tadāstām avāntarametat atigahanaṃ ca ---- iti sthitametat / etena ślokena īśvarasāṃmukhyaṃ vineyānāṃ prayojanādipratipādanaṃ ca kriyate ---- iti /
children.translated_text: from hearing this, [the students think:] 'We are those people afflicted by birth and death, with impaired faculties; desiring to render us benefit, having attained the servitude of <s>Maheśvara</s>, he establishes the recognition of Him which is the cause of attaining all prosperity; and thus we have indeed attained that recognition of such a nature.' For it is precisely in this way that the transference of the meaning of a treatise into the qualified student occurs, like an object and its reflection — it becomes the object of <s>loṭ</s> (imperative) and similar [verbal forms], the first-person meaning transforms into the second-person meaning, but not from a detached standpoint, since there would be the unwanted consequence of no distinction in the understanding of the qualified and unqualified. 'May those desiring health serve the auspicious one — serve!' — thus, when the meaning of the sentence has undergone transference into the qualified student as 'let us serve' in the second stage, and when in the third stage, even the future fruit which has arrived, [the student] considers it as already made his own through the entry into its nature without temporal limitation, and from that very [entry] arises the beautiful comprehensive awareness of expansive consciousness, from the attainment of the sense of fullness; whereas for another, the very fact of not being of this nature constitutes the disqualification sustained by detachment — thus. But let this subsidiary and exceedingly profound [matter] be set aside — thus it stands. By this verse, the turning of <s>Īśvara</s> toward [the students] and the communication of the purpose and so forth to those to be instructed — is accomplished.

will become manifest in such <s>uddeśas</s> (enunciations) and the rest — thus so much for the purport of the treatise. And the good person, familiar with the worldly lord, illuminates the people regarding <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) as endowed with qualities [befitting] a master's followers, and illuminates <s>Īśvara</s> as endowed with qualities of approachability and the like regarding the people — this much meaning has been shown in general through the genitive compound.
{The supreme vibration which illuminates the aggregate of infinite states

children.text: upoddhātāyate yasya taṃ stumaḥ sarvadā śivam //}
children.translated_text: serves as the prelude — we praise that <s>Śiva</s> always.}

children.text: nanu īśvarasya siddhireva kartavyā / keyaṃ siddhiḥ ? na tāvat utpattiḥ , nityatvāt / nāpi īśvarasiddhikārādayastasyopapattiṃ vidadhate / jñaptiḥ siddhiriti cet , anavacchinnaprakāśasya pramāṇavyāpāropādheyaprakāśātmakasiddhyanupayoga eva / nanu anavacchinnastadīyaḥ prakāśa -- iti kathametat ; nīlasukhādiprakāśe hi tatprakāśaḥ kutaḥ ? tadaprakāśe'pi suptamūrchādau nitarām , svaprakāśe'pi vā īśvare pramātḥṇāṃ kiṃ vṛttaṃ yena teṣāṃ pramāṇavyāpārānupayoga ityāśaṅkyāha
children.translated_text: Now, the very establishment (<s>siddhi</s>) of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) must be accomplished. What is this <s>siddhi</s>? It is certainly not origination, since [He is] eternal. Nor do the means of establishing <s>Īśvara</s> such as [inference] and others produce His establishment. If [you say] <s>siddhi</s> is cognition — for one whose luminosity is unlimited, establishment in the form of luminosity conferred by the operation of a means of knowledge is entirely inapplicable. But [you ask] how is His luminosity unlimited? For in the luminosity of blue, pleasure, etc., whence is His luminosity? And when that is not luminous, as in deep sleep, swoon, etc., all the more so. Or even if <s>Īśvara</s> is self-luminous, what has happened to the knowers that the operation of means of knowledge is inapplicable to them? — anticipating this objection, he says:
Regarding the Great Lord who is the agent, the knower, the self, primordially established —

children.text: ajaḍātmā niṣedhaṃ vā siddhiṃ vā vidadhīta kaḥ //
children.translated_text: who, being of non-inert nature, could produce either negation or establishment?

children.text:
iha ka īśvare kīdṛśe kīdṛśena pramāṇena asti iti jñānalakṣaṇāṃ siddhim , nāstīti jñānalakṣaṇaṃ vā niṣedhaṃ kuryāt ? pramātā iti cet , sa eva kaḥ ?
dehādirjaḍaḥ uta tadanyo vā kaścit ātmādiśabdavācyaḥ ? so'pi svaprakāśasvabhāvo vā na vā ? dehādirjaḍaḥ iti cet , sa eva svātmani asiddhaḥ paratra kāṃ siddhiṃ kuryāt ? ātmāpi asvaprakāśo jaḍa eva tattulyayogakṣemaḥ / svaprakāśasvabhāvaḥ iti cet , kīdṛśena svena rūpeṇa bhāti ? yadi pariniṣṭhitasaṃvinmātrarūpeṇa , tadā saṃvidāṃ bhedanam , bheditānāṃ ca antaranusaṃdhānena abhedanaṃ na syāt ; tena svatantrasvaprakāśātmatayā tāvat sa bhāsate , bheditānāṃ ca antaranusaṃdhānena abhedanaṃ na syāt ; tena svatantrasvaprakāśātmatayā tāvat sa bhāsate , tathābhāsamānaśca kīdṛśamīśvaraṃ sādhayet niṣedhet vā ? kartṛjñātṛsvabhāvam iti cet nanu sa pramātaiva tathābhūtaḥ iti ko'nyaḥ saḥ ? nanu sarvakartṛtvasarvajñatve pramāturna staḥ ; na khalu sarvaśabdārtho jñātṛkartṛtvayoḥ svarūpaṃ bhinatti , bhedadarśane'pi īśvarajñānacikīrṣāyajñādernityasya viṣayeṇa akāraṇabhūtena anādheyātiśayatvāt / prakāśamānatānayanameva viṣayatvam iti cet , aprakāśasvabhāvasya tathātvamanucitam ---- iti vakṣyāmaḥ / prakāśamānasvabhāvatve viṣayo'pi sarvātmanā prakāśa eva nimagna iti prakāśaḥ prakāśate ---- ityetāvanmātraparamārthatve kaḥ sarvajñāsarvajñavibhāgaḥ ? , pramāṇamapi evaṃ siddhatvāsiddhatvābhyāṃ paryanuyojyam ; evaṃ siddhirapi / tasmāt viṣayābhimataṃ vastu śarīratayā gṛhītvā tāvat nirbhāsamāna ātmaiva prakāśate vicchedaśūnyaḥ , suṣuptamapi prati prakāśata eva , anyathā smṛtyayogāt ; prakāśasya ca nityatvāt vicchedahetorabhāvena , anyapramātrapekṣayā ca prakāśamānatvāt , svaparapramātṛvibhāgasya tatsṛṣṭasya māyīyatvena vakṣyamāṇatvāt / sa cāyaṃ svatantraḥ / svātantryaṃ ca asya abhede bhedanam , bhedite ca antaranusaṃdhānena abhedanam ---- iti bahuprakāraṃ vakṣyāmaḥ / etadeva asya pārameśvaryaṃ mukhyamānandamayaṃ rūpam ---- iti pūrvamupāttaṃ

children.translated_text: As the agent —

children.text: iti / tadeva tu svātantryaṃ vibhajya vaktuṃ
children.translated_text: thus. But that very independence, to state it analytically:
As the knower —

children.text: iti pañcānnirdiṣṭam / jñānapallavasvabhāvaiva hi kriyā ---- iti vakṣyate / tena sarvakriyāsvatantre sarvaśaktike ---- iti yāvad uktaṃ bhavet tāvadeva
children.translated_text: thus has been expressed in the fifth [case-ending]. For action is indeed of the nature of a sprout of knowledge — as will be stated. Therefore, all that is said amounts to [describing] the one who is independent in all actions, endowed with all powers —
As the agent, the knower —

children.text: iti / iyameva ca saṃvitsvabhāvatā / saṃviditi tu ucyamānā vikalpyatvena prameyatāṃ spṛśanto sṛṣṭatvāt na paramārthasaṃvit ---- iti vakṣyāmaḥ / kartā jñātā ca maheśvara ---- ityabhidhāne'pi sa eva prakāra āpatet , iti yathā yathā prameyabhūmikāpādananyakkārakalaṅkaparihāraḥ śakyaḥ tathā tathā yāvadgati yatitavyam , iti bhūtavibhaktyā nirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ / upadeśāvasare hi sarvātmanā tāvat sā prameyatā asya parihartum aśakyā /
children.translated_text: Thus. And this very nature of consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>) — but when spoken of as 'consciousness,' since it touches the state of being an object of thought (<s>prameya</s>) by becoming something conceptualized, being a created [verbal designation], it is not ultimate consciousness — this we shall state. Even when it is said 'the agent and knower is <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord),' the same manner [of objectification] would apply; therefore, to whatever extent it is possible to avoid the stain of reducing [consciousness] to the level of an object of knowledge, to that extent one must strive as far as possible — thus the designation is made using the past participle [form]. For at the occasion of instruction, its objectification cannot be entirely avoided.
In one's own Self (<s>svātmani</s>) —

children.text: iti , svasmin anapāyirūpe svabhāve ityanena , vaiśeṣikādyabhimatajaḍātmavādanirāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: thus, by [saying] 'in one's own nature that never departs,' the refutation of the doctrine of the insentient self (<s>jaḍātman</s>) maintained by the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> and others [is accomplished].
Primordially established (<s>ādisiddhe</s>) —
thus, meaning 'in whom the light (<s>prakāśa</s>) is uninterrupted.'
In <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord) —

children.text: iti , etadeva māheśvarya yad anavacchinnaparkāśatvena jñātṛkartṛtvadhāropārohaḥ /
children.translated_text: thus, this very sovereignty (<s>māheśvarya</s>) consists in the assumption of the role of knower and agent through being of unlimited light.
Of non-insentient nature (<s>ajaḍātmā</s>) —

children.text: iti , yasya tu vaiśeṣikāderjaḍa ātmā sa siddhiṃ karotu īśvaraviṣayām ; anyastu sāṃkhyādiniṣedham ; sāṃkhyo'pi viṣayāvabhāsanarūpaṃ jñānaṃ buddhidharmamicchan ātmānaṃ vastuto jaḍameva upaiti ; na ca jaḍātmā svātmanyapi durlabhaprakāśasvātantryaleśaḥ kiṃcit sādhayituṃ niṣeddhuṃ vā prabhaviṣṇuḥ pāṣāṇa iva ; na ca ajaḍātmano'pi etad ucitam , tathā hi ---- sa svātmani siddhimitthaṃ kuryāt ---- yadi asya so'bhinavatvena bhāsamānaḥ pūrvaṃ na bhāsate , na bhāsanaṃ cet jaḍataiva / niṣedhaṃ ca itthaṃ vidadhyāt ---- yadi sa na prakāśate tathā ca jaḍaḥ , na ca jaḍasya etat yuktam ityuktam , nāpi ajaḍasya ; tasmāt saṃvitprakāśa eva ghaṭādiprakāśaḥ , na tvasau svatantraḥ kaścit vāstavaḥ ; prakāśa eva ca ātmāḥ ; tat na tatra kārakavyāpāravat pramāṇavyāpāro'pi nityatvavat svaprakāśatvasyāpi tatra bhāvāt //2//
children.translated_text: thus, let the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> and others, for whom the self is insentient, establish their proof regarding the Lord; and let others [respond to] the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> refutation; the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> too, holding that knowledge — the illumination of objects — is a property of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), in reality arrives at a self that is merely insentient. And an insentient self, like a stone, being devoid of even the slightest trace of the freedom of self-luminosity which is rare even in one's own self, is incapable of establishing or negating anything. Nor is this appropriate even for a non-insentient self; for consider — he would accomplish proof in his own self thus: if that [self] appears to him as something new that did not appear before — but if it does not appear, that is just insentience. And he would accomplish negation thus: if that does not appear — and then it is insentient, and it has been said that this is not proper for an insentient [entity], nor for a non-insentient one. Therefore, the illumination of a pot and such is nothing but the illumination of consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>), and that [pot-illumination] is not some independent, real thing. And light (<s>prakāśa</s>) itself is the Self; therefore, just as the operation of instruments of action (<s>kāraka</s>) [is not applicable] there, so too the operation of means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) [is not applicable], since self-luminosity, like eternality, obtains there. //2//

Here, who could produce, regarding <s>Īśvara</s>, establishment in the form of knowledge — 'He exists' — by what kind of means of knowledge? Or negation in the form of knowledge — 'He does not exist'? If [you say] the knower — then who is that very [knower]? Is it the body and such, which are inert? Or is it someone other than those, designated by the word <s>ātman</s> (self) and the like? Is that [knower] too self-luminous by nature or not? If [it is] the body and such, which are inert — that which is not established in its own self, what establishment could it produce regarding another? Even the <s>ātman</s>, if not self-luminous, is inert and in the same predicament. If [you say it is] self-luminous by nature — then by what kind of inherent form does it shine? If by the form of mere settled consciousness, then there would be differentiation of consciousnesses, and through the internal reconnection of what has been differentiated, there would be no non-differentiation; therefore, it shines by its nature of independent self-luminosity, and shining thus, what kind of <s>Īśvara</s> would it establish or negate? If [you say] one whose nature is agent and knower — but the knower itself is of that nature, so who else is that [Īśvara]? But [you object] omniscient agency and omniscient knowledge do not belong to the knower; [we reply] the meaning of the word 'all' does not split the essential nature of the knower and agent — even in the perception of difference, since <s>Īśvara's</s> knowledge, desire, sacrifice, and other [attributes], being eternal, are not caused by their objects and cannot be enhanced by them. If [you say] objecthood is merely the bringing into luminosity — [we reply] that such a status is inappropriate for what is non-luminous by nature — thus we shall state. If [the object] is luminous by nature, then the object too, in its entirety, is submerged in luminosity alone, and so luminosity illuminates [luminosity] — if this alone is the ultimate truth, what distinction is there between the omniscient and the non-omniscient? The means of knowledge too can be similarly challenged on the grounds of being established or not established; likewise establishment itself. Therefore, the self, taking as a body the object in question, shining forth, is itself luminous — devoid of interruption; even regarding one in deep sleep, it is indeed luminous, otherwise memory would be impossible; and since luminosity is eternal, due to the absence of a cause for interruption, and since it is luminous relative to another knower, and since the distinction between one's own and another's knower, being created by that [consciousness itself], will be stated to be of the nature of <s>Māyā</s> (illusion). And this [consciousness] is independent (<s>svatantra</s>). And its independence — differentiation within non-differentiation, and non-differentiation through internal reconnection within what has been differentiated — we shall explain in many ways. This very thing is its supreme sovereignty (<s>pārameśvarya</s>), whose primary form is suffused with bliss (<s>ānandamaya</s>) — thus it has been taken up earlier:

children.text: nanu kārakavyāpāraḥ pramāṇavyāpāraśca yadi īśvare na saṃbhavati , tarhi pratyabhijñāpayāmi ---- iti yo vyāpāra uktaḥ sa katamo vyāpāraḥ
children.translated_text: Objection: If the operation of instruments of action and the operation of means of valid knowledge are not possible in the Lord, then what kind of operation is that which was stated as 'I shall demonstrate the recognition' —
anticipating this [objection], he says:
But in this [Lord] who, though seen, is unrecognized due to the power of delusion,
this <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition) is demonstrated through the revelation of [His] power. //

children.text:
sa īśvarasvabhāva ātmā prakāśate tāvat , tatra ca asya svātantryam iti na kenacidvapuṣā na prakāśate , tatra aprakāśātmanāpi prakāśate prakāśātmanāpi ,
tatrāpi prakāśātmani sarvathā prakāśātmanā prakāśo bhāgaśo vā ; bhāgaśaḥ prakāśane sarvasya vyatirekeṇa avyatirekeṇa vā , katipayasya vyatirekeṇa avyatirekeṇa vā , uktaprakārapūrṇatayā vā ; tadamī sapta prakārāḥ / tatra prathamaḥ prakāro jaḍollāsaḥ , antyaḥ paramaśivātmā , madhyamā jīvā bhāsāḥ , saiva bhagavato māyā vimohinī nāma śaktiḥ , tadvaśāt prakāśātmatayā satatam avabhāsamāne'pi ātmani bhāgena aprakāśanavaśād

children.translated_text: unrecognized (<s>anupalakṣite</s>) —

children.text: sarvathā hṛdayaṃgamībhāvamaprāpte ata eva pūrṇatāvabhāsanasādhyām arthakriyām akurvati , tatpūrṇatāvabhāsanātmakābhimānaviśeṣasiddhaye
children.translated_text: not having in every way reached the state of being fully grasped by the heart, and therefore not performing the purposeful activity achievable through the manifestation of completeness — for the accomplishment of the specific self-identification (<s>abhimāna</s>) that is the manifestation of that completeness,

That Self whose nature is the Lord shines forth; and since His freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>) obtains there, there is no form in which He does not shine. There, He shines even in a non-luminous form and also in a luminous form;
even in the luminous form, the manifestation is either complete in every way or partial; in partial manifestation, either with the exclusion of everything or without exclusion, or with the exclusion of some things or without exclusion, or with the completeness of the aforementioned mode — thus there are seven modes. Among these, the first mode is the flash of the insentient; the last is the essence of <s>Paramaśiva</s> (Supreme Śiva); the middle ones are the manifestations of individual souls (<s>jīvas</s>). That itself is the deluding power of the Blessed One called <s>Māyā</s>; by its force, even though the Self constantly shines as luminous in nature, due to the partial non-manifestation —
<s>Pratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition),
which has been previously explained, is demonstrated. How?
Of the power (<s>śakti</s>) —
which is well-known as belonging to the Lord, consisting of seeing (<s>dṛk</s>) and action (<s>kriyā</s>),
through the revelation (<s>āviṣkaraṇa</s>) —

children.text: pradarśanena , abhimānasādhyārthakriyāṇāṃ tadabhimānasiddhyā vinā asiddheḥ ; tathā ca dṛṣṭāntaṃ darśayati
children.translated_text: through the demonstration, since the purposeful activities that depend on self-identification cannot be accomplished without the accomplishment of that self-identification. And thus he shows an illustration:
{...even by those very ones who have been entreated...}(<s>Īpv</s> 4,1.17.)

children.text: iti / etaduktaṃ bhavati ---- na kārakavyāpāro bhagavati , nāpi jñāpakavyāpāro'yam , api tu mohāpasāraṇamātrametat , vyavahārasādhanānāṃ pramāṇānāṃ tāvatyeva viśrānteḥ / ghaṭo'yamagragaḥ pratyakṣatvāt ---- ityanena hi ghaṭo na jñāpyate pratyakṣeṇaiva prakāśamānatvāt , anyathā pakṣe hetvasiddheḥ , kevalaṃ mohamātramapasāryate / yaścāyaṃ mohastadapasāraṇaṃ ca yat , tadubhayamapi bhagavata eva vijṛmbhāmātram , na tu adhikaṃ kiṃcit ---- ityuktaṃ vakṣyate ca //3//
children.translated_text: Thus. What is meant is this: there is no operation of an instrument of action in the Blessed One, nor is this an operation of a means of making known; rather, this is merely the removal of delusion, since the means of valid knowledge that serve practical activity rest in just that much. 'This pot is in front, because it is perceptible' — by this, the pot is not made known, since it already shines through direct perception itself; otherwise, the reason (<s>hetu</s>) would be unestablished in the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>). Only mere delusion is removed. And whatever this delusion is, and whatever its removal — both of these are merely a playful display (<s>vijṛmbhā</s>) of the Blessed One, and nothing more — this has been said and will be said. //3//

children.text: nanu paridṛśyamāne bhāvarāśau kimīyā śaktirāviṣkriyate kaṃ ca prati iti / jaḍānāṃ tāvat na jñānātmikā śaktirasti , kriyātmikāpi svātantryaprāṃā svātantryavyapagamād asaṃbhāvanābhūmireva ; tathā ca ratho gacchati ---- ityādau upacāraṃ kecana pratipannāḥ , na ca jaḍānprati vyavahārasādhanam ucitam ; atha ajaḍajīvajjanatādhikāreṇa ubhayamapi , tarhi sarvasya svātmā maheśvara ---- iti dūrataraṃ viprakarṣitā pratyāśā , tadetad āśṅkya nirūpayati
children.translated_text: Objection: In the visible mass of entities, whose power is being revealed and to whom? For insentient things certainly do not possess the power of knowledge, and even the power of action, having the nature of freedom, is impossible in them due to the absence of freedom — and thus some have understood the statement 'the chariot goes' and such as metaphorical. Nor is a means of establishing practical activity appropriate with reference to insentient things. If, then, both [powers are being revealed] with reference to the non-insentient individual souls — then the hope that 'everyone's own Self is <s>Maheśvara</s>' is pushed even farther away. Anticipating this [objection], he examines:
For the foundation of insentient beings depends on the living;

children.text: jñānaṃ kriyā ca bhūtānāṃ jīvatāṃ jīvanaṃ matam //
children.translated_text: knowledge and action are considered the life of living beings. //
'For' (<s>tathā hi</s>) —

children.text: iti yuktyupakramaṃ dyotayati , dṛśyatāṃ kila ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: thus indicates the commencement of reasoning; the meaning is 'let it be seen.'
'Thus' (<s>tathā</s>) —

children.text: ityanena sādhyaṃ sūcyate , hinā heturityanye , prakṛtaṃ sādhyaṃ hetusiddhyāyattamupakramyate ityarthaḥ / tena iti buddhivartinā , tata eva smaryamāṇena granthena varṇayiṣyamāṇena prakāreṇa yasmāt sarvametad yuktam iti
children.translated_text: by this, the thesis to be proved is indicated. Others [say it indicates] the reason. The meaning is: the thesis to be proved, which depends on the establishment of the reason, is being introduced. By 'tena' [meaning] 'by that [reasoning]' present in the intellect, by the manner being described in the text being recalled from that — since all this is reasonable —
'For' (<s>tathā hi</s>) —

children.text: iti śabdasya vārthaḥ / iha tāvat bhāvarāśiryathā vimṛśyate tathā asti , astitvasya prakāśaṃ śaraṇīkurvataḥ prakāśaprāṇitadeśīyaṃ āśritya samunmevāt , avimṛṣṭaṃ hi yadi vastu tanna nīlaṃ na pītaṃ na sat na asaditi kuta iti paryanuyoge kimuttaraṃ syāt / tena yad yathā yāvat avādhitaṃ vimṛśyate tat tathā tāvat asti , tat eva deśakālākāravitatātmāno 'pi dravyakriyāsaṃbandhādayaḥ ekatvena paramārthasanta iti vakṣyate
children.translated_text: such is the meaning of the word. Here, to begin with, the mass of entities exists as it is reflected upon (<s>vimṛśyate</s>), since existence takes refuge in manifestation, arising by relying on [manifestation] which has the nature of being animated by light. For if a thing is unreflected upon, it is neither blue nor yellow, neither existent nor non-existent — when pressed with 'whence?', what answer could there be? Therefore, whatever is reflected upon as whatever, to whatever extent, without contradiction — that exists as such and to that extent. That itself — substances, actions, relations, and so forth, whose nature extends through space, time, and form — are ultimately real as a unity; this will be stated in
{Action, relation, universal...}(<s>Īpv</s> 2,2.1)

children.text: ityādinā , tataśca vitatamapi idaṃ viśvaṃ saṃkṣepavimarśadaśādhirohe jaḍaṃ jīvacca ---- ityetāvatā dvayarūpeṇa asti / tatra jaḍā vimṛśyamānā na svatantrā bhavanti , vimṛśyamānatā hi teṣāṃ na svaśarīraviśrāntaḥ ko 'pi dharmaḥ jaḍatvābhāvaprasaṃgāt , mama nīlaṃ bhāti mayā nīlaṃ jñāyate iti / teṣām

children.translated_text: insentient beings (<s>jaḍabhūtānām</s>) —
though of the nature of consciousness (<s>cinmaya</s>), having been rendered insentient by the power of the Lord called <s>Māyā</s>,
depending on the living (<s>jīvantam</s>) —
on the knowing subject (<s>pramātṛ</s>),
is the foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) —

children.text: tatpramātrābhimukhyena avasthānam , tato jaḍā nāma na pṛthak santi / yathoktaṃ granthakṛtaivaḥ
children.translated_text: their subsistence through orientation toward that knowing subject; therefore, the insentient do not exist separately. As stated by the author of the treatise himself:

and so forth. And thus, even this extended universe, when ascending to the level of condensed reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), exists in the twofold form of insentient and sentient — just this much. Among these, the insentient, when being reflected upon, are not independent; for their being-reflected-upon is not some property resting in their own body — since otherwise the absence of insentience would follow — [as in] 'blue appears to me,' 'blue is known by me.' Of these —
{Thus, these insentient things, which are unreal in themselves, exist only as [manifestations] of light;
the insentient are nothing but light alone, [illuminated] by [light's] own and other [manifestations] of itself. //}

children.text: iti / sa eva hi svātmanā san vaktavyo yasya anyānupahitaṃ rūpaṃ cakāsti ; na ca bhārūpānupahitaṃ jaḍaṃ nāma kiñcit , tena jaḍānāṃ hi śaktirāviṣkriyate jaḍānprati ---- ityetat tāvat nirutthānameva / ye tu anye jaḍebhyo jīvanta ---- iti nāma prasiddhāḥ teṣāmapi śarīraprāṇapuryaṣṭakaśūnyākārāḥ tāvat jaḍā eva iti teṣāmapi kimucyate / ata eva ghaṭaśarīraprāṇasukhatadbh|avarūpaṃ yallagnaṃ bhāti tadeva jīvarūpabhūtaṃ satyam ; tasya ca āpāte yadyapi bahutvaṃ bhāti tathāpi tat jaḍātmakavedyaśarīrādyupādheḥ / tatastat apārabhārthikam anyonyāśrayāt , jīvā hi jaḍabhedāt bhedabhāginaḥ jaḍāśca jīvabhedāt , etaddeho 'yam etadvedyo 'yam ---- iti bhedam upeyuḥ , nīlapītādibhāvabhedāstu pramātṛsaṃlagnatayā bhedabhūmimeva paramadhirūḍhā iti / kim tena / tadayaṃ jīvānāmabheda eva saṃpanna iti jīvan pramātā ---- iti jātam / jīvanaṃ ca jīvanakartṛtvaṃ tacca jñānakriyātmakam , yo hi jānāti ca karoti ca sa jīvati ---- ityucyate / tadayaṃ pramātā jñānakriyāśaktiyogād īśvara ---- iti vyavahartavayaḥ purāṇāgamādiprasiddheśvaravat ; tadprasiddhāvapi sarvaviṣayajñānakriyāśaktimattvasvabhāvameva aiśvaryaṃ tanmātrānubandhitvādeva siddham ; tadapi ca kalpiteśvare rājādau tathā vyāptigrahaṇāt , yo yāvati jñātā kartā ca sa tāvati īśvarp rājeva , anīśvarasya jñātṛtvakartṛtve svabhāvaviruddhe yataḥ ; ātmā ca viśvatra jñātā kartā ca ---- iti siddhā pratyabhijñā / jñānakriyāśakto eva svābhāvikyau aprarūḍhabhedonmeṣe sadāśiveśvarau , bhedasya sāmānyataḥ prarohe vidyākale , viśoṣataḥ prarohe buddhikarmendriyagaṇa iva bhaviṣyati / jaḍā iti ajīvantaḥ , anye ca jīvanta ---- ityāpāte tāvad bhāti na tu saṃvidāpāte bhātīti jīvatāmiti jaṅgamā eva amī itthaṃ nirdiṣṭāḥ //4//
children.translated_text: Thus. For only that is to be called existent by its own nature whose form shines without being pervaded by anything else; and there is nothing called 'insentient' that is not pervaded by the form of light. Therefore, the claim that 'the power is being revealed with respect to the insentient, for the insentient' — this much is entirely without foundation. And as for those others who are called 'living' as distinct from the insentient — their forms as body, vital breath, <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body), and void are themselves insentient, so what can be said of them? For this very reason, that which appears as attached [to consciousness] in the form of pot, body, vital breath, pleasure, and their modifications — that alone, having become the nature of the individual soul, is real. And although at first glance its multiplicity appears, that is due to the adventitious condition (<s>upādhi</s>) of the knowable body and such, which is of insentient nature. Therefore that [multiplicity] is not ultimately real, due to mutual dependence; for the individual souls partake of differentiation from the differentiation of the insentient, and the insentient [partake of differentiation] from the differentiation of souls — 'this is its body,' 'this is its object' — thus they assume differentiation. But the differentiations of entities such as blue, yellow, and the like, being attached to the knowing subject, have ascended to the very ground of differentiation. What of it? Therefore, the non-difference of individual souls is fully established — thus the knowing subject (<s>pramātṛ</s>) who is 'living' has emerged. And 'living' means being the agent of living, and that consists of knowledge and action; for one who knows and acts is said to 'live.' Therefore this knowing subject, through possessing the powers of knowledge and action, is to be treated as the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), just like the Lord well-known from the <s>Purāṇas</s> and <s>Āgamas</s>. And even in that established [Lord], sovereignty is of the very nature of possessing the power of knowledge and action regarding all objects, since it is connected with just that much. And even in a figurative lord such as a king, since the invariable concomitance is grasped thus — whoever is a knower and agent to whatever extent, to that extent he is a lord, like a king — for knowledge and agency in a non-lord would be contrary to their essential nature. And the Self is everywhere a knower and agent — thus the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition) is established. The powers of knowledge and action are indeed innate; in <s>Sadāśiva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> [tattvas] where the sprouting of differentiation has not begun; at the general sprouting of differentiation in the <s>Vidyā</s> level; at the specific sprouting, they become like the groups of cognitive and active sense faculties. 'Insentient' means non-living, and 'others are living' — this appears at first glance, but does not appear in the light of consciousness — thus by 'living beings,' only the mobile ones are designated here. //4//

children.text: nanu jñānakriye eva kathaṃ siddhe yata aiśvaryavyavahāraḥ prasādhyate ---- iti śaṅkāṃ śamayitumāha
children.translated_text: Objection: How are knowledge and action alone established, from which the attribution of lordship is to be accomplished? To dispel this doubt, he says:

children.text: tatra jñānaṃ svataḥ siddhaṃ kriyā kāyāśritā satī /
children.translated_text: Therein, knowledge is self-established; action, being dependent on the body,
can be observed even by others; from that, another's knowledge is inferred. //

children.text: ahaṃ jānāmi , mayā jñātaṃ jñāsyate ca ---- ityevaṃ svaprakāśāhaṃparāmarśapariniṣṭhitameva idaṃ jñānaṃ nāma , kiṃ tatra anyat vicāryate , tadaprakāśe hi viśvam andhatamasaṃ syāt , tadapi vā na syāt , bālo 'pi hi prakāśaviśrāntimeva saṃvedayate / taduktam
children.translated_text: 'I know,' 'it was known by me,' 'it will be known' — thus this thing called knowledge is established precisely in the self-luminous reflective awareness of 'I' (<s>ahaṃ-parāmarśa</s>). What else is to be investigated there? For in its absence, the universe would be utter darkness, or even that [darkness] would not exist. Even a child experiences [reality as] resting in light alone. As stated:
{The knower — by what should one know that? /}(<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.5.19)

children.text: iti / tannihnave hi kaḥ praśnaḥ , kim uttaraṃ ca syāt ---- iti / tatra ca jānāmi ---- ityantaḥsaṃrambhayogo 'pi bhāti , yena śuklāderguṇāt atyantajaḍāt jānāmi ---- iti ---- vapuḥ citsvabhāvatām abhyetiḥ ; sa ca saṃrambho vimarśaḥ kriyāśaktirbhavati / yaduktam asmatparameṣṭhiśrosromānandapādaiḥ ----
children.translated_text: Thus. For if that [knower] is denied, who would ask the question, and what answer could there be? And in that [knowledge], the association with inner intensity in 'I know' also appears, by which the body — [which would otherwise be] utterly insentient like the quality of whiteness — through 'I know,' approaches the nature of consciousness. And that intensity is reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), which becomes the power of action (<s>kriyā-śakti</s>). As stated by our supreme teacher <s>Ānandapāda</s> (i.e., <s>Ānandanātha</s>) —
{Even at the time of apprehending a pot and such, the [awareness] 'knows the pot' — that is action. /}

children.text: iti / tena āntarī kriyāśaktiḥ jñānavadeva svataḥ siddhā svaprakāśā , saiva tu svaśaktyā / prāṇapuryaṣṭakakrameṇa śarīramapi saṃcaramāṇā spandanarūpā satī vyāpārātmikā māthāpade 'pi pramāṇasya pratyakṣāderviṣayaḥ / sā ca paraśarīrādisāhityena avagatā svaṃ svabhāvaṃ jñātmakamavagamayati , na ca jñānam idantathā bhāti , idantā hi ajñānatvam , na ca anyadvastu anyena vapuṣā bhātaṃ bhātaṃ bhavet , tat jñānaṃ bhātyeva param , bhāti ca yat tadeva ahamityasya vapuḥ iti parajñānamapi svātmaivaḥ ; paratvaṃ kevalam upādherdehādeḥ , sa cāpi vicārito yāvat na anya iti viśvaḥ pramātṛvargaḥ paramārthata ekaḥ pramātā sa eva ca asti / taduktam
children.translated_text: Thus. Therefore, the internal <s>kriyā-śakti</s> (power of action), like knowledge, is self-established and self-luminous by its own nature; and that very [power], by its own <s>śakti</s> (energy), moving through the body by the sequence of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body), being of the nature of vibration, becomes the object of even <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) such as direct perception in its operational aspect. And that [power], apprehended together with another's body and such, reveals its own nature as being of the nature of knowledge; and knowledge does not appear as 'this-ness,' for 'this-ness' is ignorance; nor can something that has appeared with a different form be said to have appeared [as it truly is]; therefore knowledge indeed shines as supreme, and whatever shines — that alone is the form of 'I' — thus even another's knowledge is one's own Self alone. Otherness belongs merely to the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) of body and the like; and even that, when examined, is not truly other — thus the entire class of knowers is ultimately one single knower, and that alone exists. As stated:
{... light alone exists, through one's own and others' selves. /}

children.text: iti / tataśca bhagavān sadāśivo jānāti ityataḥ prabhṛti krimirapi jānāti ---- ityantam eka eva pramātā iti phalataḥ sarvajñatvaṃ pramātuḥ / evaṃ kartṛtve 'pi vācyam / yaduktam asmatparameṣṭhibhiḥ śivadṛṣṭau
children.translated_text: Thus. And therefore, from 'the Blessed <s>Sadāśiva</s> knows' up to 'even a worm knows' — there is but one single knower; thus omniscience is the result for the knower. The same must be said regarding agency. As stated by our supreme teacher in the <s>Śivadṛṣṭi</s>:
{The pot knows through my self; and I know through the pot's self;

children.text: sadāśivātmanā vedmi sa vā vetti madātmanā //
children.translated_text: I know through <s>Sadāśiva</s>'s self; and He knows through my self.
<s>Śiva</s> Himself abides knowing His own Self through manifold forms. /}
'Ūhyate' (it is inferred):

children.text: ityanena jñānena jñānasya prameyatvaṃ na nirvahati ---- iti darśayati , anyathā hi anumīyate ---- iti brūyāt /
children.translated_text: By the word 'ūhyate' (it is inferred), he shows that knowledge does not serve as the object of [another] knowledge; for otherwise he would have said 'anumīyate' (it is inferred by formal inference).
And so forth.

children.text: tadevaṃ yeṣāṃ tārkikapravādapāṃsupātadhūsarībhāvo na vṛtto 'smin saṃvedanapathe , te iyataiva ātmānamīśvaraṃ vidvāṃso ghaṭaśarīraprāṇasukhatadabhāvān tatraiva nimajjayanta īśvarasamāviṣṭā eva bhavanti / tato 'yam upoddhātaḥ / upa iti ātmanaḥ samīpe ṭaṅkavat īśvarapratyabhijñānalakṣaṇa utkarṣo hanyate viśrāmyate yena ; etāvadeva ca asya granthasya tātparyam ---- iti / tato 'pi ayam upoddhātaḥ / upāṃśu avitataṃ kṛtvā uditi śāstrasya ūrdhva eva hanyate apasāryate prameyaviṣayo vyāmoho yena ---- iti / gatyarthatvādvā hanterjñānamarthaḥ , jñāyate prameyaṃ yena iti / kecittu gatiṃ striyaṃ gacchati ---- ityetadviṣayameva hantyarthamāhuḥ / evaṃ ślokacatuṣṭayārthabhāvanādārḍhy|adeva labhyate paramaśivaḥ / iti śivam //5//
children.translated_text: Thus, those whose path of experience has not been made grey by the dust-storm of logicians' doctrines — they, knowing the Self as the Lord by just this much, immersing the pot, body, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), pleasure, and their absence into that very [Lord], become absorbed in the Lord. Therefore this is the <s>upoddhāta</s> (introduction). 'Upa' means near one's own self; just as a chisel [carves], the excellence characterized as the recognition of the Lord is struck, i.e., brought to rest — and this alone is the purport of this treatise. Or alternatively, this is the <s>upoddhāta</s>: having made it 'upāṃśu' (whispered, i.e., concise), by 'ut,' upward beyond the treatise, the delusion concerning the objects of knowledge is struck, i.e., removed. Or, from the root 'han' in the sense of motion, knowledge is the meaning — that by which the objects of knowledge are known. Some, however, say that 'han' in the sense of motion refers to the meaning of going to a woman, pertaining to that very subject. Thus, through the firmness of contemplation on the meaning of these four verses alone, the Supreme <s>Śiva</s> is attained. Thus, may there be auspiciousness! //5//

children.text:
iti śrīmadācāryotpaladevaśiṣya ---- śrīmadācāryalakṣmaṇaguptadattopadeśa ---- śrīmadācāryābhinavaguptaviracitāyāṃ śrīpratyabhijñāvimarśinyāṃ jñānādhikāre upoddhātaḥ /
iti prathamāhnikam // 1 //
children.translated_text:
Thus ends the introduction to the knowledge chapter in the glorious <s>Pratyabhijñāvimarśinī</s> composed by the venerable master <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, who received instruction from the venerable master <s>Lakṣmaṇagupta</s>, who was a disciple of the venerable master <s>Utpaladeva</s>.
Thus ends the first daily lesson. // 1 //
Now the second daily lesson.
{By whom, having manifested the universe as difference in the form of the prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>),
it is led to the subsequent position (<s>uttarapakṣa</s>) of non-difference — to that <s>Śiva</s> we offer praise. //}

children.text: iha yat paramārtharūpaṃ āśaṅkyamānapratipakṣapratikṣepeṇa nirūpayiṣyamāṇaṃ suṣṭhutamāṃ spaṣṭokṛtaṃ bhavati / yadāha bhaṭṭanārāyaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Here, the ultimate reality, being established through the refutation of the apprehended opposing position, becomes most clearly elucidated. As stated by <s>Bhaṭṭa Nārāyaṇa</s>:
{Obeisance to You, O Lord, who, by first raising the error and confusion of worldly existence,

children.text: jñānānandaṃ ca nirdvandvaṃ deva vṛtvā vivṛṇvate //}
children.translated_text: shatters it, and having encompassed the non-dual bliss of knowledge, reveals [it]. //}

children.text: tatreha anātmānīśvaravādināṃ bhrāntibhedanapūrvakaṃ paramārthaṃ vivarīṣyan tadudbhāvanaṃ tāvat ekādaśabhiḥ ślokaiḥ karoti
children.translated_text: Here, wishing to unfold the ultimate truth by first shattering the errors of those who deny the Self and the Lord, he first presents that [error] in eleven verses:
{'Now, knowledge that manifests the particular... /}
beginning with these,
{... therefore, even the agent is imagined. //}

children.text: ityantaiḥ / tatra ślokadvayena ātmano dhruvasya dṛśyānupalabdhyā abhāva uktaḥ pratyakṣātmavādinaḥ prati / tatra ślokatrayeṇa smṛtyanusaṃdhānaṃ saṃskārāt siddham iti anyabāsiddhatvāt ātmānumānāya na paryāptam ---- iti proktam anumeyātmavādinaḥ prati / tatra ślokena jñānādi guṇairguṇini pratipattiḥ ---- iti anumānaṃ nirastam / evam ātmānaṃ nirākṛtya , tato jñānakriyāśaktisaṃbandharūpamaiśvarya nirākartuṃ jñānasya svarūpameva vyatiriktaṃ vādyantaramate , sāṃkhyamate ca ayujyamānam ---- iti nirūpitaṃ ślokadvayena / tata ekena kriyā nāma na kācit kvacidapi asti ---- iti kathitam / tatra sādhakaṃ pratikṣipya bādhakaṃ ca upanyasyati / tataḥ saṃbandhasya ślokena nāstitvaṃ pratipāditaṃ pramāṇābhāvaṃ vadatā / ślokenaiva tatra bādhakaṃ pramāṇamuktvā , na ātmā sthiro nāpi jñātṛtvakartṛtvalakṣaṇam asya aiśvaryam ---- iti svapakṣa upasaṃhṛtaḥ ---- iti pūrvapakṣasya piṇḍārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: ending with these. Therein, by two verses, the non-existence of a permanent Self is stated through the non-apprehension of the visible, directed against those who hold the Self to be directly perceived. Then, by three verses, it is stated that memory and recognition are established through impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and therefore, being established through other means, they do not suffice for inferring the Self — this is directed against those who hold the Self to be inferable. Then, by one verse, the inference that qualities such as knowledge indicate a substance possessing qualities is refuted. Thus, having denied the Self, in order to deny sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) whose nature is the relation to the powers of knowledge and action, the very nature of knowledge as something distinct is shown to be untenable in other philosophical systems and in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> system — this is established in two verses. Then, by one [verse], it is stated that action as such does not exist anywhere at all. Therein, the proof is refuted and the counter-proof is presented. Then, by one verse, the non-existence of relation is established by one who asserts the absence of a valid means of knowledge. By that very verse, having stated the counter-proof as valid means of knowledge — the Self is not permanent, nor is its sovereignty characterized by knowership and agency — thus the opponent's position is summarized. This is the gist of the prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>).
Now the meaning of the text is explained.
Now, knowledge that manifests the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is one; the other, further,

children.text: sābhilāpaṃ vikalpākhyaṃ bahudhā nāpi tad dvayam //
children.translated_text: is called <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition), accompanied by verbal expression, and is manifold; yet neither is that a duality.
Since no permanent seer whatsoever appears therein,
even this 'I'-awareness is one that determines [only] the body and such.
'Nanu' (Objection):

children.text: iti ākṣepe ; iha ātmā saṃvitsvabhāvaḥ sthiraḥ iti tāvadayuktam , sthirasyāpi svaprakāśasya aprakāśanāt / tathā hi ---- ghaṭaprakāśo ghaṭavikalpo ghaṭapratyabhijñā ghaṭasmṛtiḥ ghaṭotprekṣā ---- ityādirūpeṇa jñānānyeva prakāśante bhinnakāntāni bhinnaviṣayāṇi bhinnakārāṇi ca / tatra nīlasya prakāśaḥ
children.translated_text: This is an objection. Here, [the opponent says:] it is first of all untenable that the Self, whose nature is consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>), is permanent, since even a permanent self-luminous entity does not manifest [as such]. For thus — cognitions alone shine forth in forms such as the perception of a pot, the concept of a pot, the recognition of a pot, the memory of a pot, the imaginative projection of a pot — being of different moments, different objects, and different forms. Therein, the perception of blue is:
'Knowledge that manifests the particular' (<s>svalakṣaṇābhāsaṃ jñānam</s>) —
'sva' (its own):
that which does not follow another and partakes of contraction of its own nature;
'lakṣaṇa' (characteristic):
that whose form is of [specific] place, time, and appearance;
'ābhāsa' (manifestation):

children.text: prakāśanam antarmukhaṃ yasmin bahirmukhīnasvarūpadhāriṇi jñāne tat avikalpakam viṣayabhede 'pi ekajātīyam , svarūpavaicitrye 'pi kāraṇābhāvāt / vikalpe hi vaicitryakāraṇam abhilāpaḥ , sa ca ata nāsti ; na hi abhilāpo nīlasya dharmaḥ , na ca cakṣurgrāhyaḥ , tato 'sau prācyaḥ smartavyaḥ , aprabuddhe ca saṃskāre na smṛtiḥ , tatprabodhaśca vastudarśanotthitaḥ iti vastudarśanasamaye 'bhilāpasmṛtirnāsti /
children.translated_text: that in which there is inward-facing illumination — such cognition, which bears an outward-facing form, is non-conceptual (<s>avikalpaka</s>), of one kind even amid diversity of objects, since there is no cause for diversity in its own nature. For in conceptual cognition, the cause of diversity is verbal expression (<s>abhilāpa</s>), and that is absent here; for verbal expression is not a property of blue, nor is it graspable by the eye; therefore it must be recalled from prior [experience], and when the impression has not been awakened, there is no memory; and the awakening of that impression arises from the perception of the object — hence at the time of perceiving the object, there is no memory of verbal expression.
'Para' (the other):

children.text: vikalpakaṃ jñānam , sarvasya vikalpasya sākṣāt pāramparyeṇa vā nirvikalpakamūlatvāt /
children.translated_text: Conceptual (<s>vikalpa</s>) cognition — since all conceptual cognition, directly or indirectly, has non-conceptual cognition as its root.
'Param' (other):

children.text: iti ca anyarūpaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ tasya viṣayaḥ , svalakṣaṇe 'tisaṃkocini vitatavikalpasādhyasya vrḍdhavyāvahārikasya , aupadeśikasya vā saṃketasya kartum aśakyatvāt , kṛtasyāpi vaiyarthyāt , tena hi ananuyāyinā na punarvyavahāraḥ / tacca bahubhedam , yatastat abhilāpena saṃjalpātmanā śabdarūpeṇa saha vartate / śabdanaṃ ca idam ---- iti , tat ---- iti , tadidam ---- iti , bhavedidam ---- iti , idaṃ vā idam ---- ityādi bahudhā bhidyate / tacca na viṣayapakṣo vartate , api tu tasya vikalpasya svarūpameva vicitrokurvat pratibhāti iti vikalpo bahubhedaḥ / evam anubhavavikalpaparamparā tāvat svaprakāśatvena bhāti /
children.translated_text: means of a different nature; its object is the universal characteristic (<s>sāmānya-lakṣaṇa</s>), since in the extremely contracted particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), it is impossible to establish a convention — whether the extended practical convention of the experienced or the instructional convention — and even if established, it would be futile, for one does not transact again with that which does not recur. And that [conceptual cognition] is of many varieties, because it operates together with verbal expression (<s>abhilāpa</s>) in the form of speech. And this verbalization is divided in many ways — as 'this,' 'that,' 'that is this,' 'this might be,' 'this or this,' and so forth. And that [diversity] does not belong to the object side, but rather is the very nature of that conceptual cognition appearing in diverse formations — thus <s>vikalpa</s> is of many kinds. In this way, the succession of experience and conceptual cognition shines forth as self-luminous.
Then:

children.text: syādetat , yallagnāsau paramparā so'pi ābhāti ---- iti ; tatra , yato dvayamapi etad avikalpetararūpaṃ na anyasya

children.translated_text: 'kasyacit' (some):

children.text: etadatiriktasya draṣṭuḥ anubhavituḥ saṃbandhi , dṛśyasya tu bhavatu bāhyārthavāde / atra hetuḥ ---- yataḥ
children.translated_text: seer or experiencer that is distinct from these; though it may belong to the seen, as in the externalist doctrine. Here the reason is — since
'tasya' (of that):

children.text: draṣṭuḥ , ata eva saṃvitsvabhāvatopagamāt svaprakāśatāyogyatvāt āpannopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpteḥ ,
children.translated_text: of the seer — precisely because consciousness is accepted as his nature, because he is fit for self-luminosity, because he has already attained the character of being apprehended —
'atra' (here):

children.text: etadbodhadvayamadhye nāsti avabhāsaḥ / nanu astyeva avabhāsaḥ ---- iti asiddhā dṛśyānupalabdhiḥ / tathā hi ---- ahaṃ vedmi , niścinomi , smarāmi idam ---- iti vidādiprakṛtyartharūpāt jñānasmṛtyādeḥ idam ---- iti ca karmarūpāt viṣayāt atiriktameva aham ---- iti anuyāyini prakāśe anuyāyirūpaṃ bhāti / ka evamāha bhāti ---- iti ? bhānaṃ hi avikalpakam , aham ---- iti śabdānuviddho vikalpapratyayaḥ / nanu tathāpi kim anena vikalpyate , śarīrasantāno vā kṛśo'ham ---- ityādipratyayāt , jñānasantāno vā sukhyaham ---- iti pratīteḥ ? matvarthīyaśca santānameva spṛśati nātiriktam / tadetaduktam ----
children.translated_text: between these two kinds of cognition, there is no manifestation [of a separate self]. [Objection:] But there is indeed a manifestation — thus the non-apprehension of the visible is unestablished. For thus — 'I know,' 'I ascertain,' 'I remember this' — in a light that accompanies [all cognitions], distinct from the knowledge, memory, and such that have the form of the meaning of verbal roots like 'vid' (to know), and distinct from the object in the form of 'this' in the accusative — an accompanying form shines in the accompanying light of 'I.' Who says it shines? For shining is non-conceptual, while the 'I'-awareness is a conceptual cognition accompanied by the word. But even so, what is conceptualized by this — is it the bodily continuum, from cognitions like 'I am thin,' or the knowledge-continuum, from the awareness 'I am happy'? And the possessive suffix only touches the continuum, not something beyond it. This is what has been stated:
'Even the I-awareness' —

children.text: śarīram , ādigrahaṇāt jñānam , avasyati , saṃtānarūpatayā vikalpayati avaśyam ; sadṛśāparabhāvabhedagrahaṇasāmarthyavāsanāviṣṭatvāt ---- iti /
children.translated_text: 'the body' — and by the word 'ādi' (etc.), knowledge — 'determines,' i.e., conceptualizes necessarily as having the form of a continuum; because it is pervaded by the impression born of the capacity to grasp the difference of similar and subsequent states.
'Eṣā' (this):
is not denied by us,
'accompanied by verbal expression, called vikalpa' —

children.text: ityanena saṃgṛhītatvāt / etaduktaṃ bhavati ---- ahaṃpratītireva tāvat na ātmā , tasyā api vikalparūpatvāt asthairyācca / etatpratītipratyayo 'pi nāsti anyaḥ śarīrādeḥ , bhavannapi vā vedyapakṣapatitaḥ syāt ---- iti / tathāpi saṃvitsaṃvedyavyatiriktasya ātmano na siddhiḥ ---- ityetat apiśabdena dyotitam / evaṃ nāsti ātmā saṃvitsaṃvedyatryatirikto dṛśyasya tasyānupalabdheḥ ---- iti //1// //2//
children.translated_text: because it is already included under that. What is being said is this: the 'I'-awareness itself is not the Self, since it too is of the nature of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) and is impermanent.
