children.translated_text: And whatever the <s>kāraka</s> (grammatical case-relation) is, it too looks toward action; and action depends on time as the lord of <s>prāṇa</s> (the vital principle); and that [time] too, through the medium of action, being of the nature of all entities, raises up relation. Thus, this variegated worldly life is dependent on relation alone. As stated by the master himself:
{The semblance of worldly life, accomplished together with all objects through relation
whose nature is difference and non-difference, by His own will — I bow to that <s>Śiva</s>. //}
Thus.
Therefore, to examine relation first, he says:
Entities resting in their own selves, appearing as distinct, in a single knowing subject,
possessing mutual connection and unity of form — [these are] the ground of the cognition of relation. //

children.text: rājā puruṣaśca bahistaṭasthau svātmaikaparisamāptau pramātṛbhūmau yadaikyaṃ gacchataḥ , na ca aikyamātraṃ tayoḥ bhedavigalanāpatteḥ , api tu paraspararūpaśleṣātmakaṃ yugapadeva nimajjadunmajjadbhedābhedakoṭidvayadolārohaṇalakṣaṇam anvayarūpam , tadā tāveva sambandhadhiya ālambanaṃ bhavato

children.translated_text: 'the king's man' —

children.text: iti , tathāhi ---- rājā yadā pūrvaṃ dhiyā gṛhīto 'pi na svātmaviśrāntyā tuṣyati tadā rūpāntareṇa puṃsā śleṣaṃ bhajan kṛtārthībhavati , puruṣo 'pyevaṃ , sa ca eṣa rūpaśleṣa eka eva ubhayoḥ cidātmani tathā avasthānarūpaḥ pūrvapratilabdhasaṃvitpratiṣṭhaḥ tata eva adhikasaṃviśrimajjanāt anābhāsamānapṛthagbhavanalakṣaṇaḥ svātantrye viśrāmyati , iti tatraiva nirbhāsate samāskanditapuruṣaparamārtho 'pi , evaṃ bahiranekatā , antastu paraspararūpaśleṣeṇaikyam , iti saṃbandhasya rūpam //4//
children.translated_text: thus. For when the king, though previously grasped by cognition, is not satisfied by resting in his own self, then he becomes fulfilled through adhesion with another form — the man. And the man likewise. And this adhesion of forms is one and the same for both, of the nature of such subsistence in the consciousness-self, resting upon the previously obtained establishment in consciousness; from that very [establishment], through further immersion in consciousness — [immersion] characterized by the non-appearance of separate existence — it rests in freedom. Therefore, it shines there, even though the ultimate reality of the man has been absorbed. Thus, externally there is multiplicity, but internally there is unity through mutual adhesion of forms — this is the nature of relation. //4//

When the king and the man, who are externally separate and each complete in their own selves, attain unity at the level of the knowing subject — and not mere unity, since the unwanted consequence of the dissolution of difference [would follow] — but rather, a form of connection (<s>anvaya</s>) that consists in the mutual adhesion of their forms, characterized by simultaneously sinking-and-emerging at the two extremities of difference and non-difference, as if riding a swing — then those very two become the ground of the cognition of relation:
The appearances of the universal and substance — conceptual constructions take as their support
even externally the one-form, and also the difference of individual instances and parts. //

children.text: jātyavabhāsasya avabhāsamānarūpāyāḥ jāteḥ grāhikā yāḥ kalpanāḥ , tā na kevalaṃ saṃbandhavat antar ekarūpatāṃ bahiśca anekarūpatām ālambante , yāvad bahirapi vyaktibhedalakṣaṇam anaikyaṃ bahireva ca tadanusyūtatārūpām ekatām ālambanatvaṃ nayanti /

children.translated_text: 'Cows' —

children.text: iti hi pratibhāse pṛthakkṛtā bahir vyaktayo bhānti , yena ca bahuvacanam , anuyāyi ca āsāṃ bhāti vapuḥ yata ekaprātipadikārthaparāmarśānugamaḥ , ubhayaṃ ca tad bahireva
children.translated_text: in this appearance, the individuals shine as externally differentiated — hence the plural number — and yet a form that accompanies them also shines, by which there is the following of the reflective grasping of a single nominal-stem meaning. And both of these are external —
'these' —

children.text: iti aṅgulyā nirdeśāt , kevalaṃ bāhyatvamapi sthite paramārthaprakāśāntarbhāve , iti na tatra bhedābhedau dūṣaṇaṃ citrasaṃvedana iva / anena dravye 'pi raktāraktādi virodhaḥ kṛtapratividhānaḥ , āntaraṃ tu aikyaṃ saṃbandhadvāreṇa tadvadeva sarvatra , evam avabhāsamānasya ghaṭa iti avayavidravyasya prāhikā yāḥ kalpanāḥ tā na kevalaṃ saṃbandhavat antarbahīrūpatayā ekānekaviṣayā yāvat bahirapyekaṃ niḥsaṃdhibandharūpatvena bhinnaṃ ca avayavalakṣaṇaikadeśadvāreṇa svīkurvate , ghaṭa iti hi niḥsandibandhanaikaghanātmā vitatarūpaśca bhāti iti //5//
children.translated_text: since they are indicated by pointing with the finger. Only, even externality [is maintained] while the inclusion within ultimate luminosity is established — thus, difference and non-difference there are not a fault, just as in variegated perception. By this, the contradiction of colored and non-colored and such in substance is also remedied. The internal unity, however, through the medium of relation, is exactly the same everywhere. Similarly, the conceptual constructions that grasp a composite substance (<s>avayavin</s>) — appearing as 'pot' — take as their support not only, like relation, the one-and-many as internal and external, but also, even externally, the one through the form of seamless cohesion, and the differentiated through the medium of parts characterized as portions. For 'pot' shines as a single compact mass of seamless cohesion and also as extended in form. //5//

The conceptual constructions that grasp the universal — the universal that is appearing in its appearing form — take as their support not only, like relation, the one-form internally and the many-form externally, but they bring even externally the non-unity characterized by the difference of individuals, and also the unity of the form that pervades them even externally, to the status of being their support.
The synthesis of the <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations) has action-reflection as its content;
the cognition of direction and such takes as its support the connection of the delimited and its delimiter. //

children.text: kārakāṇāṃ kartrādiśaktyādhārāṇāṃ dravyāṇāṃ ca yo 'nyonyaṃ samanvayo dṛśyate , yathā mātṛmeyamānānāṃ mithaḥ , so'ntarlīnapramātmakakriyādiśeṣaparāmarśaikanimittakaḥ , na hi pramāparāmarśam antarvartinaṃ vihāya vastunaḥ sākṣāt anvayo 'tra saṃvedyate , ananyatra bhāvarūpatānimittatā atra viṣayārthaḥ , kārakaśaktināmapi yaḥ svāśrayaiḥ saṃbandhaḥ so'pi kriyāparāmarśanimittakaḥ , dravyāṇāṃ ca śaktīnāṃ ca kriyayā sākaṃ sākṣāt saṃbandhaḥ iti iyaṃ kriyaiva bhagavatī etāvadvijṛmbhitaṃ saṃbandham āvirbhāvayati / asmādidaṃ pūrvaṃ paraṃ dūre ityevaṃ vahirbhinnatayāparāmṛśyamānayoḥ bhāvayorantar abhedanapūrvakaṃ bhedāvamarśamadhyam abhedaviśrāntaṃ ca yat rūpam āmṛśyate tat dig ityucyate / atra hi tayoḥ mukhādyavayavaviśeṣaparāmarśādaraḥ tatsaṃmukhatvaparāṅmukhatvādiniścayaḥ saṃyogasaṃyuktasaṃyogālpatādiparigrahaśca upayogī / kālaparāmarśasya pūrvaparādirūpatve janmasthityalpatādivimarśaścirakṣiprādirūpatve ca , pakṣyati pacati apākṣīt ityādau tu saṃbhāvitasya sphuṭasya sphuṭabhūtapūrvasya ātmīyasaṃvedanaspanditaprāṇādityādikriyāntarasya phalaviśeṣasya ca odanādeḥ parāmarśa upayujyate , evaṃ saṃkhyāparimāṇapṛthaktvasaṃyogavibhāgaprabhṛtiṣu saṃbandharūpataiva vācyā , sarvathā ayaṃ sakṣepaḥ , yatra padārthābhāsasya ātmaviśrāntyā saṃtoṣamapuṇyataḥ ābhāsāntaraparāmarśaviśrāntisākāṅkṣatayā svarūpapariniṣṭhā tatra saṃbandharūpataiva kriyāśaktivijṛnbhāmayī , tatrāpi bhāvāntarāpekṣayā saṃbandhāntaramapi astu , yathā saṃkhyādau samavāyaṃ manyante , na ca anavasthā bhavantyapi doṣāya , pūrvāparakalpasṛṣṭyanavastheva , nahi uttarasaṃbandhasṛṣṭyā vinā pūrvasaṃbandhāvabhāse hāniḥ kācit yen mūle kṣatiḥ śaṃkyeta //6//
children.translated_text: The mutual synthesis (<s>samanvaya</s>) observed among the <s>kārakas</s> — substances that are the substrata of the powers of agent and such — such as the mutual [synthesis] of knower, known, and means of knowing — that is caused solely by the reflective grasping (<s>parāmarśa</s>) of action and such which is dissolved within the knowing subject. For the direct synthesis of things is not perceived here apart from the reflective grasping of the knowing subject that exists within. 'Not elsewhere' here means having the nature of existence as its cause. Even the relation of the <s>kāraka</s>-powers with their substrata is caused by the reflective grasping of action. And the direct relation of substances and powers with action — this action itself, the glorious one, manifests this much relation as its display. 'From this,' 'before that,' 'near,' 'far' — what is reflectively grasped as the form of two entities that are grasped as externally differentiated in this way, but preceded by internal non-differentiation, with difference-awareness in the middle, and resting in non-difference — that is called direction. For therein, the grasping of particular parts such as face and such, the determination of facing-toward and facing-away, and the acceptance of conjunction, conjunction-with-conjunction, proximity, and such are useful. In the reflective grasping of time — when of the form of prior and posterior, the reflection on birth, persistence, proximity, and such [is relevant]; when of the form of long and short duration — and in 'he will cook,' 'he cooks,' 'he cooked' — the reflective grasping of what is anticipated, what is clear, what was previously clear, of the action of other [things] such as one's own vital breath animated by awareness, and of the particular fruit such as cooked rice — is useful. Similarly, in number, measurement, separateness, conjunction, disjunction, and so forth, the nature of relation alone is to be stated. In every case, this is the summary: wherever an appearance of a category, not satisfied by resting in its own self, desiring to rest in the reflective grasping of another appearance, has its own nature established [through that] — there, the nature of relation, which consists of the display of the power of action, [applies]. And even there, with reference to another entity, let there also be another relation — as when some consider <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) in number and such. And there is no infinite regress — even if there is, it is not a fault — just like the infinite regress of prior and subsequent world-creations. For there is no loss in the appearance of the prior relation without the creation of the subsequent relation, by which damage at the root might be apprehended. //6//

children.text: evaṃ sakalalokayātrānuprāṇitakalpānalpasaṃbandhabandhurībhāvaṃ kriyāśaktivijṛmbhātmakam abhidhāya , tasya sthairyopayogau pūrvasūcitau nirūpayitumāha
children.translated_text: Having thus described the elaborate intertwining of innumerable relations that animate all worldly life, as consisting of the display of the power of action, in order to examine the stability and utility previously indicated, he says:
In just this way, the accomplishment of purpose would occur for the knowing subject who desires purposeful activity;
therefore, there is no error of this kind in an object that possesses both difference and non-difference. //

children.text: iha bhāvānāṃ na sattāsaṃbandhaḥ sattvam , avyāpakatvād anavasthāvaiyarthyādidoṣāt , na arthakriyā vastvantaratvāt , na tatkāritvaṃ sarvadā tadāveśādaśanāt , uktaṃ hi
children.translated_text: Here, the being of entities is not their connection with universal existence (<s>sattā</s>), due to the fault of non-pervasiveness, infinite regress, purposelessness, and such; nor is it causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>), since that is a different thing; nor is it the capacity to produce that [efficacy], since the infusion of that is not always observed. For it has been said:
{Causal efficacy too is not innate to objects... //}

children.text: iti / tatkāritvasya ca pratyakṣānupalambhātmakānvayavyatirekagamyasya apratyakṣatve sayo'pi apratyakṣatvaprāptaḥ , nārthakriyākaraṇayogyatvaṃ tasya satyāsatyake niścayakāle duravadhāratvāt , sarvasya ca asya agrakāśamānatvena naraśṛṅgaprāyatvam , arthakriyāntaraparyeṣaṇe ca anavasthā , iti prakāśamānataiva anunmūkyamānatathocitavimarśaparispandā bhāvasya sattvam , sā ca bhedābhedavapuṣāṃ saṃbandhādīnāmasti , iti ---- nirāśaṅkameva satyatvameva eṣām , tathāpi yadi paro'nubadhnīyāt ---- iha lokaḥ prācuryeṇa arthakriyārthī tatkāriṇi satyatvaṃ vyavaharati , tat kiṃ saṃbandhādīnām asti iti , tadasya hṛdayam āśvāsyate , yadi na kupyasi tat sarvatraiva vyavahāre yatrāpi sphuṭā saṃbandhādidhīḥ na udeti eṣameva tatrāpi , iti saṃbandhādirūpatayā bhedābhedavān yo 'rthaḥ tenaiva athakriyā , na tu svātmamātraviśrāntena kācidapi kadācidapi arthakriyā , tathāhi sukhena smaryamāṇena abhilāṣaḥ , ityādi krameṇa sarvo vyavahāraḥ sukhābhāsaśca yo'nubhūtaḥ sa eva abhilaṣyate na tu anyo'nanubhūtaḥ , sa eva abhilaṣyate na tu anyo'nanubhūtaḥ , sa eva ca yadi prāpyate tadabhilaṣitaṃ prāptam iti tuṣyate yadi ca tat tadeva tarhi kim abhilaṣyate ---- prāptatvāt , atha atadeva tathāpi katham arthyate ---- ajñātatvāt , tasmāt etat evaṃ bhavati ---- yadi tadeva ca atadeva ca tadapi ca atadapi ca iti / evaṃ sukhasādhaneṣu vācyam / taduktam ācāryeṇaiva
children.translated_text: Thus. And the capacity to produce that [efficacy], being ascertained through co-presence and co-absence which are of the nature of perceptual apprehension and non-apprehension — if that is non-perceptual, then even co-presence would be non-perceptual. Nor is the capacity to produce that [efficacy] [the criterion], since at the time of determining whether something is real or unreal, it is difficult to ascertain. And all of this, by virtue of not yet being manifest, would be like a hare's horn. And in seeking yet another causal efficacy [to validate the first], there would be an infinite regress. Therefore, the very state of being manifest — with an appropriate reflective vibration (<s>vimarśa</s>) that is not uprooted — is the being of an entity. And that [being] belongs to relations and such, which have the form of both difference and non-difference — therefore, their reality is entirely beyond doubt. Still, if the opponent persists: 'The world, for the most part, being desirous of causal efficacy, attributes reality to what produces it — do relations and such have that?' — to reassure his heart: 'If you are not angered, then in every practical activity, even where a clear cognition of relation and such does not arise, this very [principle applies] there too.' That is, the object that possesses both difference and non-difference in the form of relation and such — it is through that alone that causal efficacy [operates], and never is there any causal efficacy through what rests in its own self alone. For example: through pleasure that is being remembered, desire arises — and thus, in sequence, all practical activity [proceeds]. And the pleasure that was experienced as an appearance is the very one that is desired, not some other that was not experienced; and if that very one is obtained, then one is satisfied that the desired has been obtained. But if it is that very same thing, then why is it desired — since it is already obtained? And if it is not that very same thing, then how can it be sought — since it is unknown? Therefore, this can only be so if it is both that and not-that, and also both that and not-that. Similarly, this should be stated regarding the means of pleasure. As the master himself has said:
{In the desire for something desired, is it the desired itself that is reflected upon, or is it what produces the desired?
And what is unseen cannot be desired; even heaven is desired as the ground of unseen enjoyments.

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ ca saha dṛṣ.yaiva vinaṣṭamiti kārthitā /
children.translated_text: And what was seen is destroyed together with the seeing itself — so what is the desire?
That, through the unity of the seer, is unfallen... //}

children.text: ityādi / evaṃ ca ābhāsātmani asmin asaṃvedyamapi ābhāsāntaraṃ sāmānyasaṃbandharūpatayā anupraviṣṭam , anyathā na kathaṃcidvyavahāraḥ iti sakaladeśakāladaśāpuruṣopayogī yadi ayaṃ vyavahāro na satyaḥ tarhi na anyasya satyatvaṃ vidmaḥ ---- iti na atra bhrāntiḥ iti bhramitavyam / iti śivam //7// āditaḥ 104//
children.translated_text: and so forth. And thus, in this entity whose nature is appearance, even another appearance that is not being perceived has entered in the form of a general relation. Otherwise, there would be no practical activity whatsoever. Thus, if this practical activity, which is useful for all persons, in all places, times, and conditions, is not real, then we do not know what else could be real — therefore, there is no error here: one should not be deluded. Thus ends what is auspicious. //7// From the beginning, [this covers kārikās] 1-104. //

Thus concludes the second chapter (<s>āhnika</s>), entitled 'Examination of Difference and Non-difference' (<s>bhedābhedāvamarśana</s>), in the Action Section (<s>kriyādhikāra</s>) of the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s> composed by the illustrious master <s>Utpaladeva</s>, with the commentary called <s>Vimarśinī</s> composed by the illustrious master <s>Abhinavagupta</s>. // 2 //
Third chapter (<s>āhnika</s>) of the Action Section (<s>kriyādhikāra</s>).
{The means of valid knowledge, whose mouths look toward the knowable object, in the entry into valid cognition, in the sequence of advancing through their own power —

children.text: yasya vaktrāvalokīni prameye taṃ stumaḥ śivam //
children.translated_text: Him, <s>Śiva</s>, whose [they are], we praise. //}

children.text: evaṃ kriyāśaktivisphāranirūpaṇaprasaṅgena saṃbandhapuraḥsaraṃ sāmānyādīnāṃ tattvam upapāditam , adhunā tu saṃbandhatattvameva ekaghanatayā vyutpādanīyam / tacca dvividhameva paramārthataḥ jñāpyajñāpakatā kāryakāraṇatā ca , tatra pūrvasyāṃ mānameyabhāvādicintāspadabhūtāyāṃ sarvam uktacaraṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ ca āyattaṃ ---- pramāṇādhīnā vastusiddhiḥ iti tatra tatra prasiddheḥ , evaṃ ca prakṛtasamarthanīyavastūpayogitayā svayaṃ ca saṃbandha rūpatayā avaśyavicāryāṃ mānādisthitiṃ nirūpayitum
children.translated_text: Thus, in the course of establishing the expansion of the power of action, preceded by relation, the nature of universals and such has been demonstrated. But now, the nature of relation itself must be taught in a concentrated manner. And that is, in ultimate truth, of only two kinds: the relation of revealer and revealed (<s>jñāpya-jñāpaka</s>) and the relation of cause and effect (<s>kārya-kāraṇa</s>). Therein, in the former — which is the ground of deliberation on the relation of valid means, knowable, and such — everything that has been said and will be said depends on it, since the establishment of a thing depends on a valid means of knowledge, as is well known everywhere. And thus, in order to examine the status of valid means and such, which must be investigated both because of their usefulness for the matter at hand and because they are themselves of the nature of relation —
{'This is of such a nature...' /}
beginning with this,
{'...the transaction of Lord and such proceeds. //'}

children.text: ityantaṃ ślokasaptadaśakena āhnikāntaramārabhyate / tatra ślokadvayena pramāṇatatphalasvarūpam , tataḥ prameyasya svarūpaṃ nirūpayituṃ pratyābhāsaṃ pramāṇasya vyāpāro na tu svalakṣaṇātmakavastvekaniṣṭhatāniyamena ---- iti darśayituṃ pratyavamarśabalena ābhāsavyavasthā , iti daśabhiḥ ślokaiḥ ucyate , tatprasaṃgāt mithyājñānasvarūpaṃ ślokena , prameyasvarūpasiddhiśca prakṛtamapi īśvaravādam ava;ambya ghaṭate ---- iti ślokena upadarśyate , sa ca eṣa sarvaḥ pramāṇatatphalaprameyādipravibhāgaḥ sati pramātari pradarśitarūpe , tato na tasya prameyatā yena atrāpi pramāṇavyāpārasaṃbhavaḥ , kevalaṃ vyavahāramātrasiddhiphalaṃ pramāṇam atra , iti ślokatrayeṇa ---- iti tātparyārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: ending with this — a new chapter is begun with seventeen verses. Therein, in two verses, the essential nature of the valid means and its result; then, in order to establish the nature of the knowable, [he shows] that the operation of the valid means is with respect to each appearance and not restricted to a single thing of the nature of the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) — and to show this, through the power of reflective grasping, the arrangement of appearances — this is stated in ten verses. In connection with that, the nature of erroneous cognition in one verse. And that even the establishment of the nature of the knowable is accomplished by relying on the doctrine of the Lord, even as the primary concern — this is shown in one verse. And all this division of valid means, its result, the knowable, and such is [possible only] when the perceiver of the demonstrated nature exists; therefore, it is not a knowable object, by which the operation of the valid means would apply even here; rather, the valid means here has as its fruit merely the establishment of practical activity — this in three verses: such is the purport.
'The cognitions of action, relation, and such are not of the nature of error' —

children.text: iti , tadeva nirṇetuṃ pramāṇatatphalasvarūpaṃ tāvat prasiddhamanuvadati /
children.translated_text: in order to determine that very thing, he first restates the well-known nature of the valid means and its result:
What was stated —
That by whose power a thing is established thus — 'this is of such a nature' —
is the valid means of knowledge; and that [valid means] is its own appearance, a novel arising.
That [appearance], internally, having the nature of reflective grasping, in a single object of designation
that does not differ in space, time, and such — is the uncontradicted cognition of a thing.
such as blue, pleasure, and the like,
is established — does not transgress a definite boundary of manifestation —
'this' —
in its own form,
'of such a nature' —
with the conjunction of qualifying properties such as permanence, impermanence, and such — that, in the world,
is established as a 'valid means of knowledge' (<s>pramāṇa</s>).

children.text: iti sthitam , tacca vivecakena vicāryam ---- iha vastunaḥ svarūpaṃ svātmavaśenaiva na tāvat vyavatiṣṭhate ---- jaḍatvāt , mama nīlaṃ prakāśate caitrasya veti ca tadā kathamavabhāsaḥ , tasmāt anyavaśena vyavatiṣṭhate , anyo 'pi cet jaḍaḥ tat andhena andhasya hastādānam , tasmāt anyo'sau saṃvidāsmā , so 'pi yadi śuddho nirviśeṣo na tarhi nīlasyaiva vyavasthāhetuḥ bhavet ---- pītādāvapi tasya tathātvāt , tadasau nīloparakto nīlonmukho nīlaprakāśasvabhāva ityābhāsaḥ san nīlasya vyavasthāpakaḥ , tatprakāśasvabhāvataiva hi tadvyavasthāpakatā , sa ca nīlasya prakāśo yadi avyatiriktasya , tat pītasyāpi syāt ---- prakāśātmakacittattvatādātmyāviśeṣāt , tena vyatiriktīkṛtasya nīlasya sa prakāśaḥ / nīlaṃ ca ittham tato vyatirekābhāsayogyaṃ yadi so'pyā ---- bhāso mahataḥ prakāśāt vyatiricyate , mahāprakāśāvyatireke tasya tato nīlādeḥ vyatirekābhāvaprasaṃgāt , mahāprakāśācca na vyatirekaṃ kiṃcidapi sahate , iti nūnaṃ tena saṃkoca ātmani nirbhāsanīyaḥ , saṃvido vastūnāṃ ca saṃkocanaprāṇo nañartharūpo'sau śūnya ityucyate , saṃkocāvabhāsa eva ca māyīyapramātuḥ utthānam , ata ekayā sṛṣṭiśaktyā pramātṛpramāṇaprameyollāsaḥ pramārthataḥ , tena ---- śūnyadhīprāṇadehādyupādhyāśrayasvīkārātmakasaṃkocaparigrahasaṃkucitāt m-ayāpramātuḥ anantakālāntarmukhasaṃvedanarūpāt sa pramāṇābhimata ābhāso yāvat prameyonmukhatāsvabhāvaḥ tāvat prameyasya deśakālākārābhāsasaṃbhedavattvāt so 'pi tathaiva kṣaṇe anyānyarūpaḥ sraṣṭavyaḥ , taduktam
children.translated_text: And that is to be examined by the discerning one. Here, the essential nature of a thing does not establish itself by its own power — because it is inert. 'Blue appears to me, or to <s>Caitra</s>' — and how then would there be manifestation? Therefore, it is established by the power of another. And if that other too is inert, then it is the blind leading the blind. Therefore, that other must be of the nature of awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>). And if that too is pure and without distinction, then it would not be the cause of the establishment of blue alone — since it is of the same nature with respect to yellow and such also. Therefore, it is an appearance — colored by blue, turned toward blue, having the nature of blue-luminosity — that establishes blue. For its being of the nature of blue-luminosity is itself its capacity to establish blue. And if that luminosity of blue is of what is non-different [from consciousness], then it would also apply to yellow — due to the non-distinction of identity with the consciousness-principle whose nature is luminosity. Therefore, that luminosity is of blue that has been made distinct. And blue, thus fit for appearing as distinct from that [consciousness], if that appearance too is distinct from the great luminosity — then in the non-distinction from the great luminosity, there would be the consequence of the non-distinction of blue and such from it. And nothing whatsoever tolerates distinction from the great luminosity. Therefore, surely a contraction must be manifested in the self. The vital principle of the contraction of consciousness and things is that whose form is the meaning of negation — and that is called 'void.' And the very appearance of contraction is the arising of the <s>Māyic</s> perceiver. Therefore, by a single power of creation, the efflorescence of perceiver, valid means, and knowable is [produced] in ultimate truth. Therefore, from the <s>Māyā</s>-perceiver — who has been contracted by the adoption of contraction in the form of accepting the substrate of limiting adjuncts such as void, intellect, vital breath, body, and such, and who is of the nature of awareness turned inward for infinite time — that appearance which is considered a valid means, as long as it is of the nature of turning-toward-the-knowable, and since the knowable is mixed with appearances of space, time, and form, that [appearance] too, being of such [varied] form at every moment, must be created. As stated:
'abhinavodayaḥ' (novel arising):

children.text: iti ---- abhinavaḥ ---- kṣaṇaparivāsamlānyāpi na kalaṅkitaḥ , tena
children.translated_text: 'abhinava' (novel) — not tainted by even a moment's staleness; therefore,
'nava-navodaya' (ever-new arising) —

children.text: ityuktaṃ bhavati , so'pi yadi tathābhūto māyāpramātṛlagno na bhavet tato mama nīlāvabhāso yasya tasyaiva pītābhāso mama iti na syāt , asti ca idaṃ svasaṃvedanaṃ ---- yat sarvatra abādhyamānam , ityevaṃ svatvena ābhāsamāno ya ābhāso ---- navanavaprameyaunmukhyāt navanavodayaḥ sa pramāṇam yataḥ pramāṃ vidhatte / kāsau ? pramāṇaphalasvabhāvā iti cet , āha ---- sa eva bodharūpa ābhāso mitiḥ pramāṇaphalam iti saṃbandhaḥ / nanu evaṃ paryāyatvamuktaṃ bhavet na tu phalabhāvaḥ , āha ---- bāhyonmukhatayā prakāśarūpayā tatra tat pramāṇam , yā tu tasyaiva antarmukhātmā vimarśarūpatā prāk upapāditā tatsvabhāvena kevalaṃ viṣayadaśāsaṃkucitena sa eva bodhaḥ phalam , yathāhi
children.translated_text: this is what is meant. And if that [appearance], being of such nature, were not attached to the <s>Māyā</s>-perceiver, then 'the appearance of blue belongs to me, and the appearance of yellow belongs to that other person' — this would not be [possible]. But this self-awareness exists — being uncontradicted everywhere. Thus, the appearance that manifests as belonging to oneself — being an ever-new arising due to the ever-new turning toward the knowable — that is the valid means, since it produces valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>). What is that [valid cognition]? If it is of the nature of the result of the valid means — he says: that very appearance of the nature of cognition is the cognition (<s>miti</s>), the result of the valid means — this is the connection. Objection: In this way, synonymity would be stated, not the status of being a result. He says: Insofar as it is turned outward, in its form as luminosity, there it is the valid means; but the reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) that is the inward-facing nature of that very [luminosity] — which was established earlier — in that nature alone, contracted to the state of the object, that very cognition is the result. Just as:
'He who is valorous — that same I — is victorious' —

children.text: iti ekaniṣṭhe śūratvavijayatve vivekavatā hetuphalabhāvena vyavasthāpyete , yato hi
children.translated_text: thus, valiance and victory, though residing in a single [person], are established by the discerning as having the relation of cause and result; since
'Because I am valorous, therefore [I am] victorious' —
thus. Similarly, 'Because there is the luminosity of blue, therefore' —
'this is blue' —

children.text: iti parāmarśa iti ekarūpatve 'pi hetuphalabhāvaḥ , yayoktaṃ
children.translated_text: the reflective grasping — even though of one form, the relation of cause and result [obtains]. As has been stated:
By whose power — capacity — a thing,
{'By the power of that, by the establishment of that...' /}

Therefore, there is non-difference of the valid means and its result. And since the valid means [operates] through the power of reflective grasping, and reflective grasping is animated by language, and language operates only when an appearance is not touched by other appearances of the nature of space, time, and such — i.e., in a mere appearance of a single category — 'pot,' 'red,' — therefore, the valid means operates with respect to an appearance that has become general through the non-admixture of the two appearances of space and time, which are inclined toward conferring the status of a particular —

Therefore, mere appearance alone is the real thing; but the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is another appearance entirely — one that has the form of the appearance of co-referentiality with that appearance. And the means of valid knowledge for that [co-referentiality] is separate; and for those mixed appearances, the [cognition] that grasps what has been grasped is not a means of valid knowledge — this will come later. By the one who says that determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), which in our view is animated by words, has validity resting in each individual appearance, and [has validity] dependent on that [appearance] as well — it is precisely the validity resting in each individual appearance that has been accepted. But enough of this — what use is further discussion? Objection: If reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) is the operation of valid cognition, then does it not also exist in the case of two moons? Not so; for that [vimarśa], through connection with latent impressions, while connecting itself to [the expectation of] attaining the well-known accepted purposeful activity, and being stable with its operation not uprooted — in that state it becomes such [a valid means]. children.translated_text: is not being uprooted by hearing the words of other people, one recognizes [it as valid] through self-awareness itself. Objection: In this case, where one does not seek purposeful activity, how can the transaction of sublation and non-sublation [operate]? Let it not — what is lost for us? For activity is not everywhere [generated] solely from valid cognition; rather, from doubt itself in some cases, due to the preponderance of the object-side, or due to gradations of desire — since activity is seen in agriculture, in eating poisoned food, and in theft where the danger is certain, probable, or witnessed. Therefore, the intensity of desire is the ground of worldly activity; and one who, having acted, has in some case unreduced valid cognition attains the status of [having] valid cognition, and in some case, becoming otherwise, [attains] its opposite. Thus, from birth — since one has practiced from birth or from hundreds of births the distinction between valid and invalid cognition — just as with gems and silver, one sees its essential nature as different at the very first glance. For there exists an ultimate difference due to difference of cause and such. And therefore, when one considers the limited and bearable pain [of caution], and is not driven hither and thither by the great seizure of desire, then — fearing discordance — acting on the basis of cognition whose validity is certain, whether regarding the unseen or even the seen, one is not contradicted. Such a person is called 'one who acts with deliberation.' By this, the worldly nature of valid cognition has been described, in order to dispel — even regarding the cognition of universal, relation, and such — the doubt of invalidity arising from delusion. For this very reason, the public has not been burdened here with examinations of specific definitions, distinctions, and such. Whatever produces the fruit of reflective awareness that is of unsubiated stability and hence of unobstructed continuance — that, being of the nature of cognition, resting in the knowable, and established in the essential nature of the knowing subject — is a valid means of knowledge. And in sense-cognition, in the awareness of pleasure and such, and in the knowledge of <s>yogins</s>, this is uncontested — since there is direct resting in the appearance that is principally of the form of the knowable. But the cognition born of inference is the understanding of one appearance from another appearance — whether of the nature of an effect or of essential nature — and the restriction of the cause-effect relation of another entity with that, and the restriction of co-referentiality, must be understood as depending solely on the <s>niyati-śakti</s> (power of necessity) of the Lord, and not otherwise. Therefore, inference is a valid means of knowledge in whatever domain of space or time the restriction is known. But <s>āgama</s> (scripture) — being of the nature of inner verbalization in another form, consisting of the firmest reflective awareness — is the most intimate operation of the Lord whose nature is consciousness, virtually the life-force of perception and such. Therefore, whatever is reflectively grasped in whatever way — that is exactly so. Just as:

Although a pot, seen externally, is a single object, it is not of just that extent; rather, it also tolerates being analyzed separately. children.text: iti sattvābhāsameva paśyati , aparān ābhāsān nāmnāpi tu nādriyate , tathā udakāharaṇārthī ghaṭābhāsam , svatantranayanānayanayogyavastvarthī dravyābhāsam , mūlyādyarthī kāñcanāvabhāsam , hṛdyatārthī aujjvalyābhāsam , ādigrahaṇāt dṛḍhatarabhāvārthī dārḍhyābhāsam iti draṣṭavyam , evaṃ rucivyutpattyorapi yojanīyam / evam ete ābhāsabhedā eva vastu ābhāsamānatāsāratvāt vastutāyāḥ / yo 'pi ābhāsasya prāṇabhūto vimarśaḥ so'pi pratyābhāsameva , śabdasya abhijalpātmano bodhajīvitaprakhyasya pratyābhāsameva viśrānteḥ , sat ghaṭo lohitaḥ ityādi / arthakriyākāritvamapi anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ pratyābhāsameva niyataṃ ---- sadābhāsena hṛdbhaṅgaparihāramātrasya saṃpādanāt , tatra ābhāsāntarasya yā apekṣā sā agnyābhāsena arthakriyāyāṃ sādhyāyāṃ pātrābhāsasya iva tadābhāsanāntarīyakatvena ābhāsāntarasyāpi niyatasya apekṣaṇāt / evaṃ yena yena mukhena artho vicāryate tena tena ābhāsamātrātmaiva tathaiva pratibhāsanāt vimarśanāt arthakriyākaraṇācca iti siddham / evaṃ prasiddhataraprasiddhāprasiddhatvātiśayena eko'pi arthogranthakāreṇa traidhaṃ nirūpito
children.translated_text: thus, [the person] sees only the existence-appearance and does not regard the other appearances even by name. Similarly, one desiring to fetch water [sees] the pot-appearance; one desiring an object that can be freely carried or not carried [sees] the substance-appearance; one desiring value and such [sees] the gold-appearance; one desiring attractiveness [sees] the brilliance-appearance; and by the word 'ādi' (etc.), one desiring greater firmness [sees] the firmness-appearance — thus it should be understood. The same should be applied to matters of taste and linguistic usage. Thus, these very differences of appearance constitute the object, since the essence of objecthood is being-manifested. Even the <s>vimarśa</s> (reflective awareness) that is the life-force of appearance is per-appearance, since the word — which is of the nature of inner verbalization and resembles the life of cognition — rests per-appearance: 'existent,' 'pot,' 'red,' and so on. Causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>) too, through co-presence and co-absence, is fixed per-appearance — since by the existence-appearance alone, the mere avoidance of heartbreak is accomplished. The dependence on another appearance therein is because, just as in the causal efficacy to be accomplished, the pot-appearance [is needed] alongside the fire-appearance, so too another fixed appearance is dependent as necessarily entailed by that appearance. Thus, by whichever way the object is examined — by that way it is established as being nothing but appearance, since it appears precisely thus, is reflectively grasped thus, and produces causal efficacy thus. In this way, the author of the treatise has examined a single object in three ways, through the gradation of more well-known, well-known, and less well-known:
'long, circular — smoke — existent pot' —

Thus. Or, seeking a purposeful activity — of the nature of concealment — regarding things that pervade extended space, one would differentiate. Similarly, in practical usage, wishing to learn or to teach what the elders call 'long,' one would make the analysis. Thus, there is the differentiation of appearances there. But the single particular — because of resting in a single appearance of place and a single appearance of time; for the appearances of space and time alone, functioning in the vicinity of universality-producing pervasion, eternality-breaking, and such, extend the nature of particularity. Similarly, like man-ness, the other appearances such as Brahmin and such should also be analyzed. Thus, here to begin with, the differentiation of appearances is more well-known — due to being the ground of very many properties common to both insentient and sentient. By this illustration, even in smoke, the well-known differences of appearances — smoke-ness, sandalwood-ness, the-state-of-having-arisen-from-śrīkhaṇḍa-sandalwood, and such — should be differentiated. By the well-known illustration, even in the case of the pot — the part that is not well-known — there too, the differentiation of appearance-portions exists. For, when one who is experiencing a sort of heartbreak of the thought 'there is nothing at all here' sees a pot —

children.text: nanu evaṃ pratyābhāsameva vastutve eko ghaṭātmā na vastu syāt ityāśaṃkyāha
children.translated_text: Objection: If objecthood is thus per-appearance, then a single pot-entity would not be an object — anticipating this, he says:
From the difference of appearances, the definite causal efficacy of objects [arises]; again,
from the appearance of those that are non-different through co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>).

children.text: ābhāsānāṃ miśraṃ yadrūpaṃ tatra avaśyaṃ kaścidābhāsaḥ pradhānatvena anyābhāsānāṃ viśrāntipadīkāryaḥ sa teṣāṃ samānamadhikaraṇam , tena saha yasteṣāṃ saṃbandhaḥ tat sāmānādhikaraṇyam , tena upalakṣito yaḥ pratibhāsaḥ ---- arthonmukhaḥ prakāśaḥ tadanuprāṇakaśca napadātmā parāmarśaḥ ---- tasya sarvasya ekābhāsaviśrāntatāniyamāt , tasmāt taṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyābhāsaṃ samanughrāṇayati yo vākyātmā vākyārthaparāmarśarūpo vimarśaḥ ---- iha idānīṃ eṣa ghaṭo'sti ityevaṃrūpaḥ tato hetoḥ ye abhedina ekasvalakṣaṇatām prāptā na ca svarūpabhedam ujjhantaḥ teṣām anyā viśiṣṭā samuditā arthakriyā / ābhāsavimarśabhede punaranyā niyatā ekaikamātrarūpā ābhāsapratibhāsaśabdābhyāṃ sūtre vimarśo'pi ākṣipto mantavyaḥ / punaḥ śabdo viśeṣadyotakaḥ kākākṣivat ubhayatra yojyaḥ / bahuvacanena aikye'pi svarūpabhedāparityāga uktaḥ , tatra ca aikyāvabhāse paratantraṃ sat pṛthaktvaṃ yadā ābhāsānāṃ tadā samānarūpavyaktyuparañjakatvena pāramārthikaṃ sāmānyarūpatvam , ghaṭābhāsasya tu śuddhasya svatantraparāmarśe yogyatāmātreṇa sāmānyarūpatā na vastuto ---- dravyādanyo hi sarvaḥ padārthaḥ paratantratāsāraḥ , evam eko'pi ghaṭātmā ca ityapi satyameva ---- ābhāsavimarśārthakriyābalena tathā vyavasthāpanāt iti //6//
children.translated_text: Among the mixed form of appearances, necessarily some appearance must be made primary as the resting-ground of the other appearances — that is their co-location (<s>samāna-adhikaraṇa</s>); the relation of those [appearances] with it is <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-location). The appearance that is qualified by that — the luminosity directed toward the object, and the reflective awareness of the nature of a verbal expression that animates it — all of this is fixed in resting upon a single appearance. Therefore, the <s>vimarśa</s> of the nature of a sentence-meaning-reflective-grasping that favors that co-locating appearance — of the form 'here, now, this pot exists' — from that reason, those [appearances] that have attained non-difference — having reached the state of a single particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) without abandoning their own-nature-difference — their causal efficacy is different, specific, combined. When there is difference in appearance and <s>vimarśa</s>, there is yet another, definite, single-unit causal efficacy — by the words '<s>ābhāsa</s>' and '<s>pratibhāsa</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s>, <s>vimarśa</s> too should be understood as implied. The word 'punaḥ' (again) indicates distinction, and should be applied in both places like the crow's-eye [principle]. By the plural number, even in unity, the non-abandonment of own-nature-difference is stated. And therein, when in the appearance of unity the separateness of appearances is dependent, then through the tinting by instances of similar form, there is ultimate universality (<s>sāmānya</s>). But for the pure pot-appearance, the universal form exists only through mere fitness for independent reflective grasping, not in reality — for every category other than substance has dependence as its essence. Thus, even a single pot-entity is indeed real — since it is so established by the force of appearance, <s>vimarśa</s>, and causal efficacy. // 6 //

children.text: nanu ekenaiva arthakriyā na tatra , api tu ābhāsasamudāyāt arthakriyāsamudāyaḥ , ābhāsāśca bhinnā api yadi ekām arthakriyāṃ kartuṃ miśrībhavanti , tadā kasteṣām iyattāvadhiḥ iti codyam apavadati /
children.translated_text: Objection: A single [appearance] does not produce causal efficacy; rather, from the aggregate of appearances arises an aggregate of causal efficacies. And if appearances, though different, become mixed to produce a single causal efficacy, what is the limit of their measure? — he dispels this objection:
Just as the lights of separate lamps, or streams [entering] the ocean —
so, of non-contradictory appearances, the cognition of unity [arises from] a single effect.

children.text: pṛthak vatinyo yāḥ pradīpasya prabhāḥ sūkṣmatamāvalokanasāmarthyādhānalakṣaṇāṃ yām arthakriyāṃ na kṛtavatyaḥ tāmeva ekabhavanābhyantaraṃ saṃmūrchitātmāno vidadhate , na tatra arthakriyāṇāṃ samudāyo 7sti / sāgarapatitāni ca srātāṃsi bahutarataraṅgāraṃbhārthakriyākārīṇi / tadvat ghaṭaḥ kāñcano lohitaḥ tato'yaṃ śivaliṅgaśiromārjanocitasalilāharaṇārthakriyocito dṛṣṭamātra eva tīvraprītilakṣaṇārthakriyākārī ; iti siddhamevārthakriyākāritvam / yat punarābhāsānāṃ miśraṇe kā sīmā iti ? tatra ucyate ---- yeṣām avirodhaḥ ta eva ābhāsā miśrībhavanti , nahi rūpābhāso mārutābhāsena miśrībhavati ---- virodhāt , so'pi ca niyatiśaktyutthāpitaḥ / pṛthak ye dīpaprakāśāḥ teṣāṃ saṃbandhi yadekaṃ sāgare srotasāṃ ca yadekaṃ vastu tena kāryā yathā aikyadhīḥ tathā aviruddhā ye avabhāsā ghaṭalohitakāñcanādayaḥ teṣāṃ saṃbandhi tadekaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ tatkāryā aikyadhīriti saṃbandhaḥ . aikyadhiyā ---- pratibhāso vimarśo 'rthakriyā ca iti svīkṛtam //7//
children.translated_text: The rays of a lamp, when separate, do not accomplish the causal efficacy that consists of bestowing the capacity for the subtlest observation; but when combined within a single room, they accomplish precisely that. There is no mere aggregate of causal efficacies there. And streams that have entered the ocean produce the causal efficacy of initiating extremely numerous waves. Similarly, a pot that is golden and red — therefore, this [pot] is fit for the causal efficacy of fetching water suitable for washing the head of a <s>Śivaliṅga</s>, and produces the causal efficacy of intense delight at the mere sight. Thus, causal efficacy is already established. As for the question — what is the boundary when appearances mix? — to that it is said: only those appearances that are non-contradictory become mixed; for the form-appearance does not mix with the wind-appearance — due to contradiction; and even that [contradiction] is raised by <s>niyati-śakti</s> (the power of regulation). The separate lights of lamps — that single thing related to them; and of streams in the ocean — that single thing; by that is caused the cognition of unity. Similarly, of non-contradictory appearances — pot, red, golden, and such — that single particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) related to them, by that is caused the cognition of unity — this is the connection. Through the cognition of unity — appearance, <s>vimarśa</s>, and causal efficacy — [all three] are accepted. // 7 //

children.text: nanvevaṃ pratyābhāsaṃ pramāṇasya viśrāntatvāt agnyābhāse agnijñānaṃ pramāṇaṃ dhūmajñānaṃ ca dhūmābhāsamātre kāryakāraṇabhāvāvabhāso 'pi tāvanmātre , tataśca dhūmābhāso'pi agnyābhāsaṃ vyabhicaret ityādi bahutaropaplavaprasaṃgaḥ iti śaṃkām apohitum āha
children.translated_text: Objection: If the means of valid knowledge rests per-appearance, then the knowledge of fire is valid for the fire-appearance alone, the knowledge of smoke for the smoke-appearance alone, and the appearance of the cause-effect relation [extends only] to that much. And therefore, the smoke-appearance too would deviate from the fire-appearance — and so there would be the consequence of numerous confusions. To remove this doubt, he says:
Therein, in the undifferentiated fire and such, the properties of being-an-effect, being-a-cause, heat,
being-the-referent of such-and-such words, and so on — are known from a single means of valid knowledge.

children.text: tatreti ---- pratyābhāsaṃ pramāṇaṃ viśrāmyati , ityasminnapi pakṣe na kaścit doṣaḥ , tathāhi ---- aviśiṣṭo yadyapi bahnyābhāso deśakālābhāsapramukhaiḥ ābhāsaiḥ asaṃkīrṇatvena sāmānyamātrarūpatvāt tathāpi sa evābhāso yāvadbhirābhāsairavinābhūto bhagavatyā niyatiśaktyā niyamitaḥ tāvato 'vabhāsān svīkṛtyaiva pramāṇakṛtāṃ niścayapadavīm avatarati / tataśca bahnyābhāsa indhanakāryatvābhāsena dhūmakāraṇatābhāsena uṣṇasvabhāvatābhāsena ca svābhāvikāvyabhicaritaniyamaḥ pratīyamāno viśvatraiva sarvadaiva ca tathā pratīto bhavati ---- ekatvāt tasya / asvābhāviko 'pi yaḥ svabhāvaḥ puruṣakṛtasamayādimukhaprekṣī , tadyathā ---- agniśabdavācyatvaṃ ghaṭapratipattikāritvamityevamādiḥ , so'pi ekapratyakṣādevaniścīyate , tasya hi pramātuḥ kṛtrimeṇa itareṇa vā rūpeṇa ābhāsāntaranāntarīyakatayā asau bahnyābhāsaḥ saṃviditaḥ sarvadeśakālagataḥ tathā saṃviditaḥ , iti tatra kiṃ pramāṇāntareṇa / tasya yathecchaṃ puruṣasamayena niyujyamānasya śabdasya artho 'yaṃ jvaladbhāsvarākāra ābhāsa ityanena niyatiśaktireva sarvatra śaraṇam iti piśunayati / etaduktaṃ bhavati ---- yatkiṃcit kṛtrimam itaradvā bhāvābhāsasya ābhāsāntareṇa nāntarīyakatayā pratibhāti tatra niyatiśaktimātrameva paraṃ vijṛmbhate / tattu niyatirūpaṃ pūrvāparavitatakālam ---- indhanakāryatve dhūmakāraṇatve uṣṇasvabhāvatve ca ābhāsamāne , anaticirakālaṃ tu bahnyādiśabdavācyatāvabhāsādāviti viśeṣaḥ / tataśca niyatiśaktyupajīvanena dhūmābhāso 'pi agnyābhāsāvyabhicārī iti na kaścit viplavaḥ / kāryatā kāraṇatā uṣṇatā ca tasya tasya śabdasyārthatā tattacchabdā bhidheyatā , ādigrahaṇāt ---- gandharasaśūnyatā ūrdhvadiksaṃyogitā jalavirodhitā ca , ityevaṃbhūto ya ātmā svabhāvo vahnyādau sa ekasmādeva pramāṇāt mataḥ ---- saṃvidita iti yāvat / avicchedaḥ iti kāvye ayaṃ samayo , na granthe dvitīyatṛtīyapādayoḥ sāmastye 'pi adoṣaḥ / pṛthagbhāvapratyayaprayogo vastvantarāpekṣānapekṣātaḥ kṛtakatvākṛtakatvābhyāṃ vargabhedaṃ sūcayitum //8//
children.translated_text: 'Therein' — even in this position that the means of valid knowledge rests per-appearance, there is no fault whatsoever. For thus: although the fire-appearance is undifferentiated — in the sense of being of the nature of a mere universal, due to non-admixture with appearances such as space, time, and such — nevertheless, that very appearance, with however many appearances it is invariably concomitant as regulated by the blessed <s>niyati-śakti</s> (power of regulation), enters the path of certainty through the means of valid knowledge only by accepting all those appearances. And therefore, the fire-appearance, being experienced with an invariable and natural concomitance with the appearance of being-an-effect of fuel, the appearance of being-a-cause of smoke, and the appearance of having-heat-as-its-nature — is experienced thus everywhere and always — due to its unity. And even the non-natural property — a nature that looks toward person-made convention and such — such as being-the-referent of the word 'fire,' being the cause of the cognition of a pot [when used as a source of light], and so forth — that too is ascertained from a single perception. For that fire-appearance has been cognized by that perceiver, with its artificial or natural form, as necessarily entailed by other appearances, in all places and times, as so cognized — so what need is there of another means of valid knowledge? For the word whose object is arbitrarily assigned by human convention — that this object, the blazing and shining appearance, is [the referent of the word 'fire'] — by this, it is hinted that <s>niyati-śakti</s> (power of regulation) alone is the refuge everywhere. What is being said is this: whatever artificial or other inseparability of one entity-appearance with another appearance appears — therein, <s>niyati-śakti</s> alone supremely plays forth. But the regulation-form extends over a long temporal span — in the case of being-an-effect of fuel, being-a-cause of smoke, and having-heat-as-its-nature when they appear; but over a not-very-long time in the case of the appearance of being-the-referent of the word 'fire' and such — this is the distinction. And therefore, through dependence on <s>niyati-śakti</s>, the smoke-appearance too is invariably concomitant with the fire-appearance — so there is no confusion whatsoever. Being-an-effect, being-a-cause, heat, and being-the-referent of such-and-such word, being-expressible by such-and-such word — and by the word 'ādi' (etc.): being devoid of smell and taste, conjunction with the upward direction, opposition to water — the nature or essence that is of such a kind in fire and such is known from a single means of valid knowledge alone — meaning, cognized. The rule in poetry that [compounds should be] without break [does not apply] in a treatise; in the second and third <s>pādas</s> [of the verse], even in combination there is no fault. The usage of separate case-affixes, [distinguishing] between dependence and non-dependence on another entity, hints at the class-distinction of artificial and natural [properties]. // 8 //

children.text: evaṃ bhāvasvabhāvavyavasthāpanaṃ pratyābhāsaviśrāntena ekena pramāṇena kriyate , teṣāmapi ābhāsānāṃ yathocitaṃ yadanyonyanāntarīyakatvaṃ tat ekena saṃvedanarūpeṇa tadanekapramitābhāsaviṣayapūrvapravṛttasaṃvedanakalāpānuprāṇakāntarmukhasvarūpeṇa niścīyate , tacca aikyābhāsamātre anusaṃdhānarūpaṃ pramāṇam , anusandhīyamāneṣu tu ābhāseṣu gṛhītagrāhitvāt apramāṇam , tatra tu pratyekaṃ prācyameva pramāṇam / bhāvasvabhāvavyavasthāpanātmakamānasapravṛttyatiriktakāyapravṛttyupayogastu yathā pramāṇaviṣayaḥ taṃ prakāraṃ darśayitum āha
children.translated_text: Thus, the establishment of the nature of entities is accomplished by a single means of valid knowledge that rests per-appearance. And the appropriate mutual inseparability of those appearances is ascertained by a single cognition — which is of an internal nature animating the aggregate of prior cognitions that had for their object the many previously cognized appearances. And that means of valid knowledge, which is of the form of recognition (<s>anusaṃdhāna</s>), operates only upon the mere appearance of unity; but with respect to the appearances being recognized, since those appearances have already been grasped, it is not a means of valid knowledge [for them] — for that, per-appearance, the prior [cognition] alone is the means of valid knowledge. But the utility for bodily activity that goes beyond the mental activity of establishing the nature of entities — how that is the domain of the means of valid knowledge — to show that manner, he says:
But that activity, of one who desires [a particular result], in a particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) differentiated by other perceptions relating to space and such, is
contemporaneous activity... //

children.text: bāhyā tāvat arthakriyā svalakṣaṇataḥ svālakṣaṇye ca deśakālābhāsayojanasyaiva antaraṅgatvam tatrāpi ca viśeṣarūpatāpi parāmarśa vinā na kiṃcit , parāmarśadvāreṇa tu pramātari viśrāmyantī pramātuḥ saṃvedanaikarūpasya deśakālāyogena aikyāt abhyujjhatyeva viśeṣarūpatām , iti sarvatra advayaṃ paramārthataḥ , tathāpi tu yā viśeṣarūpatā bhāti tasyāṃ parameśvarasvātantryameva nimittaṃ yat , tat māyāśaktirityucyate / tatra viśeṣasādhyārthakriyāviśeṣeṇa yo'rthī tasya yā svalakṣaṇe tasmin viśeṣarūpe arthe tatkālabhāvinī vāṅmanaḥ kāyapravṛttiḥ sā deśe , ādigrahaṇāt kāle svarūpāntare tadanusandhānādau ca yāni adhyakṣāntarāṇi bahūni pratyakṣāṇi teṣāṃ bhinne bhede nimitte sati bhavati , na anyathā / naikaikataḥ pramāṇāt sā pravṛttiḥ api tu pramāṇasamūhādeva / samūhatā ca parasya na upapannā , asmākaṃ tu ekasvasaṃvedanaviśrāntimayī sā budhyate , iti uktaṃ prāk
children.translated_text: External causal efficacy, to begin with, is from the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>); and in [establishing] particularity, the association of space-and-time-appearances alone is the inner factor. And even therein, without <s>vimarśa</s> (reflective awareness) the specific form is nothing; but through the medium of <s>vimarśa</s>, resting in the perceiver — who is of the single nature of awareness — through unity due to the non-conjunction of space and time, it abandons its specific form. Thus, everywhere, ultimately there is non-duality. Nevertheless, the specific form that appears — the sole cause thereof is the Supreme Lord's absolute freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>), which is called <s>māyā-śakti</s>. Therein, for one who desires a specific causal efficacy accomplished through specific [features], the activity of speech, mind, and body that is contemporaneous with that specific object — the particular — that activity occurs in space, and by the word 'ādi,' in time, in other forms, in the recognition of those and such, when there is the occasion of differentiation through the many perceptions — and not otherwise. That activity arises not from a single means of valid knowledge, but from an aggregate of means of valid knowledge. And the aggregate-nature is not tenable for the opponent; but for us, it is understood as consisting of resting in a single self-awareness. Thus it has been said previously,
{If they are not internally included... /} (<s>Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā</s> 2.3.7)

children.text: ityatra / iyameva ca sā pramāṇānāṃ yojanā , yojikā ca yuktirityucyate / gandhadravyādiyuktivat / evaṃ pratyakṣasamūhādeva pravṛttiriti tātparyam / deśādikeṣvadhyakṣeṣvapi deśābhāsādiyojanāyāmapi , antaḥ ---- pramātari abhinnaṃ yat svalakṣaṇaṃ tatra iti vā saṃgatiḥ / deśādikairadhyakṣāntaraiḥ pratyakṣībhūtairābhāsāntarairbhinne svalakṣaṇe nimitte sati pravṛttiḥ , iti vā yojanā / atrāpi prameyavahutvanirūpaṇadiśā tadanuyāyitvena abhidhīyamānaḥ pramāṇasamūho nimittatvena ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text: in that context. And this very arrangement of the means of valid knowledge is the arranging logic called <s>yukti</s> (reasoning) — like the logic of fragrance, substance, and such. Thus, the purport is that activity arises from an aggregate of perceptions alone. Even in perceptions relating to space and such — even in the association of space-appearance and such — 'antaḥ' means in the perceiver, in the non-different particular; the connection may also be thus. [Alternatively:] when there is the occasion of differentiation of the particular through perceptions — appearances that have become perceptual — relating to space and such through other perceptions, then activity occurs — this too is a possible construal. Here too, the aggregate of means of valid knowledge, being described as following the multiplicity of the provable, is stated to be the occasion [of activity].

children.text: nanu kiṃ prāttyakṣyāmeva pravṛttau pramāṇasamūha upayogī ? netyāha
children.translated_text: Objection: Is the aggregate of means of valid knowledge useful only in activity [arising from] direct perception? He answers: No —
...even from inference. // <s>Īpk</s> 2,3.9 //

children.text: na kevala pratyakṣataḥ pravṛttiḥ deśādikādhyakṣāntarabhedarūpapramāṇasamūhanimittā yāvat anumānato 'pi tathaiva / dhūmābhāsamātre agnyābhāsamātre dhūmasyāgnyābhāsāvyabhicāritve parvatābhāse ca yāni pratyakṣāntarāṇi yacca tadgṛhītātirikte ayogavyavacchede

children.translated_text: 'there is fire here' —

children.text: ityevaṃbhūte pṛthak anumānaṃ pramāṇam tatsamūhādeva arthinaḥ tātkālikī pravṛttiḥ iti saṃbandhaḥ //9//
children.translated_text: the contemporaneous activity of the one who desires [arises] from that aggregate alone — this is the connection. //9//

Not only does activity [arise] from perception — [that is,] from an aggregate of means of valid knowledge of the nature of other perceptions consisting of differences of space and such — but even from inference, in the same way. The other perceptions regarding the mere smoke-appearance, the mere fire-appearance, the non-deviation of smoke from fire-appearance, and the mountain-appearance — and the separate inference as a means of valid knowledge, in the exclusion of non-connection with respect to what is additional to what those have grasped, of the form

children.text: evaṃ vimarśabalādeva bhedābhedavyavasthā , tadeva hi parameśvarasya saṃvedanātmanaḥ śivanāthasya svātantryaśaktivijṛmbhitam ; tataśca paraiḥ yat ucyate

children.translated_text: 'in [appearing as] far and near and such, the object is non-different' —

children.text: iti tadapi uappadyate , na tu anyathā kathaṃcit , ---- iti nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: this too is accounted for, but not otherwise in any way — this is demonstrated.

Thus, by the force of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) alone is the determination of difference and non-difference. For that is precisely the display of the power of freedom (<s>svātantrya-śakti</s>) of the Supreme Lord, Lord <s>Śiva</s>, whose nature is consciousness. And therefore, what others say —
Through being far and near of objects, through [their being] hidden and directly present in nature,
through internality and externality, through defects of the revealing [instrument], or otherwise as well —
even of those whose hue of appearance is different, the unity that is called
a single reflective grasping, from the primary appearance, is unobstructed. //

children.text: pratibhāsamātreṇa vyavasthāṃ kurvataḥ kathaṃ dūrādūrayorvastunorabhedaḥ , pratibhāsasya sakalāsakalāvṛtānāvṛtāditayā yathākathaṃcidapi bhedāt ? nanuvimarśe'pi pratyābhāsaṃ tathaiva bhinnatā , ? satyam , tathāpi tu paro yo vimarśaḥ sa evāyaṃ padārthaḥ iti ekapratyavamarśarūpaḥ , tena prāṇitakalpena ā samantāt khyānaṃ prathanaṃ yasya mukhyāvabhāsasya ekarūpabhāvābhāsasya , ekapratyavamarśe taducito 'pi hi astyekāvabhāsaḥ , ābhāsavimarśayoranyonyabhaviyogāt / tasmāt mukhyāvabhāsādekatvamapratihatamāste / yadevānumitaṃ tadeva dṛṣṭam , ---- ityatra pratyakṣaparokṣatārūpeṇātmanā svabhāvena bhinnā avabhāvacchāyā amukhyo'vabhāso yeṣāṃ teṣām ekatvaṃ mukhyāvabhāsata ekapratyavamarśānuprāṇitāt , ---- iti saṃgatiḥ / bāhyāntaratayā bhināvabhāsānāmaikyaṃ yathā yadeva dṛṣṭaṃ tadevāntarahamullikhāmi , ---- iti / vyañjakānāṃ dīpālokādīnāṃ doṣairbhonnāvabhāsānām aikyam , yadeva raktotpalaṃ dīpena nīlaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tadeva sūryāṃśubhirlohitaṃ paśyāmi , iti / anyenāpi prakāreṇa indriyāpāṭavādinā ekapārśvasaṃmukhatvādinā vā yeṣāmavabhāsacchāyā bhinnā , teṣāmapi mukhyapratyavamarśānuvartyavabhāsasvarūpabalāt aikyameva , ---- iti sthitam //10////11//
children.translated_text: How can there be non-difference of objects that are far and near, for one who establishes [things] by mere appearance alone — since appearance differs in every way through being complete, incomplete, covered, uncovered, and so forth? Objection: Even in reflective awareness, there is differentiation per-appearance in the same way. True, but still, the other reflective awareness — 'this is the very same object' — being of the form of a single reflective grasping, and being the life-force, as it were, by which the primary appearance — the single-form-nature-appearance — is fully manifest from all sides — in a single reflective grasping, there is indeed a suitable single appearance as well, due to the mutual inseparability of appearance and reflective awareness. Therefore, the unity from the primary appearance remains unobstructed. 'That which was inferred is the very same that was seen' — here, those whose non-primary appearance, whose hue of appearance, is different through the nature of being directly perceived and being hidden — their unity from the primary appearance, animated by a single reflective grasping — this is the connection. The unity of those whose appearances differ through internality and externality — as in 'the very thing I saw is what I inwardly depict.' The unity of those whose appearances differ through defects of the revealing [instruments] such as lamplight and such — 'the very red lotus that was seen as dark by lamplight, I see as red by sunlight.' And by any other mode as well — through dullness of sense faculties, or through being oriented toward one side, and such — even of those whose hue of appearance is different, the unity from the primary reflective grasping, by the force of the appearance-nature that follows it — is established. //10// //11//

children.text: nanu dūrādūrādāvastu sa evārthaḥ pramātradhyavasitārthakriyāṃśe tathaivopayogāt , vāhyāntaratvādau katham , āntarasyārthakriyāyāṃ pramātradhyavasitāyāmanuyogāt ---- iti bhrāntiṃ bhaṅktumāha
children.translated_text: Objection: In the case of far and near, it is indeed the same object, since the utility is the same in the aspect of causal efficacy determined by the knowing subject; but in the case of external and internal, how can [there be identity], since the internal is challenged regarding [its] causal efficacy as determined by the knowing subject? To break this confusion, he says:
Even causal efficacy is not innate to objects; it is regulated by the will of the Lord.

children.text: niyatā sā hi tenāsyā nākriyāto'nyatā bhavet //
children.translated_text: For that [causal efficacy] is fixed by Him; therefore, there can be no otherness [of the object] from [the absence of] its efficacy. //

children.text: iha {kāryakaraṇatā}(Ipk 2,3.8) ityatra svarūpamivārthakriyāpi yā madhye gaṇitā , sā sahajārthasvarūpabhūtā na bhavati , tatkāritvaṃ hi yasmāt īśvarecchayā niyataṃ bhavane cābhavane ca / yato naiṣā svarūpaṃ tena tasyā akaraṇāt hetorbhāvasyānyatvaṃ nāśaṅkanīyaṃ svarūpabhedāt hi saṃbhāvyetānyatvaṃ , na ca svarūpam arthakriyākāritvam , ---- ityuktaṃ vakṣyate ca bahuśaḥ / svarūpaṃ ca pratyavamarśavalādekameva bāhyāntarādāvapi , iti //12//
children.translated_text: Here, in {'causal capacity'} (<s>Īpk</s> 2,3.8), the causal efficacy that was counted in the middle as if it were the essential nature — that is not the innate essential nature of the object. For its capacity to produce [effects] is regulated by the will of the Lord — both in production and in non-production. Since this is not its essential nature, the otherness of an entity from the cause — [namely] from the absence of producing [causal efficacy] — should not be apprehended. For otherness could be surmised from difference of essential nature, and causal capacity is not the essential nature — this has been stated and will be stated many times. And the essential nature, by the force of reflective grasping, is one and the same even in the external and internal and such. //12//

children.text: nanu vimarśabalādeva yadi vastūnāṃ bhedābhedavyavasthā tarhi idānīṃ trijagati nivṛttā bhrāntisaṃkathāḥ , śuktikāyāmapi satyarajatataiva āpatati

children.translated_text: 'this is silver' —

children.text: iti vimṛśyamānatvāt , tataśca bhrāntyabhāve bādhānupapatteḥ kimarthamuktaṃ {mitirvastunyavādhitā}(Ipk 2,3.2) iti / vyabhicārābhāve hi

'unsublated' —

children.text: ityasya viśeṣaṇasya vyavacchedyaṃ na labhyate , ityāśaṅkāṃ nirasyati

Objection: If the determination of difference and non-difference of things is by the force of reflective awareness alone, then now the talk of error in the three worlds is ended! Even in the case of a shell, the consequence would be that the silver is real,
Even though there is a single reflective grasping of silver in a shell, the silver does not abide [there];
due to non-concordance of the adventitious locus — even in the two moons, the sky is otherwise. //
'This is silver — stable, common to all knowing subjects, fit for causal efficacy' —

children.text: iti idamaṃśe rajatādyaṃśeṣu tatsaṃmelanāṃśe ca ābhāsavimarśanabalāt na tāvat kiṃcit mithyātvam / kiṃtu uttarakālaṃ yo bhaviṣyati vimarśo
children.translated_text: by the force of the appearance and reflective grasping of the 'this'-aspect, the silver-aspects, and their combination-aspect, there is certainly no falsity. But the subsequent reflective grasping that will arise —
