children.text: evamadhikāradvayena jñānakriyāsvarūpaṃ vitatya nirṇītam / athedaṃ vaktavyaṃ kriyā nāma viśvapadārthāvabhāsalakṣaṇā ityuktaṃ samanantarameva , ke ca te viśve padārthāḥ , iti / tatrābhāsarūpā eva jaḍacetanalakṣaṇāḥ padārthāste ca kriyatā rūpeṇa saṃgṛhyante , nahi pratyakṣaṃ māyāpramātuḥ sarvatra kramate / anumānamapyevam , na hi yadyadasti tatra tatra liṅgavyāptyādigrahaṇasaṃbhavaḥ / āgamastvaparicchinnaprakāśātmakamāheśvaravimarśaparamārthaḥ kiṃ na paśyet , iti tadanusāreṇa padārthanirṇayaṃ viśvaprameyīkaraṇapratilabdhatadviśvottīrṇapramātṛpadahṛdayaṅgamīkārābhiprāyeṇa nirūpayitumācārya āgamādhikāraṃ tṛtīyamārabhate /
children.translated_text: Thus, through the two sections, the nature of knowledge and action has been determined at length. Now, this is to be stated: action has been defined as the manifestation of the totality of universal entities — and immediately [the question arises]: what are those universal entities? Therein, those entities, characterized as insentient and sentient, are of the nature of appearances, and they are subsumed under the form of being-acted-upon. For direct perception of the <s>Māyā</s>-perceiver does not extend everywhere. Inference is likewise [limited], for not everywhere that something exists is it possible to grasp the logical mark, pervasion, and such. But <s>āgama</s> (scripture), whose ultimate reality is the reflective awareness of the Great Lord whose luminosity is unlimited — what would it not see? Therefore, with the intention of determining entities in accordance with scripture, and of making the entire universe an object of valid knowledge, thereby bringing to the heart the supreme perceiver-level that transcends the universe — the master commences the third <s>Āgamādhikāra</s> (Scripture Section).
'Thus, abiding internally and externally' —
beginning with this,
'from the distinction of gross, subtle, and supreme' —
ending with this — the individual-appearance-nature of each [tattva], from <s>Śiva</s> down to the edge of earth, established by scripture, which in other systems is called
'the universal' —

children.text: iti yadvyavahṛtaṃ , yasya sāmānādhikaraṇyayogādanantasvalakṣaṇāvabhāsanavyūhaviśeṣapūrvakaḥ samasto 'yaṃ śarīrabhuvanādivibhavaḥ , taṃ parameśvarāgamasiddhaṃ yuktyāpyavagataṃ pratyekatastattvagrāmaṃ darśayati ityāhnikatātparyam /
children.translated_text: and whose association with co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) is preceded by the specific array of infinite particular-appearance-manifestations — [showing that] this entire splendor of bodies, worlds, and such [arises from that] — he displays the entire group of principles (<s>tattvas</s>), established by the scripture of the Supreme Lord and also understood through reasoning, each individually. This is the purport of the daily lesson.
Therein, in eleven verses,

children.text: tatrādhikārasaṃgatiṃ yojayan pūrvapakṣapratikṣepaṃ copasaṃharan śivatattvasvarūpameva darśayitumāha
children.translated_text: There, connecting the sections and also concluding the refutation of the opponent's position, in order to show the very nature of the <s>Śiva-tattva</s> (Śiva principle), he says:
Thus, action, which is the internal-external operation following the sequence of time,
belongs to the perceiver alone; therefore, knowledge and action are inseparable from each other.

children.text: evamiti , yataḥ paradarśanoktaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvo jaḍarūpapratiṣṭho na kathaṃcidupapannaḥ , kintu cidrūpa evāntarbahirātmanā prakāśaparamārthenāpi vapuṣā tathābhāsanarūpeṇa vartamānaḥ kālakramamākṣipan kriyābhidhīyate , tasya pramātureva jñānaśaktivapuṣo dharmastat iti / tasmādaviyuktaṃ jñānaṃ kriyā ca / jñānaṃ vimarśānuprāṇitam , vimarśa eva ca kriyeti / na ca jñānaśaktivihīnasya kriyāyogaḥ iti / tadetadaviyuktajñānakriyārūpaṃ kriyādvāreṇa sakalatattvarāśigatasṛṣṭisaṃhāraśatapratibimbasahiṣṇu yat tadupadeśabhāvanādiṣu tathābhāsamānamanābhāsamapi vastutaḥ śivatattvamityuktaṃ bhavati //1//
children.translated_text: 'Thus' — since the cause-and-effect relation as stated by other systems, resting on the nature of the insentient, is in no way tenable; but rather, existing in the consciousness-form alone, abiding as internal and external, with a body that is of the ultimate reality of luminosity, occurring in the form of such manifestation, attracting the sequence of time — it is called action; and that is the property of the perceiver alone, who is of the body of <s>jñāna-śakti</s> (power of knowledge). Therefore, knowledge and action are inseparable. Knowledge is animated by reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), and reflective awareness itself is action. And without the power of knowledge, the conjunction with action is not possible. This very thing — of the form of inseparable knowledge and action — through the medium of action, capable of bearing hundreds of reflections of creation and dissolution occurring in the entire mass of principles — that which, in instruction, contemplation, and such, though manifesting as such, is in reality even non-manifesting — is stated to be the <s>Śiva-tattva</s> (Śiva principle). // 1 //

children.text: nanyevaṃbhūtaṃ śivatattvaṃ cet tarhi tato'natiricyamānamidaṃ viśvamiti kimanyat tattvaṃ syāt / ekacittattvaviśrāntau ca tattvānāṃ kathaṃ kramo bhavet , deśakālābhedāt ? evametat
children.translated_text: Objection: If the <s>Śiva-tattva</s> is of such a nature, then this universe, not being different from it, would not be another principle. And if all principles rest in one consciousness-principle, how could there be a sequence of principles, given the non-difference of space and time? That is indeed so —
However, due to the predominance of the internal condition, the principle called <s>Sadākhya</s> (the 'Existent-named') comes first;
and when there is predominance of the external state, the <s>Pārameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord principle) comes after.

children.text: yadyapyekameva śivatattvaṃ tathāpi tadīyameva svātaṃtryaṃ svātmani svarūpabhedaṃ tāvatpratibimbakalpatayā darśayati / svarūpavaicitryameva deśakālakramaḥ / mūritikriyāvaicitryamayo hi asau / tataścāntarī jñānarūpā yā daśā tasyā udrekābhāsane

children.translated_text: 'Sadākhya' —

children.text: sadākhyāyāṃ bhavam / yataḥ prabhṛti saditi prakhyā / sadākhyāyāśca sadāśivaśabdarūpāyā idaṃ vācyaṃ tattvam / sṛṣṭikramopadeśādau prathamamucitam / tatsādākhyaṃ tattvam /
children.translated_text: belonging to the <s>Sadākhyā</s> (the stage of the 'Existent'). From which [stage] the designation 'Sat' (Existent) [begins]. And the principle denoted by the word <s>Sadākhyā</s>, whose verbal form is <s>Sadāśiva</s> — this is the principle. It is appropriate to mention first in the order of instruction regarding creation. That is the <s>Sādākhya-tattva</s> (principle of the Existent).
'Of the external state' —
consisting of <s>kriyā-śakti</s> (power of action),
'when there is predominance' —
when there is the predominance of manifestation,
'Pārameśvara' —

children.text: parameśvaraśabdavācyamīśvaratattvaṃ nāma / tacca sādākhyasya pañcāducitāvabhāsanam / etaduktaṃ bhavati / iha tasya bhāvastattvam , ---- iti bhinnānāṃ vargāṇāṃ vargīkaraṇanimittaṃ yadekamavibhaktaṃ bhāti tattattvam / yathā girivṛkṣapuraprabhṛtīnāṃ nadīsaraḥsāgarādīnāṃ ca pṛthivīrūpatvamabrūpatvaṃ ceti / tataśca śuddhacaitanyavargo yo mantramaheśvarākhyaḥ , tasya prathamasṛṣṭāvasmākamantaḥkaraṇaikavedyamiva dhyāmalaprāyamunmīlitamātracitrakalpaṃ yadbhāvacakram , tathā saṃhāre ca dhvaṃsonmukhatayā tathābhūtameva cakāsti pratibimbaprāyatayā , tasya caitanyavargasya tādṛśi bhāvarāśau tathāpravanaṃ nāma yaccidviśeṣatvaṃ tatsadāśivatattvam / mantreśvarādirūpasya tu caitanyarāśeḥ sphuṭībhūtamasmadbahiśkaraṇasaraṇisaṃprāptabhāvavargapratimaṃ viśvaṃ pratibimbakalpatayā bhāti , tasya tu tat tathāprathanamīśvaratattvam / yastu sadāśivabhaṭṭāraka īśvarabhaṭṭārakaśca dhveyopāsyādirūpatayā sa brahmaviṣṇutulyaḥ pṛthageva mantavyo na tu nāmasārūpyāt bhramitavyam / yathāhureke
children.translated_text: the principle called <s>Īśvara</s>, denoted by the word <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord). And that is the fifth appropriate manifestation of the <s>Sādākhya</s>. What is being said is this: here, the 'principle' (<s>tattva</s>) of an entity means that one undivided [factor] that is the ground of classification of the different groups, which appears as one. Just as the earth-nature is the [principle] of mountains, trees, cities, and such, and the water-nature of rivers, lakes, oceans, and such. Therefore, the group of pure consciousness called <s>Mantra-Maheśvara</s> — at its initial creation, the circle of entities [manifesting] as cognizable by our internal organ alone, predominantly dim, merely opened out, resembling a variegated painting — and likewise in dissolution, facing destruction, appearing in just such a form, like a reflection — the specific consciousness-nature that is thus inclined in such a mass of entities belonging to that consciousness-group — that is the <s>Sadāśiva-tattva</s>. But for the consciousness-mass of the form of <s>Mantreśvara</s> and such, the universe appears as a reflection, having become distinct, resembling the class of entities that have reached the path of our external senses. The principle that is the spreading-forth of that [consciousness-mass] in that manner is the <s>Īśvara-tattva</s>. But the Lord <s>Sadāśiva</s> and the Lord <s>Īśvara</s> — in the form of the worshipped deity and such — they are like <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to be considered as entirely separate; one should not be confused by the similarity of names. As some say:

children.text: brahmaviṣṇurudrā api tattvamadhye kiṃ na gaṇitāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Why are <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Rudra</s> not counted among the principles?' —
thus. // 2 //

Although the <s>Śiva-tattva</s> is indeed one, nevertheless its very freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>) displays in its own Self a difference of its own nature, in the manner of reflections. The variety of its own nature is itself the sequence of space and time. For that [sequence] consists of the variety of form and activity. Therefore, when there is the predominance of the manifestation of the internal condition, which is of the nature of knowledge —
He shows another designation for this pair of principles:
<s>Īśvara</s> is the external opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>); the internal closing (<s>nimeṣa</s>) is <s>Sadāśiva</s>;
and the co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) [of the two] is <s>Sadvidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge), [being] of the cognitions 'I' and 'this.'

children.text: yasyonmeṣāṭudayo jagataḥ , ityatra īśvaratattvamevonmeṣaśabdenoktam , viśvasya hi sphuṭatvabāhyatvamunmeṣaṇam , nimeṣaṇaṃ tvapshuṭatvāpādanamahantārūpatodrecanam , iti nimeṣaḥ sadāśivatattvam / yato jagataḥ pralaya iti / śuddho'yaṃ spandaḥ parameśvarasyācalasyāpyaprarūḍharūpāntarāpattilakṣaṇaḥ kiṃciccalanātmatayā sphuradrūpatvāt / parameśvarasya hi paramārthata etāḥ śaktayo yastattvagrāmaḥ , kācittu śaktiranyabahutaraśaktikroḍīkāraṃ kurvatī nikaṭatvādupāsyā ghaṭasyeva ghaṭatvātmikā , kācidanyāpekṣiṇī svarūpamātraniṣṭhā dūrā ghaṭasyeva sattāsmikā / evaṃ nimeṣonmeṣaśaktī eva sadāśiveśvarau tayostvadhiṣṭhātṛdevate api tathānāme //
children.translated_text: In 'whose opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>) is the arising of the world,' the <s>Īśvara</s>-principle itself is denoted by the word '<s>unmeṣa</s>' (opening). For the becoming-manifest and becoming-external of the universe is '<s>unmeṣaṇa</s>' (opening of the eyes); '<s>nimeṣaṇa</s>' (closing of the eyes), however, is the rendering-non-manifest, the absorption into the form of the Great Self — thus '<s>nimeṣa</s>' is the <s>Sadāśiva</s>-principle. Because 'from whom is the dissolution of the world.' This pure <s>spanda</s> (vibration) of the Supreme Lord, even though He is motionless, has the character of a slight movement in the form of not-fully-developed assumption of another form, because it has the nature of shining forth. For of the Supreme Lord, these powers — which constitute the group of principles — are in the ultimate sense [His own]; but a certain power, by virtue of encompassing many other powers within itself, is, due to its proximity, to be contemplated — like 'pot-ness' for a pot; while another, depending on [further] others, abiding in mere own-nature, is remote — like 'existence' for a pot. Thus, the powers of <s>nimeṣa</s> (closing) and <s>unmeṣa</s> (opening) are indeed the <s>Sadāśiva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> [principles]; and their presiding deities too are of the same name. //

children.text: atha tadadhiṣṭhātṛdvayagataṃ karaṇaṃ vidyātattvamāha / prakāśasya yadātmamātraviśramaṇamananyonmukhasvātmaprakāśatāviśrāntilakṣaṇo vimarśaḥ so'ham iti ucyate / yastvanyonmukhaḥ sa

children.translated_text: '<s>idam</s>' (this).

children.text: iti / sa ca svaprakāśamātre punarananyonmukharūpe viśrāmyati paramārthataḥ / tatrādye vimarśaṃ śivatattvam dvitīye vidyeśatā madhyate tu rūpe
children.translated_text: And that [outward-directed awareness], in ultimate reality, rests upon mere self-luminosity, which is of the form not-directed-toward-another. In the first [case], the reflective awareness is the <s>Śiva</s>-principle; in the second, it is the <s>Vidyā-Īśvara</s> state; but in the intermediate form,
'<s>aham-idam</s>' (I-this)

'<s>aham</s>' (I)
and
'<s>idam</s>' (this)
— [as] cognitions: in the <s>Māyā</s>-perceiver, they have separate substrata —
'<s>aham</s>' (I)
in the grasper,
'<s>idam</s>' (this)

children.text: iti ca grāhye , tannirāsenaikasminnevādhikaraṇe yatsaṃgamanaṃ saṃbandharūpaṃ prathanaṃ tat satī śuddhā vidyā , aśuddhavidyāto māyāpramātṛgatāyā anyaiva / tatra yadā
children.translated_text: in the grasped. The negation of that [separation], the coming together in a single substratum — that manifestation in the form of relation — that is pure <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge), altogether different from impure <s>vidyā</s> which belongs to the <s>Māyā</s>-perceiver. Therein, when
'<s>aham</s>' (I) —

children.text: ityasya yadadhikaraaṇaṃ cinmātrarūpaṃ tatraivedamaṃśamullāsayati tadā tasyāsphuṭatvāt sadāśivatā
children.translated_text: that whose substratum is of the form of pure consciousness alone — causes the '<s>idam</s>' (this)-aspect to shine forth within that very [substratum], then, because of the non-manifestness of that [idam-aspect], it is the <s>Sadāśiva</s>-state —
'<s>aham-idam</s>' (I-this).'
Thus.
'<s>Idam-aham</s>' (this-I),'

children.text: iti tu idamityaṃśe sphuṭībhūte 'dhikaraṇe yadāhamaṃśavimarśaṃ niṣiñcati tadeśvaratā , ---- iti vibhāgaḥ //3//

children.text: apūrṇatvamanyāpekṣitedamiti / atra ca tattvadvaye bhāvānāṃ dhyāmalādhyāmalarūpāṇāmubhayāṃśasparśāt parāparatvamiti / vedyabhāvaniṣṭhā daśā tattvasvarūpā tadavabhāsayitṛmantreśvarādiśuddhapramātṛsaṃvedyavastusārā / yā tu tanniṣṭhasaṃvedanadaśā sā śuddhā vidyā , tatpramātradhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ śrīsadāśiveśvarabhaṭṭārakarūpatā iti sakṣepaḥ //5//

The state abiding in the knowable-entity is the nature of the principle; the deities who illuminate it — <s>Mantreśvara</s> and other pure perceivers — are the essential reality of the objects cognized [by them]. children.text: ityācchādako yo bhāgaḥ tatprathāpradhānā śuddhavidyā / anye tu manyante , ---- yo 'sāvidaṃbhāga ācchādanīyastasya yadavabhāsanaṃ tatpradhānā śuddhavidyā / anyathā hi sa idamaṃśaḥ kena bhāsyatāṃ māyāyāstatrābhāvāt bhāve vā prarohaprasaṅgāt ; ata eveyaṃ prarohāsahiṣṇuṃ yata idantāṃ bhāsayati tataḥ śuddhā / bhāsanācca vidyeti / tata evāpraruḍhamāyākalpatvāt mahāmāyeyaṃ śrīrauravādigurubhirupadiṣṭā , tadetadāha /
children.translated_text: the aspect that covers [the idam] — pure <s>Vidyā</s> has the predominance of the manifestation of that [aham-aspect]. Others, however, maintain: ---- the '<s>idam</s>'-aspect which is to be covered — pure <s>Vidyā</s> has the predominance of the manifestation of that [idam-aspect]. For otherwise, by what would that '<s>idam</s>'-aspect be illuminated? — since <s>Māyā</s> is absent there; or if present, there would be the unwanted consequence of its growth. Hence, because it illuminates the 'this'-ness without [allowing] growth, it is 'pure.' And because it is illumination, it is '<s>vidyā</s>' (knowledge). For that very reason, because it is of the nature of <s>Māyā</s> that has not [yet] grown, it has been taught by the venerable gurus of the <s>Raurava</s> and other [āgamas] as <s>Mahāmāyā</s> (the Great Māyā). He states this:
Thus, in the view of some:
The very cognition of difference in entities, which belongs to the agent who is also of the nature of awareness —
That, say others, is <s>Vidyā</s>, [operating] through <s>Māyā</s>-power — as the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> (Lords of Knowledge) [demonstrate].

children.text: māyāpramātari śūnyādirūpe 'pyanullasite , cinmātra eva pramātari kartari ca sati cidekarūpaṣvapi bhāveṣu yadacidrūpatayā bhedaprakāśanalakṣaṇaṃ svātantryaṃ sā śuddhavidyā māyāśaktyā tulyā , vedyabhāge bhedaprakāśanāt / na ca māyaiva , grāhakasya cinmātrabhāge tāvadaviparyāsanāt , yena prakāreṇa vidyeśvarā bhagavanto 'nantādyā vatante / te hi śuddhacinmātragṛhītāhaṃ bhāvāḥ svatastu bhinnaṃ vedyaṃ paśyanti , yathā dvaitavādināmīśvaraḥ / evaṃ grāhake'ṃśataścaitanyarūpāt paramārtharūpe grāhyaviparyāsanaśaktiḥ śuddhavidyā vidyeśvarāṇām //6//
children.translated_text: In the <s>Māyā</s>-perceiver — even though the form of void etc. has not been dissolved — in the perceiver who is of the nature of pure consciousness alone, and who is an agent, even in the entities that are of a single consciousness-form, the sovereignty (<s>svātantrya</s>) characterized by the manifestation of difference as non-consciousness — that is pure <s>Vidyā</s>, comparable to <s>Māyā</s>-power, because of manifesting difference in the knowable aspect. Yet it is not <s>Māyā</s> itself, because in the grasper-aspect of pure consciousness there is at least no distortion — in the manner in which the blessed <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>, <s>Ananta</s> and others, exist. For they, whose 'I'-nature is grasped as pure consciousness alone, perceive the knowable as different by their own nature — like the God of the dualists. Thus, in the grasper-aspect, [which is] partially of consciousness-form and of ultimate nature, the power of distortion with respect to the grasped is pure <s>Vidyā</s>, belonging to the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>. //6//

children.text: pare prāhuḥ ---- bhagavataḥ pramaśivasyāprarūḍhabhedāvabhāsanaṃ sadāśiveśvaratā / tatrāsphuṭe bhede icchāśaktirīśvarasya vyāpriyate , sphuṭatve jñānaśaktiḥ , grāhyagrāhakaviparyāsadvayaprarūḍhau tu māyāśaktiḥ , sā ca paśupramātṛṣu , grāhakagrāhyobhayaviparyāsasaṃskāre tu avinivṛtte'pi yadetat vastuparamārthaprathanaṃ tatra vidyāśaktivyāpāro yogijñāniprabhṛtiṣvapaśupramātṛṣu / tadetaddarśayati /
children.translated_text: Others say: ---- The non-fully-developed manifestation of difference of the Blessed Supreme <s>Śiva</s> is the <s>Sadāśiva</s>-<s>Īśvara</s> state. Therein, when difference is non-manifest, <s>Icchā-śakti</s> (the power of will) of <s>Īśvara</s> operates; when manifest, <s>Jñāna-śakti</s> (the power of knowledge) [operates]. But when the double distortion of grasped and grasper has fully developed, it is <s>Māyā-śakti</s> (the power of illusion) — and that pertains to bound-soul perceivers. But when the impression of the double distortion of grasper and grasped has not ceased, yet there is this manifestation of things as they ultimately are — there the operation of <s>Vidyā-śakti</s> (the power of knowledge) [occurs], in <s>yogins</s>, <s>jñānins</s>, and other non-bound-soul perceivers. He shows this:
Of that [Lord] whose nature is sovereignty, the <s>Vidyā-śakti</s> (power of knowledge) is that which illuminates
In the state of the bound soul ...... //
'In the state of the bound soul' —

children.text: viparyāsaikarasatvalakṣaṇe pāśanīyatve 'svataṃtratve dṛśyadraṣṭṭadarśanabhede satyapi jāte pūrvoktayuktibalena yadetadaiśvaryamuktaṃ tasya yā prakāśikā parameśvaraśaktiḥ ---- yadvaśāt kecideva tā yuktīrādṛtya tadā śvastahṛdayāḥ kṛtino bhavanti ---- sā vidyāśaktiḥ / ayameva ṣaḍardhasārādidṛṣṭo'pyasyācāryasya hṛdayamāvarjayati pakṣaḥ ,

This is the very position that captivates the heart of this master [<s>Abhinavagupta</s>], as found in the <s>Ṣaḍardhasāra</s> and other [texts],

children.text: māyāśaktiḥ punaracidrūpe śūnyādau pramātṛtābhimānaṃ prarūḍhaṃ dadhrtā bhāvānapi cinmayān bhedenābhimānayantī sarvathaiva svarūpaṃ tirodhatte āvṛṇute vimohinī sā / tirodhānamatra na vilayanarūpaṃ mantavyaṃ , yat kṛtyapañcakamadhya āgameṣu gaṇyate , dīkṣitasyāpi gurumantrādinindanaprāyamapi tvāvaraṇameva //7//
children.translated_text: <s>Māyā-śakti</s> (the power of illusion), establishing the fully-developed sense of perceiver-hood in the non-conscious form of void etc., and causing even the consciousness-natured entities to be identified with difference — in every way conceals, covers over the true nature. She is the deluder. '<s>Tirodhāna</s>' (concealment) here should not be understood as dissolution, which is counted among the five acts (<s>kṛtyapañcaka</s>) in the <s>āgamas</s>; rather, it is indeed <s>āvaraṇa</s> (veiling) — which, even for the initiated (<s>dīkṣita</s>), mostly takes the form of disparaging the guru, <s>mantra</s>, and such. //7//
He clarifies that <s>tirodhāna</s> (concealment) is of the nature of veiling:
When difference alone shines as a single savour, and the non-Self is perceived with 'I'-ness —
In the void, in the intellect, or in the body — <s>Māyā-śakti</s> unfolds.

children.text: ityātmatvena vīkṣyate ; ucchvasananiḥśvasanādau vā prāṇa eva tejaḥsamupavṛṃhitaḥ , svacchodakāśayakalpā vedyapratibimbanavatī vā buddhirabhiniviśyate antarahaṃ vedmi duḥkhyahamiti cintādyavasthāsu , śarīrameva tu pṛthivīprāyaṃ kṛśo'hamityādidaśāsu ahamityātmatayā bhāti / sarvameva cedaṃ śūnyādi vastutaścinmātrasārameva māyayaiva tāvadacidrūpatayā bhāsitam / tathāvidhameva tu sat ahamiti saṃvidrūpatābhiniveśasthānaṃ saṃpāditamapraśāntajaḍabhāvameva iti atiduṣkaravastusaṃpādanāpratīghātarūpā parameśvarasya māyāśaktiḥ , ---- ityetat
children.translated_text: '<s>aham</s>' (I) — as the Self. Or <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) alone, in [activities such as] exhalation and inhalation, nourished by <s>tejas</s> (fire-element); or the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), like a pool of clear water capable of reflecting the knowable, is entered into in states of thought etc. [such as] 'internally I know,' 'I suffer'; but the body, which is predominantly earth, in states like 'I am thin' — shines as 'I,' as the Self. And all this — void and the rest — is in reality of the essence of pure consciousness alone; it is by <s>Māyā</s> alone that it has been first made to appear as non-conscious. And being of such [non-conscious] nature, it has been made a locus of the insistence on consciousness-nature as 'I' — [yet] without the inert nature having been dispelled. Thus, [this is] the <s>Māyā-śakti</s> of the Supreme Lord, whose nature is the irresistible accomplishment of an extremely difficult thing — this is what is shown
by the word '<s>vijṛmbhate</s>' (unfolds).
He also indicates that even external things — son, wealth, wife, and such — are included as objects of the insistence on 'I'-ness. //8//

children.text: nanvacidrūpatvādanātmā yadi śūnyādistadātmatayāsau abhiniviśyamānaścidrūpa eva , ---- iti sarvajñatvasarvakartṛtvādiviśuddhaiśvaryadharmaiva syāt , ---- ityāśaṅkyāha
children.translated_text: Objection: If the void etc. is non-Self because of being non-conscious, then when it is identified as the Self, it would be of the nature of consciousness alone — and thus one would possess the pure sovereign qualities of omniscience, omnipotence, and so forth. Anticipating this, he says:

children.text: yaś ca pramātā śūnyādiḥ prameye vyatirekiṇi /
children.translated_text: And whatever perceiver — [identifying with] void etc. — in relation to a knowable that is different [from himself],
That perceiver, being himself a knowable, is enveloped by the group of five [beginning with] <s>Kāla</s> (time).

children.text: syādaiśvaryadharmayogaḥ śūnyādeḥ yadyahamityabhiniviśyamāno'pi meyatāṃ jahyāt / tathāhi sati prameyamapyasya nīlādivyatiriktatayā naiva bhāseta / yāvatā yaḥ śūnyādiḥ pramātā kathitaḥ , sa yāvadeva svarūpādvyatirekābhimate nīlādau prameye pramātā tāvadeva svayamapi meyabhūtaḥ eva san mātā / meyaṃ hi mīyamānatvādeva parimitam , ---- iti tādṛśādeva meyāntarādupapannavyatirekam , na tvevaṃ cidrūpamaparimitatvāt / parimitatvaṃ ca śūnyāderahaṃbhāvasya yat tadeva kālādipañcakam . tathā hi kālaḥ kramamāsūtrayan pramātari vijṛmbhamāṇastadanusāreṇa prameye 'pi prasarati , yo'haṃ kṛśo'bhavaṃ sa sthūlo varte bhaviṣyāmi sthūlataraḥ ityevamātmānaṃ deharūpaṃ kramavantamiva parāmṛśaṃstatsahacāriṇi prameye'pi bhūtādirūpaṃ kramaṃ prakāśayati / asya śūnyāderjaḍasya vidyā kiṃcijjhatvonmīlanarūpā buddhidarpaṇasaṃkrāntaṃ bhāvarāśiṃ nīlasukhādiṃ vivinakti / kalā kiṃcitkartṛtvopodvalanamayī kāryamudbhāvayati , kiṃcijjānāmi / kiṃcitkaromi , ---- iti / atra cāṃśe tukye'pi kiṃcittve kasmādidameva kiṃcit , ---- ityatrārthe'bhiṣvaṅgarūpaḥ pramātari dehādau prameye ca guṇādyāropaṇamaya iva rāgo vyāpriyate / na ca tadbuddhigatamavairāgyameva , taddhi sthūlaṃ vṛddhasya pramadāyāṃ na bhavedapi , rāgastu bhavatyeva / buddhidharmāṣṭake'pi ca dṛṣṭo'bhiṣvaṅgaḥ / atraiva kasmādabhiṣvaṅga ---- ityayamartho niyatyā niyamyate iti / evaṃ kalāvidyākālarāganiyatibhirotaproto māyayāpahṛtaiśvaryasarvasvaḥ san punarapi prativitīrṇatatsarvasvarāśimadhyagatabhāgamātra evaṃbhūto'yaṃ mitaḥ pramātā bhāti ---- idānīmidaṃ kiṃcijjānānaḥ , idaṃ kurvāṇo'tra rakto'traiva ca yaḥ so 'ham ---- iti / eṣāṃ ca bhinnaviṣayatvamapi bhavati kadācit , yathānyatra rakto'pi niyatyānyat kāryate iti / ete ca pramātṛlagnatathaiva bhānti , ---- iti tasyaiva śaktirūpāḥ pratipramātṛbhinnā eṣa , kadācit tu naṭamallaprekṣādāvīśvarecchayā ekībhaveyurapi / na hyeteṣāmīśvarecchātiriktaṃ nijaṃ kimapi jīvitamasti , ---- ityasakṛduktaṃ vakṣyate ca //9//
children.translated_text: Objection: Let there be the connection with the property of sovereignty for the void and such [perceivers]; [but] if, even while identifying with 'I,' [the void-perceiver] were to abandon the status of being knowable — then, in that case, the knowable (<s>prameya</s>) too would not appear at all as different from blue and such. Inasmuch as the perceiver described as the void and such — to the very extent that he is a perceiver with respect to the knowable such as blue, which is considered different from his own nature — to that very extent, he himself, being an object (<s>meya</s>), is [also] a knower. For the knowable, precisely because it is being measured (<s>mīyamāna</s>), is limited — thus it has a demonstrated distinction from other knowables of just such a kind, but the consciousness-form is not so, because of its unlimitedness. And the limitedness of the void and such, of the I-sense — that itself is the pentad of <s>kāla</s> (time) and such. Thus: <s>kāla</s> (time), unfolding succession in the perceiver, extends in accordance with that into the knowable as well — 'I who was thin, am now stout, and shall become stouter' — thus, reflectively grasping oneself in the form of the body as if possessing succession, one manifests in the co-existing knowable also a succession in the form of past and such. For this void-perceiver, who is insentient, <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) — whose nature is the slight opening of insentience — discriminates the mass of entities such as blue, pleasure, and such that have entered into the mirror of intellect (<s>buddhi</s>). <s>Kalā</s> — consisting of the slight augmentation of agency — brings forth the effect: 'I know something; I do something' — thus. And in this aspect, even in the universal 'something-ness,' [the question arises:] why is it this particular 'something' and not another? — in this regard, <s>rāga</s> (attachment), whose nature is passionate clinging, operates in the perceiver as if superimposing qualities and such upon the body and such knowable — it is active. And that is not merely the lack of dispassion residing in the intellect; for that [lack of dispassion], being gross, might not arise in an old person toward a woman, yet <s>rāga</s> indeed arises. And in the eightfold properties of the intellect too, attachment is observed. 'Why attachment to just this?' — this meaning is regulated by <s>niyati</s> (regulation). Thus, being woven through and through by <s>kalā</s>, <s>vidyā</s>, <s>kāla</s>, <s>rāga</s>, and <s>niyati</s>, having had the entirety of sovereignty stolen by <s>Māyā</s>, and yet being merely a portion within the distributed mass of that entire sovereign wealth — such a limited perceiver shines in this form: 'Now knowing this something, doing this, attached here, and who is here — that am I.' And these [limiting factors] sometimes have different domains, as when one, though attached elsewhere, is caused by <s>niyati</s> to act on something else. And these shine in just that way as attached to each perceiver — thus they are of the nature of His powers, different for each perceiver. But sometimes, by the will of the Lord, in spectacles of actors and wrestlers and such, they may even become unified. For these [powers] have no life of their own apart from the will of the Lord — this has been stated repeatedly and will be stated [again]. // 9 //

children.text: yaduktamidamityatra prameye vyatirekiṇi mātā , ---- iti tatra tatprameyaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: What was said — that in the knowable, which is different, the perceiver is 'this' — regarding that, he shows the knowable:
The knowable is of twenty-three kinds, being of the nature of effects and instruments;
of that, the one whose form is non-differentiation is <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), the root cause. //

children.text: yat kāryakaraṇarūpaṃ trayoviṃśatiprakāraṃ yacca tasya mūlabhūtaṃ kāraṇaṃ sarvakāryakaraṇāvibhāgarūpaṃ pradhānaṃ nāma tatsarvaṃ meyam ---- iti sambandhaḥ / yogimantratadīśvaraprabhṛtīnāṃ hi bhūtatanmātrakaraṇapradhānavaśīkārayogitvātsarvameva prameyam / saṃsāriṇāmapyanumānāgamādidiśā prameyameva , itīyat prameyam / kālādayastu prameyā api pramāryeva lagnāḥ , ---- iti pramātṛśaktisvabhāvatvāt na prameyatvenehāvasare māyāpramātṛcyatiriktaprameyaprastāve gaṇitāḥ / vastuto hi atratyo'yaṃ pramātāpi prameya eva , sa tu pramātrīkriyamāṇa ācchāditaprameyatāka ihocyate //10//
children.translated_text: That which is of the form of effects and instruments, of twenty-three kinds, and that which is its root cause, whose form is the non-differentiation of all effects and instruments, called <s>Pradhāna</s> — all that is the knowable — this is the connection. For <s>yogins</s>, <s>mantras</s>, their lords (<s>Īśvaras</s>), and the rest, since they have mastery over elements, subtle elements, instruments, and <s>Pradhāna</s>, everything is indeed knowable. For worldly beings (<s>saṃsārins</s>) too, through inference, scripture, and such directions, it is indeed knowable — to this extent is the knowable. But <s>kāla</s> and such, though knowable, are attached to the perceiver alone — thus, being of the nature of the perceiver's powers, they are not counted here as knowable in this context of the presentation of the knowable that is other than the <s>Māyā</s>-perceiver. In truth, this perceiver too is indeed a knowable, but he, being made into a perceiver, is spoken of here as one whose knowability has been concealed. // 10 //

children.text: nanvatra trayoviṃśatau kiṃ kāryaṃ kiṃ karaṇam ? ityāśaṅkyāha
children.translated_text: Objection: In this [scheme of] twenty-three, what is the effect and what is the instrument? Anticipating this, he says:
And here, the series of external and internal instruments is of thirteen kinds;
and the group of effects is of ten kinds, through the distinction of gross and subtle. //

children.text: pramātuḥ pūrvaṃ karaṇopayogaḥ , ---- ityatrādau trayodaśa karaṇāniḥ tatra buddhirapyavasāyasāmānyamātrarūpā , grāhyagrāhakābhimānarūpo'haṃkāraḥ , saṃkalpādikāraṇaṃ manaḥ , ---- ityantaḥkaraṇaṃ tridhā / buddhau śabdādyadhyavasāyarūpāyāmupayogīni buddhīdntriyāṇi pañca ---- śrotraṃ , tvak , cakṣuḥ , jihvā , dhrāṇam , ---- iti / karmaṇi tūpayogīni pañca karmendriyāṇi / tathā hi ---- tyāgo grahaṇamiti dvayam , ---- bahirviṣayaḥ yat tatra pāṇiḥ pāyuḥ pādaḥ , ---- iti karaṇāni / etadevāntāḥ prāṇe yena kriyate tadvāgīndriyam / tatprakṣobhapraśāntyā viśrāntikriyopayogī upasthaḥ / sarvadehavyāpakāni ca karmendriyāṇyahaṅkāraviśeṣātmakāni / tena cchinnahasto bāhubhyāmādadānaḥ pāṇinaivādatte , evamanyat / kevalaṃ tattatsphuṭapūrṇavṛttilābhasthānatvāt pañcāṅgulirūpamadhiṣṭhānamasyaucyate , ---- ityevaṃ karaṇāni trayodaśa / eṣāṃ ca kāryatve 'apyasādhāraṇena karaṇatvena vyapadeśaḥ / sthūlaṃ kāryaṃ pṛthivī , āpaḥ , tejo , vāyuḥ , nabhaḥ , ---- iti pañca bhūtāni / sūkṣmameṣāmeva rūpaṃ , gandho , raso , rūpaṃ , sparśaḥ , śabdaḥ , ---- iti / tatraikaikaguṇamākāśādi , ekaikavṛddhaguṇaṃ vā , ---- iti darśanabhedaḥ , ---- iti na vivecito , nupayogāt / tatra sthūlaṃ vibhaktamavibhāgasvānumāpakam , ---- iti sthūlarūpopakramamuktam / atra pṛthivyādyābhāsā eva miśrībhūya ghaṭādisvalakṣaṇībhūtāḥ karmendriyairupasarpitāḥ , buddhīndriyairālocitāḥ , antaḥkaraṇena saṃkalpitābhimataniścitarūpāḥ , vidyayā vivevitāḥ, kalādibhiranurañjitāḥ , pramātari viśrāmyanti , ---- iti tātparyam / etacca vistaratastatpradhāneṣu tantrālokasārādiṣu mayā nirṇītam , ---- itīhānupayogānna vitānitam , ---- iti śivam //11//
children.translated_text: The use of instruments comes first for the perceiver — thus, here first the thirteen instruments: therein, <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) too, whose form is merely the generality of determination; <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), whose form is the self-arrogation of the grasped and the grasper; <s>manas</s> (mind), which is the instrument of intention and such — thus the internal instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is threefold. Useful in the <s>buddhi</s>, which is of the form of the determination of sound and such, are the five cognitive sense-faculties (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>) — hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell. But useful in action are the five action sense-faculties (<s>karmendriyāṇi</s>). Thus: giving up and grasping — these are two [functions]; the external object, in which [they operate] — there the hand, the organ of excretion, the feet — these are the instruments. That which is the inner boundary of these in <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), by which [action] is performed — that is the organ of speech. That which is useful for the activity of rest through the agitation and calming of that [prāṇa] is the generative organ. And the action sense-faculties pervade the entire body, being of the nature of specifications of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego). Therefore, one whose hands are cut off grasps with the arms — by the hand itself he grasps; similarly for the others. It is only because [each organ] is the locus of obtaining the distinct and complete operation of that particular [function] that the five-fingered form is called its seat — thus the instruments are thirteen. And though they are also effects, they are designated as instruments by virtue of their distinctive function as instruments. The gross effect is fivefold: earth, water, fire, air, and space — the five elements. Their subtle form [consists of] smell, taste, color, touch, and sound. Therein, whether each [element] from space onward has one quality [each], or each has one additional quality [in succession] — this is a difference of views and is not analyzed here, as it is not useful [for the present discussion]. There, the gross [universe] was said to have been stated beginning with the gross form: 'the gross is differentiated, [yet] indicative of its own non-differentiated [source] through inference.' Here, the appearances of earth and such, having been mixed together and become the specific forms (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) of pots and such, approached by the action sense-faculties, perceived by the cognitive sense-faculties, made into objects of intention, self-arrogation, and determination by the internal instrument, discriminated by <s>vidyā</s>, colored by <s>kalā</s> and such — they come to rest in the perceiver. This is the purport. And this has been determined by me at length in those [works] principally devoted to this topic, such as the <s>Tantrālokasāra</s> and such — therefore it is not elaborated here, as it is not useful [in this context]. May there be auspiciousness! // 11 //

Thus ends the first daily lesson, entitled 'Determination of Principles' (<s>Tattvanirūpaṇa</s>), in the Scripture Section (<s>Āgamādhikāra</s>) of the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s> composed by the venerable master <s>Utpaladeva</s>, accompanied by the commentary called <s>Vimarśinī</s> composed by the venerable master <s>Abhinavagupta</s>. // 1 //
In the Scripture Section (<s>Āgamādhikāra</s>), the second daily lesson.
<s>Vimarśinī</s>
{He whose essential nature is unbroken, yet who displays variegated perceiver-constructions
upon the circle of His own golden orb — Him, <s>Śiva</s>, we praise! //}

children.text: evaṃ tattvarāśau nirṇīte etadantarbhāvenoltamapi mukhyatayā nirṇetavyaṃ pramātṛtattvaṃ vitatya nirṇetuṃ

children.translated_text: 'Therein, the mere perceiver-hood' —
beginning with this,
'<s>Vyāna</s>, of universal nature, is supreme' —

children.text: ityantairviṃśatiślokairāhnikāntaraṃ prastūyate / tathāhi ---- pramāturatra svarūpapratyabhijñānamupadiśyate śāstre / sa hi heyamupādeyaṃ ca svaṃ svabhāvaṃ vidvān paramopādeyarūpaṃ śivasvabhāvaṃ svātmānamabhedenāviśan jīvanneva mukto bhavati , ---- iti / tatra ślokena brahmāditrayasvarūpam , tatkataṃ ca pramātṛbhedaṃ ślokasaptakena , dvayena samāveśasvarūpam , ślokapañcakena pramātureva suṣuptādyavasthāḥ , trayeṇa tāsāṃ heyopādeyavibhāgaṃ nirūpayati , ---- ityāhnikatātparyam / granthārthastu nirūpyate //
children.translated_text: ending with this — through twenty verses, a new daily lesson is commenced. Thus: in this scripture, the recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) of one's own essential nature is being taught to the perceiver. For he, knowing the to-be-rejected and the to-be-adopted as his own nature, entering into his supreme, most-to-be-adopted nature which is the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, entering non-differently into his own Self — becomes liberated even while alive (<s>jīvanmukta</s>). Therein, by one verse the nature of the triad beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, by a group of seven verses the distinction of perceivers caused by that, by two [verses] the nature of <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption), by a group of five verses the states of the perceiver such as deep sleep and such, by three [verses] the distinction of what is to be rejected and what is to be adopted regarding those [states] — [these] he determines. This is the purport of the daily lesson. The meaning of the text is now determined:

Thus, the mass of principles having been determined, the perceiver-principle (<s>pramātṛ-tattva</s>) too, which is to be determined primarily though subsumed under these — in order to determine it at length,
Therein, when abiding in mere perceiver-hood, <s>Rudra</s> is the presiding deity;
in the spreading forth of differentiated knowables, <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> are established. //

children.text: tatreti , evaṃbhūte 'sminnāgamasiddhe yuktyanugate ca tattvasvarūpe sati yadetat kālādipañcakaveṣṭitaṃ pramātṛtārūpam , tadeva yasyāṃ śuddhamupasaṃhṛtaprameyajātaṃ bhavati daśāyāṃ saṃhārākhyāyāṃ tasyāmadhiṣṭhātṛdevatātvaṃ taddaśāsaṃpādanena svopāsakalokasya taddaśādhyānāveśasamāpannasya svābhimukhyasaṃpādanena ca bhajamāno bhaṭṭāraka īśvara eva rudro bhagavān , yo māyāpade 'pi prāṇāpānātmakadharmādharmasūryendudinaniśādivimuktamadhyamajyotīrūpapramātṛsvarūpasparśād unmīlitatṛtīyanetraḥ / bhinnasya tu prameye tatsaṃtānapravahaṇalakṣaṇe prasare 'dhiṣṭhātṛdevatā viṣṇuḥ , ata eva tayoḥ prameyaprasararūpasya

children.translated_text: 'this is blue' —
of such a nature, which is luminosity, is predominant —

children.text: iti pramātṛdaśāveśaśūnyatvāt na tṛtīyanetronmīlanam / devataiva daivatam /
children.translated_text: due to the absence of absorption in the perceiver-state, there is no opening of the third eye. The deity itself is the divinity (<s>daivata</s>).
'Spreading forth' (<s>prasara</s>) —
means origination and continuation. // 1 //

'Therein' — in this nature of principles as it is, established by scripture and conforming to reasoning: that which is this perceiver-form enveloped by the pentad of <s>kāla</s> and such — in whichever state it becomes pure, with the mass of knowables withdrawn — in that state called dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>), [<s>Rudra</s>] the blessed Lord <s>Īśvara</s> himself, assuming the role of presiding deity of that state — by bringing about that state and by turning toward Himself the community of His worshippers who have attained contemplative absorption in that state — is <s>Rudra</s>, the blessed one, who, even in the <s>Māyā</s>-level, through contact with the perceiver-nature whose form is the middle light — free from <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, which are of the nature of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, sun and moon, day and night, and such — has his third eye opened. But when the knowable spreads forth in the form of the flowing continuation of its succession, the presiding deity is <s>Viṣṇu</s>; therefore, for those two — since the form of the spreading forth of the knowable

children.text: yadetanmātṛtāmātramuktaṃ tasya vibhāgamāgamikaṃ ca saṃjñābhedaṃ nirūpayati /
children.translated_text: What has been stated as 'mere perceiver-hood' — of that he determines the division and the designation-distinctions according to scripture:
<s>Eṣa pramātā</s> (This perceiver), blinded by <s>Māyā</s>, is a <s>saṃsārin</s> (worldly being), bound by <s>karma</s>;
with sovereignty made known through <s>vidyā</s>, being a compact mass of consciousness, he is called liberated. //
When entities are of the nature of one's own limbs, the perceiver is called <s>Pati</s> (Lord);
when differentiated from [him] by <s>Māyā</s>, sullied by afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>), <s>karma</s>, and such — [he is called] <s>paśu</s> (bound soul). //

children.text: māyayāndho vimohitaḥ , ata eva karmāṇi svātmano bandhakānyabhimanyamāna

children.translated_text: 'this [perceiver]' —

children.text: iti kālādiveṣṭitaḥ śūnyādipramātā saṃsarati , ---- ityataḥ saṃsārī / deho 'pi hi svarūpasādṛśyaṃ bālyayauvanādiṣvanuvartayan saṃsaratīva / buddhyādestu janmāntare'pi saṃsaraṇam / vidyayā tu svarūpaprakāśanaśaktyā pratyabhijñāpadaṃ prāpitamaiśvarayaṃ yasya , ata eva śarīrādyapi viśvamapi ca saṃvedanamevābhimanyamāno'ta eva cideva ghanā anvācidrūpavyāmiśraṇaśūnyā yasya rūpam , sa punarjanmabandhavirahāt dehe 'pi sthite
children.translated_text: thus, the perceiver of the void and such, enveloped by <s>kāla</s> and such, transmigrates — therefore [he is] a <s>saṃsārin</s> (worldly being). Even the body, maintaining a resemblance of essential nature through childhood, youth, and such [stages], transmigrates, as it were. But for <s>buddhi</s> and such, there is transmigration even into another birth. But through <s>vidyā</s> — the power of manifesting one's own essential nature — one whose sovereignty has been brought to the stage of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), therefore regarding even the body and even the universe as nothing but consciousness (<s>saṃvedana</s>), therefore one whose form is consciousness alone, dense, unmixed with anything non-conscious — he, through freedom from the bondage of rebirth even while the body remains,
'liberated' —

children.text: iti vyapadeśayogyaḥ / patite tu śiva ekaghanaḥ iti kaḥ kuto muktaḥ / bhūtapūrvagatyā tu pramātrantarāpekṣayā muktah śivaḥ , ---- iti vyavahāraḥ /
children.translated_text: is worthy of this designation. But when the body has fallen, [he is] <s>Śiva</s> — one compact mass — so who [is liberated] from what? But in terms of former course, with reference to other perceivers, the liberated one is <s>Śiva</s> — this is the conventional usage.
Blinded by <s>Māyā</s>, deluded — therefore, regarding <s>karmas</s> as the bondage of one's own self —

children.text: yaścāsau muktaḥ sa bhāvān svāṅgavadabhimanyamānaḥ pramimīte iti sa teṣāṃ svāmī , svarūpaparamārthasamarpaṇācca pālakaḥ iti patirupadiṣṭaḥ śāstre / māyāśaktikṛtabhedān vyatiriktāneva sato yadā mimīte tadā taireva meyaiḥ pāśarūpaiḥ pāśitaḥ iti paśuruktaḥ / tathāhi vedyarāśivaśādevāsmāvi dyāsmitārāgadveṣābhiniveśādayaḥ kleśāḥ , dharmādharmādirūpāṇi karmāṇi , ādipadādāśayarūpā vāsanā , phalabhogarūpo vipākaḥ , ---- iti kāluṣyamanantaprakāram , yataḥ pāśitatvāt

children.translated_text: '<s>paśu</s>' (bound soul) —
he is called. // 3 //

And he who is liberated, regarding entities as his own limbs, measuring them — he is their master, and through the bestowal of their ultimate essential nature, he is their protector — thus he is taught as <s>Pati</s> (Lord) in the scripture. When he measures entities as existing separately, differentiated by the power of <s>Māyā</s> — then, bound by those very knowables which are of the form of fetters (<s>pāśa</s>) — he is called <s>paśu</s> (bound soul). Thus: from the mass of knowables arise <s>asmitā</s> (egoism), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life), and such — the afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>); <s>karmas</s> of the form of <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and such; by the word 'ādi' (etc.), the latent impressions (<s>āśaya/vāsanā</s>) of the form of dispositions; and <s>vipāka</s> (fruition), of the form of the enjoyment of results — thus the defilement is of infinite variety; because of being fettered,
That very <s>paśu</s>-form — that itself, in the scriptures, is the threefold <s>mala</s> (impurity) — thus he says:
The loss of freedom of knowledge, and the non-awareness of the freedom [of action] —
this twofold <s>āṇava-mala</s> (innate impurity), through the negation of one's own essential nature; //
in the very manifestation of differentiated knowables is the one called <s>māyīya</s> (impurity of <s>Māyā</s>), giving rise to birth and experience;
when there is non-awareness in the agent, [it is] <s>kārmika</s> (<s>karma</s>-impurity) — this triad is through <s>Māyā-śakti</s> alone. //

children.text: iha jñātṛkartṛrūpaṃ tāvaccittattvasya svarūpaṃ , tasyāpahāro nāmāṇavaṃ malaṃ yenāsāvaṇuḥ saṃkucito jātaḥ / tatra svarūpasya nimīlanaṃ saṃkocaḥ / tatsthite bodharūpe kartṛtvalakṣaṇasya svātantryātmanaḥ svarūpāntarasya nimīlanaṃ viparyayo vā , ---- ityubhayayāpyāṇavaṃ malaṃ svarūpāpahānirūpamekameva /
children.translated_text: Here, the essential nature of the <s>cit-tattva</s> (consciousness-principle) is of the form of knower and agent. Its removal is called <s>āṇava-mala</s> (innate impurity), by which it becomes an <s>aṇu</s> (atom/limited being), contracted. Therein, the closing of one's essential nature is contraction. The closing — or reversal — of another aspect of one's essential nature, namely freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>) characterized by agency, while the cognition-nature remains — by either [interpretation], the <s>āṇava-mala</s>, which is of the nature of the removal of one's essential nature, is one alone.

children.text: atraiveti , satyāṇave male dviprakāre svarūpasaṃkoce vṛtte bhinnasya yatprathanaṃ tasya

children.translated_text: 'māyīya' (Māyic) —

children.text: iti saṃjñāmātram / māyākṛtatvena māyīyatā malatrayasyāpi / tatra karturabodharūpasya dehāderbhinnavedyaprathane sati dharmādharmarūpaṃ kārmaṃ malam , yato janma bhogaśca sa ca niyatāvadhikaḥ , iti jātyāyurbhogaphalaṃ karma ityuktaṃ bhavati //4////5//
children.translated_text: is merely a designation. Being produced by <s>Māyā</s> is the <s>Māyic</s> nature — [this applies] even to all three impurities. Therein, when the differentiated knowable has been manifested for the agent who is of a non-cognitive nature, [what arises is] <s>kārma-mala</s> (the impurity of action), which is of the nature of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit). From that arise birth and experience, and that has a fixed duration. Thus, it is stated that <s>karma</s> has as its fruit birth-class (<s>jāti</s>), lifespan (<s>āyus</s>), and experience (<s>bhoga</s>). //4////5//
'Atraiva' (in this very [context]): when the <s>āṇava-mala</s> exists, when the twofold contraction of one's essential nature has occurred, the manifestation of what is differentiated — for that,
'svātantryahānirbodhasya' (the loss of freedom of cognition) —
he first states the domain of this [verse]:
Now, in order to clarify the essential nature of these impurities through the determination of their distinct domains —
Those who, even though of the nature of pure cognition, do not possess supreme agency —

children.text: nirmitāḥ svātmano bhinnā bhartrā te kartṛtātyayāt //
children.translated_text: they have been created as different from His own Self by the Lord, due to the loss of agency.

children.text: iti svātmaviśrāntyānandarūpaṃ pramaṃ svātantryam / te parmeśvareṇa tayā nirmitāḥ svātmanaḥ sakāśādvyatiriktāḥ / atra hetuḥ ----
children.translated_text: the supreme freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>) which is of the nature of bliss resting in one's own Self through valid cognition. They have been created by the Supreme Lord as distinct from His own Self. The reason here:
'of agency' —
of the supreme freedom —
'atyayāt' (due to the loss) —
due to the absence [of supreme freedom]. But the Supreme Lord has the nature of cognition inseparable from supreme freedom — this is the remainder of the intention. //6//
Those whose ultimate reality is mere consciousness alone, but not

children.text: nanvasmāddhetorbhavatu parameśvarāt teṣāṃ bhinnatvamanyonyatastu kathaṃ bhedo bodharūpasya vyāpitvanityatvakṛtasya ca deśakālābhedasya samābatvāt ; anyonyabhedābhāve ca

children.translated_text: 'they have been created' —
how is the plural number [justified]? He dispels this doubt:

Objection: By this reason, let them be different from the Supreme Lord; but how can they be different from each other, since cognition-nature is pervading and eternal, and there is sameness of non-difference in space and time? And in the absence of mutual difference,
Even in the unity of the single characteristic of cognition, their mutual difference
is by the Lord's will of differentiation; and they are <s>vijñānakevalas</s> (consciousness-only beings).

children.text: iha hi sarvatrāpratihataśaktiḥ parameśvara eva tayābubhūsaṃstathā tathā bhavati , natvanyaḥ kaścit paramārthayo 'sti , ---- ityasakṛduktam ; tataśca vyāviśeṣeṇa teṣāṃ śarīrādiśūnyāntapramātṛpadottīrṇānāṃ bodhatvanityatvavibhutvādidharmajātasyaikye 'pyanyonyaṃ bhedaḥ , te ca śāstre vijñānakevalā uktāḥ / tatra vijñāmakevalo malaikayuktaḥ , ---- ityādau

children.translated_text: 'vijñāna' (consciousness) —
the form whose nature is cognition,
'kevala' (only/mere) —
devoid of freedom — this is their [nature]. //7//

Here indeed, everywhere, the Supreme Lord alone, whose power is unobstructed, becomes thus and thus by that [power] in His desire to become — and there is no other [being] that is ultimately real. This has been stated repeatedly. And therefore, without distinction, even among those who have transcended the perceiver-level ranging from the body to the void, though there is unity of the group of properties such as cognition-nature, eternality, all-pervasiveness, and such — there is mutual difference. And they are called <s>vijñānakevalas</s> (consciousness-only beings) in the scriptures. Therein, the <s>vijñānakevala</s> is one endowed with a single impurity — and in the [explanation] beginning with that,
'the loss of freedom of cognition' —
having stated the domain of this portion as pertaining to the <s>vijñānākalas</s>,
'and even of freedom, the non-cognition' —
he clarifies this other portion by showing its domain:
Thus,
But those of the nature of non-cognition, such as the void — they are agents, <s>pralayākalas</s> (dissolution-only beings);
for them, the <s>kārma-mala</s> (impurity of action) also exists; but the <s>māyīya</s> (Māyic impurity) is contingent.

children.text: śūnye jaḍatvādanodharūpe eva , yadi vā prāṇe buddhau vā yeṣāṃ ahamiti camatkārayogāt kartṛtvaṃ te pralayena kṛtāḥ

children.translated_text: 'akalāḥ' (without <s>kalā</s>) —

children.text: kalātattvopalakṣitakaraṇakāryarahitā abodharūpāḥ kartāraśca / pralayāvadhi hi te tathākṛtāḥ uttarakālaṃ tu kāryakaraṇasaṃbaddhā eva bhavanti ; yatasteṣāṃ na kevalamuktarūpa ā,ava eva malo yāvat kārmo 'pi vāsanāsaṃskārarūpo dharmādharmātmāstyeva / yadyevam , bhinnavedyaprathāpyeṣāṃ syāt / satyam , savedye suṣuptapade , 'pavedye tu na bhavati ; tena māyīyo mala eṣāṃ vikalpito vyavasthitaviṣayatvena / tathā hi ---- ke'pi śūnyādibhāgaviśrāntā gāḍanidrājaḍīkṛtā apavedyasuṣuptapadabhājaḥ / anye tu buddhyādiniṣṭhāḥ sukhaduḥkhāvaśeṣasāmānyātmakabhinnavedyasaṃvedanayogitaḥ savedyasauṣuptapadalīnāḥ / sthūladehendriyātmakakāryakaraṇaviyogarūpatvaṃ tu pralayākalalakṣaṇaṃ sarveṣāṃ tukyam //8//
children.translated_text: devoid of the instruments and effects characterized by the <s>kalā-tattva</s> (principle of limited agency) and such — of a non-cognitive nature, yet agents. For they are made thus only until dissolution; in the subsequent time, they become connected with effects and instruments. Because for them, not only the aforementioned <s>āṇava</s> impurity exists, but also the <s>kārma</s> [impurity], which is of the nature of latent impressions and conditioning, and whose nature is <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit). If so, then they should also have the manifestation of differentiated knowables. True — in the state of deep sleep that has knowable objects, [they do]; but in the state without knowable objects, [they do] not. Therefore, the <s>māyīya-mala</s> for them is contingent — having a determinate domain. For thus: some, resting in the void-aspect, rendered inert by deep sleep, partake of the state of deep sleep without knowable objects. Others, established in the intellect and such, by virtue of connection with the perception of differentiated knowables consisting of the residual generality of pleasure and pain — are absorbed in the state of deep sleep with knowable objects. But the character of the <s>pralayākala</s> — the separation from the gross body and sense organs that constitute effects and instruments — is equal for all. //8//

Those for whom, in the void — which is of the nature of inertness and hence of non-cognition — or in the vital breath or intellect, there is agency due to the conjunction with the marvel of 'I' — they are made by dissolution,
'and even of freedom, the non-cognition' —

children.text: ityevamaṃśaḥ sphuṭīkṛtaḥ , prasaṅgācca kārmamalasya viṣayo darśitaḥ , māyāmalasya ca pākṣikatvamuktam / adhunā punarāṇavakārmamaladvayābhāve'pi śuddho'sti māyākhyasya malasya viṣayaḥ , ---- iti darśayati

Thus,
Even of those cognitions endowed with agency, when the <s>kārma-mala</s> has been exhausted,
for those possessing differentiated knowables, the <s>Māyā-mala</s> [remains]; and they are <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> (Lords of Knowledge).

children.text: iti ca camatkārollāsāt kartārastata eva sarvajñāḥ sarvakartāraśca te vidyeśvarāḥ / kintu tanukaraṇabhuvanādi yadeṣāṃ vedyatayā kāryatayā ca bhāti, tat kuvindapaṭadṛṣṭyā bhinnameva sat , ---- ityasti vidye śvarāṇāṃ māyākhyamalayogaḥ //9//

Those who see mere consciousness alone as the Self,

children.text: atha malatrayasyāpi yaugapadyena yo viṣayastaṃ darśayitumāha /
children.translated_text: Now, to show the domain where all three impurities exist simultaneously, he says:

'tatrāpi' (even among those) —

children.translated_text: even when all three exist, the <s>kārma-mala</s>, falling primarily, is the cause of transmigration. As stated:

Here, the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> and <s>vijñānākalas</s> are not subject to transmigration, since they have crossed beyond the path up to <s>Māyā</s>. The <s>pralayākalas</s> too are without transmigration for some time. But the gods and others down to stationary beings — the fourteen [classes] enumerated in the scriptures — who revolve within the domain of the <s>Māyā-tattva</s> — all of them are
{From <s>karma</s> alone [arise] the bodies, the sense-objects, and the instruments. /}

children.text: iti / tanukaraṇaviṣayasaṃbandha eva ca vartamāno bhaviṣyaṃśca , ---- ityanavarataṃ prabandhato vartamānaḥ saṃsaraṇamucyate / āṇavamāyāmalau tu yadyapi na kāraṇaṃ saṃsāre , tathāpi kārmeṇa vinā tau dehādivicitrabhāvābhinirvartanaśaktiśūnyau vijñānākalādiṣu , ---- iti mukhyaṃ kārmameva malaṃ saṃsārakāraṇaṃ tatra tatra śāstre gaṇyate / ata eva tadupakṣaye vṛtte dattastāvadasaṃsaraṇasopānapadabandhaḥ , ---- ityāśayena karmabandhābhimānaparihānireva yatnataḥ sāṃkhyapurāṇabhāratādiśāstreṣūpadiśyate / evaṃ malatrayasyaikaikabhedaistribhirdvibhedaistribhistribhedenaikena , iti sapta pramātāra uttiṣṭhanti / tathā ca śāstre
children.translated_text: Thus. The connection with body, instruments, and objects — which is present and future — continuously flowing in an unbroken series — is called transmigration. The <s>āṇava</s> and <s>māyā</s> impurities, although not the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, are nevertheless — without <s>karma</s> — devoid of the power to bring about the variegated states of body and such, as in the <s>vijñānākalas</s> and others. Therefore, the <s>kārma-mala</s> alone is counted as the primary impurity causing <s>saṃsāra</s> in this and that scripture. For this very reason, when it is diminished, the steps of the ladder to non-transmigration have been granted. With this intention, the abandonment of the false conceit of the bondage of <s>karma</s> is carefully taught in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Purāṇa</s>, <s>Bhārata</s>, and other scriptures. Thus, from the three impurities, with their individual varieties — three from single [varieties], three from dual [varieties], and one from the triple [variety] — seven perceivers arise. And thus in the scriptures:
{From <s>Śiva</s> down to <s>Sakala</s>, those endowed with power are seven. /}
Thus it is stated. And therein, through sub-varieties, through the distinction of secondary and primary, through the varieties of alternatives and combinations — there is infinite variety. //10//

children.text: asya ca malatrayasyodbhavatirobhāvabhedāt saṃsāriṇāṃ prakāradvayam , ---- iti darśayati
children.translated_text: And from the difference of the arising and concealment of these three impurities, the two modes of transmigrating beings are shown:
And this <s>cit-tattva</s> (consciousness-principle), brought forth by <s>Kalā</s> (limited agency), is of the nature of agency;
it is measured as a quality of what is of non-conscious nature, such as the void and others.
But the primacy of agency and of cognition, which is of the nature of consciousness,
in the void and such, which are its qualities — that knowledge characterized by <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption).

children.text: etacceti , yat tridaśādīnāṃ bhavināṃ caitanyaṃ kartṛtāṃśasya prādhānyānmalena saṃvidbhāgasya nimajjitatvāt kartṛtāmayam cidrūpasya tattvaṃ svātantryam , kalākhyena parameśvaraśaktyātmanā tattvena

children.text: idantāpannadehādiśūnyāntaprameyabhāganimagnatvāt prameyam , yo gauro , yaḥ sukhī , yastṛṣito , yaḥ sarvarūparahitaḥ so'ham , ---- iti hi idantaivāntarnītāhaṃbhāvā saṃsāriṇāṃ parisphurati / seyaṃ jāgratsvaprasuṣuptarūpā saṃsārāvasthā /
children.translated_text: due to having fallen into the state of 'this' — submerged in the knowable portion ranging from the body to the void — it is a knowable. 'I am the one who is fair-skinned,' 'I am the one who is happy,' 'I am the one who is thirsty,' 'I am the one devoid of all form' — thus, for transmigrating beings, the I-awareness flashes forth with its I-nature drawn into this-ness. This is the state of <s>saṃsāra</s> consisting of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep.

'This' — the consciousness of the gods and other transmigrating beings: since, due to the predominance of the agency-aspect, the consciousness-portion has been submerged by the impurity, it is of the nature of agency; and the freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>) that is the principle of what is of the nature of consciousness,

children.text: yadā tūktagurūpadeśādidiśā tenaivāhaṃbhāvena svātantryātmanā vyāpakatvanityatvādidharmaparāmarśamātmani / vidadhatā tataḥ śūnyādeḥ prameyādunmajjyevāsyate tadā turyātītāvasthā / yadāpi parāmṛṣṭatathābhūtavaibhavādinityaiśvaryasaṃbhedenaivāhaṃbhāvena śūnyādidehadhātvantaṃ siddharasayogena vidhyate , tadāsyāṃ turyadaśāyāṃ tadapi prameyatāmujjhatīva / seyaṃ dvayyapi jīvanmuktāvasthā

children.translated_text: 'samāveśa' (absorption) —

children.text: ityuktā śāstre / samyagāveśanameva hi tatra tatra pradhānam , tatsiddhaye tūpadeśāntarāṇi / yathā gītam /
children.translated_text: in the scriptures. For complete absorption (<s>samāveśana</s>) is indeed the primary [goal] everywhere; other instructions serve for its accomplishment. As stated in the <s>Gītā</s>:

But when, through the direction of the teaching of the guru and such as stated, by that very I-awareness whose nature is freedom, merely by performing the reflective grasping of properties such as all-pervasiveness, eternality, and such in oneself — one rises, as it were, out of the void and other knowables — then that is the state beyond the fourth (<s>turyātīta</s>). And when, by that very I-awareness conjoined with the always-sovereign glory and such that has been reflectively grasped, the range from the void to the body and bodily constituents is penetrated as if by the elixir of the <s>siddhas</s> — then, in that fourth state (<s>turya</s>), even that [void-to-body range] abandons, as it were, its knowable nature. This twofold [state] is the condition of <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living), called
{Those who, fixing their mind on Me...} (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 12.2)
Thus.
{Or, to fix the mind [on Me]...} (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 12.9)

children.text: ityādi ca / samāveśapallavā eva ca prasiddhadehādipramātṛbhāgaprahvībhāvabhāvanānuprāṇitāḥ parameśvarastutipraṇāmapūjādhyānasamādhiprabhṛtayaḥ karmaprapañcāḥ / yadgītamapi /
