Thus. But upon the fall of the body, there is the Supreme Lord alone as one single essence — so who would enter where and how? He says this: Now, the primacy of agency and the consequent subordinate status of the void and such — and in that subordinated non-conscious [element],

children.text: nanvevaṃ patyuḥ samāveśātmikā turyatadatītarūpā bhavatu daśā , paśostu kathaṃ suṣuptasvapnajāgradṛśābheda āgameṣūktaḥ , ---- ityāśaṅkya suṣuptasvarūpameva tāvadācaṣṭe ślokatrayeṇa /
children.translated_text: Objection: Let the lord (<s>pati</s>) have the state of the fourth and beyond-the-fourth in the form of <s>samāveśa</s>; but how is the difference of deep sleep, dream, and waking of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) stated in the scriptures? Anticipating this, he first describes the nature of deep sleep in three verses:
In the void, whose nature is the absence of intellect and such, which is the abode of I-awareness and agency,
which possesses only faint and formless impressions — there is the voidness of the knowable.
The internal activity that impels the vital breaths and such — considered as belonging to the senses —
or the I-awareness that resides in the vital breath and is of the nature of the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>), called 'living' —
the state of remaining in just that much is declared to be the state of deep sleep, resembling dissolution,
with or without knowable objects, and with or without the <s>māyā-mala</s>.

children.text: iha cittattvaṃ svasvarūpamācchādayat jñeyarūpeṇa buddhyādinā dehāntena ghaṭādinā vābhāsate / ekameva cedaṃ svātantryavijṛmbhitaṃ , na tvatra vāstavaḥ kramo vā bhedo vā / tatrāpi tu svātantryāt kramaśca bhedaścābhāsate / tadevaṃsthite yaścittattvasya svarūpācchādanabhāgaḥ sa evottarabhāgāntrāsaṃkīrṇo yadā viśrāmyati tadanudayādvā tatpradhvaṃsādvā pralaya iva tadanādaraṇādvā nidrāsamādhimūrcchādāviva , tatraiva cāhantārūpaṃ kartṛtāyāḥ padaṃ parāmarśo 'sphuṭatvādarūpātmanā saṃskāreṇa śuddhena vedyapadavīmaprāptena yukto bhavati , tadā saivāvasthā netyevaparāmarśaleśānapekṣitaniṣedhyabuddhyādiviṣayasuspaṣṭaparāmarśasaṃbhedāpi avaśyaṃbhāviniṣedhyayogāt

children.translated_text: 'I have nothing' —
like this, it accepts a universal-form to-be-negated; and precisely for this reason, having the knowable reduced to a mere latent impression, it
is called 'void' (<s>śūnya</s>).

children.text: ityucyate / tathāvidhe buddhyādīnāṃ dehādinīlāntānāmabhāvarūpe śūnyatvamucyate , yatastatra jñeyānāṃ
children.translated_text: In such a nature, the void-ness of the intellect and such, body and such, up to blue — is stated in the form of absence; since therein, of the knowables,
'voidness' (<s>śūnyatā</s>) —

children.text: abhāvarūpatā saṃskāraśeṣatā / iyameva hi sarvatrābhāvo na tu satāṃ sarvātmanā vināśaḥ /
children.translated_text: means having the form of absence, being reduced to a mere latent impression. For this alone constitutes absence everywhere — not the total annihilation of existents.

Here, the consciousness-principle (<s>cit-tattva</s>), concealing its own nature, appears in the form of the knowable — as intellect and such up to the body, or as pot and such. This is a single display of freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>); there is no real sequence or difference here. Yet even therein, through freedom, sequence and difference appear. This being the case, the aspect of consciousness that conceals its own nature — when it rests without admixture with the subsequent aspects, either due to non-arising [of those aspects] or due to their destruction — as in dissolution — or due to disregarding them — as in sleep, <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), fainting, and such — and therein the reflective awareness (<s>parāmarśa</s>) whose form is 'I'-awareness, which is the seat of agency, is conjoined with a pure latent impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) that has not reached the domain of the knowable, due to its indistinctness — then that very state, even though it does not depend upon the trace of the negation-reflective awareness 'not [this],' since it is not mixed with the clearly manifest reflective awareness of the to-be-negated — the intellect and such as its object — nevertheless, since it necessarily has the capacity for the to-be-negated,

children.text: tatraiva śūnye pramātari samavetā prāṇāpānasamānodānavyānātmake vāyucakre preraṇātmikā śaktiḥ , sā ca vidyākalayoḥ prapañcabhūtau yau krameṇa buddhīndriyakarmentriyavargau tayorāntarī vṛttiḥ / bāhyā hi tayoḥ śabdādyālocanaśabdābhivyaktisthānābhihananādikā vṛttiḥ / taduktam
children.translated_text: In that very void perceiver, the power of impulsion — co-present in the wind-circle consisting of <s>prāṇa</s> (in-breath), <s>apāna</s> (out-breath), <s>samāna</s> (equalizing breath), <s>udāna</s> (upward breath), and <s>vyāna</s> (pervading breath) — that [power] is the internal operation of the two groups — the cognitive sense organs and the action sense organs — which are the elaborations of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge-power) and <s>kalā</s> (limited agency) respectively. For their external operation consists of the apprehension of sound and such, the utterance of speech, the striking of specific places, and such. As stated:
{The five breaths — <s>prāṇa</s> and such — are the common operation of the senses.} (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 29)

children.text: iti / evaṃ śūnya evāhantā akṣacakropodvalitā jīvanam , iti sa śūnya eva jīvaḥ saṃsarati / yadi vendriyaśaktīnāmeva yāntarī sādhāraṇaprāṇanātmikā prāṇaśabdavācyā prāṇādimārutaviśeṣapreraṇāmayī saiva

ityadhiśayānā jīvanam , tadā prāṇa eva jīvaḥ saṃsārī , sa eva śūnyaḥ , prāṇāśca puryaṣṭakaśabdavācyaḥ , prāṇādipañcakaṃ buddhīndriyavargaḥ karmendriyagaṇo niścayātmikā ca yato dhīrvyajyate / tanmātrapañcakaṃ mano'haṃbuddhya ityanye
children.translated_text: presiding thus, is the life-force — then <s>prāṇa</s> itself is the <s>jīva</s>, the transmigrating one; that itself is the void. And the <s>prāṇas</s> are denoted by the word <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body) — the five-fold group of <s>prāṇa</s> and such, the group of cognitive senses, the group of action senses, and the intellect whose nature is determination, from which it is manifested. Others [include in the puryaṣṭaka] the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), mind, ego, and intellect —

Thus. In this way, when in the void itself, the 'I'-awareness, supported by the sense-circle, is the life-force — then the void itself is the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) that transmigrates. Or, if the internal [function] of the sense-powers — which is of the nature of common vitalization, denoted by the word <s>prāṇa</s>, and consisting of the impulsion of the specific winds <s>prāṇa</s> and such — if that very [function],
{In the form of the arising of the <s>tanmātras</s>, mind, ego, intellect... /} (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 4.19)
thus.
{Earth, waters, fire... /} (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 7.4)
— thus say [others].

children.text: evaṃ yadubhayātmakaṃ puryaṣṭakaṃ tāvatyeva śuddhe yā viśrāntiḥ , tasyāṃ satyāṃ yadahantāyāḥ suṣuptāyā bodhalakṣaṇaṃ bhāvarūpaṃ karma ca kriyāsvabhāvaṃ tat sauṣuptam / malena hi pramātā suptaḥ kalayā tvasupta iva , atra tannimajjane suṣṭhu suptastasya bhāvaḥ karma vā , ---- iti / tatra śūnyasauṣupte na kiñcidvyatiriktaṃ vedyam , ---- iti māyīyamalābhāvādapavedyaṃ tat ; prāṇasuṣupte tu sparśakṛtasya sukhaduḥkhāderbhāvāt māyākhyamasti malam , ---- iti savedyaṃ tat / evaṃ gāḍhāgāḍhasuṣuptadvitayavat pralayo 'pi mantavyaḥ / sa paraṃ dehādipradhvaṃsānudayakṛtaściratarakālaśca / suṣuptaṃ tu dehādyanādarakṛtamacirakālaṃ ca , ---- iti viśeṣaḥ / tatrāpi śramakṛtaṃ nidrā , dhātudoṣakṛtaṃ mūrcchā , dravyakṛtaṃ madonmādādi , svātantryakṛtaṃ samādhiḥ , ---- ityādyavāntarabhedaḥ / kecittu samādhirūpaṃ savedyamanyadapavedyam , ---- iti prapannāḥ //15//
children.translated_text: Thus, when the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s>, which is of both kinds, rests in that much alone that is pure — when that [state] obtains, the being-nature (<s>bhāva</s>) and the action of the nature of activity that belong to the 'I'-awareness in its dormant state, having the character of awakening — that is the <s>sauṣupta</s> (deep sleep state). For the perceiver is asleep through <s>mala</s> (impurity), but by <s>kalā</s> (limited agency) is as if unsleeping; when there is thorough immersion in that [mala], he is well asleep (<s>suṣupta</s>) — and that is his state or action. Therein, in the void-deep-sleep, there is no distinct knowable whatsoever — and therefore, due to the absence of <s>māyīya-mala</s> (impurity of Māyā), that [state] is without knowable content. But in the <s>prāṇa</s>-deep-sleep, since there exists touch-produced pleasure, pain, and such, the impurity called <s>Māyā</s> exists — and therefore, that [state] has knowable content. Similarly, dissolution too should be considered as twofold, like deep and shallow deep-sleep. But that [dissolution] is produced by the destruction and non-arising of the body and such, and extends over a very long time. Deep sleep, however, is produced by the disregarding of the body and such, and extends over a short time — this is the distinction. Even therein, [sleep] produced by fatigue is <s>nidrā</s> (sleep); produced by imbalance of bodily humors is <s>mūrcchā</s> (fainting); produced by substances is intoxication, madness, and such; produced by freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>) is <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) — thus the sub-divisions. Some, however, maintain that the <s>samādhi</s> form has knowable content and the other [forms] are without knowable content. // 15 //

children.text: nanvevaṃ sphuṭavedyapadavinirmuktā suṣuptāvasthāstu , svapnajāgrahaśayostu sphuṭavedyāvabhāsayoginyoḥ ko bhedaḥ ? ityāśaṅkya ślokadvayena bhedamāha
children.translated_text: Objection: Let the deep-sleep state, which is free from manifest knowable content, be thus; but for the dream and waking states, which possess the appearance of manifest knowables — what is the difference? Anticipating this, he states the difference in two verses:
Even though on the path of mind alone, due to the delusion of being objects of the senses,
the creation of entities with clear appearance — that is considered the dream state.
But that creation which, through being the object of all senses, is stable due to externality,
and is common to all perceivers — that is waking.

children.text: bāhyendriyāṇi cakṣurgolakādīni nimīlitāni nidrāyamāṇasya lakṣyante , na ca teṣu nimīliteṣu bāhyendriyagrahaṇavyāpāro dṛṣṭaḥ , tena śuddha eva manomārge rūpasparśādayo bhāvā akṣagrahaṇasamucitena spaṣṭena vapuṣā bhāsanayogyāḥ parmeśvareṇa sṛjyante , na tvaṇunā , aniṣṭasyaiva darśanāt , iṣṭasyāpi deśakālāntarādiyogena / ata eva manomātrasthitatvādeva na pramātrantarasādhāraṇīyaṃ sṛṣṭiḥ / yattu tatra bāhyendriyaviṣayatvaṃ pramātrantarasādhāraṇyaṃ cakāsti , tadyadyapi yāvadbhāti tāvat tathaiva , tathāpyuttarakālaṃ prabuddhasya na tathā , ---- iti parāmarśena tadrūpaṃ nirmūlatvenāvabhāti , ---- iti bhrāntam / yāni hi pramātrantarāṇi svapne sventriyāṇi ca bhānti , etāni prabodhakālabhāvibhireva tairabhinnāni , ---- iti niścayaḥ , prabodhakāle ca na tathā , ---- iti niścayānuvṛttirapahṛtaiva / tenobhayamapi bhrāntamucyate ; bhrāntatvameva cāsthairyam / evamindriyāviṣayatvenaivāsādhāraṇatvamākṣiptam ,
children.translated_text: For one who is sleeping, the external senses — the eyeball and such — are observed to be closed; and when they are closed, no operation of grasping by the external senses has been observed. Therefore, on the pure mental path alone, the Supreme Lord creates entities — forms, touches, and such — with a clear form appropriate for sense-grasping, as fit for manifestation. But not by an atom [does the individual cause them], since even what is not desired is seen, and even what is desired [appears] with conjunction of different place, time, and such. For this very reason — precisely because they exist only on the mental path — the creation is not common to other perceivers. And the appearance of being objects of the external senses and of being common to other perceivers that shines therein — although, as long as it shines, it is indeed so — nevertheless, for one who has awakened later, it is not so. Thus, through reflective awareness, that form appears as groundless — hence it is erroneous. For the other perceivers and one's own senses that appear in the dream — these are non-different from the very ones that exist at the time of waking. This is the certainty. But at the time of waking, the continuation of that certainty is simply taken away — [the certainty] 'it is not so.' Therefore, both [certainties] are said to be erroneous; and erroneous-ness itself is instability. Thus, through not being the object of the senses, the non-commonness is implied:
{And through delusion alone, instability... /}

children.text: iti svakaṇṭhena , tat jāgratpratiyogidharmanirūpaṇāvasare'pi na darśitam / evaṃbhūtā yā sṛṣṭiḥ sā paśoḥ svapnasamaye bhāvāt

children.translated_text: 'the dream state' —

children.text: svapnakāle viṣayaḥ iti , tathābhūtaviṣayaṃ pramātṛttvaṃ paśoḥ svapnāvasthā iti yāvat / akṣagrahaṇaṃ bāhyendriyadaśakasyopalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: the domain at the time of dream. The subjecthood possessing such a domain, for the bound soul, is the dream state — to that extent. The word 'sense-grasping' is illustrative of the ten external senses.

— by the author's own words. That was not demonstrated even at the occasion of determining the counter-correlative properties of waking. A creation of such a nature — since it occurs for the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) at the time of dream — is

children.text: yatra tu bāhyākṣavi.ayaṃ sarvapramātṛsādhāraṇatvaṃ ca niścayānuvṛttyā bādhārahitayā paramārthatvena cakāsti , tata eva sthairya viṣayasya sā sṛṣṭiḥ paśoḥ jāgaraḥ ; tadviṣayaṃ pramātṛtvaṃ jāgarāvasthā , ---- iti yāvat / yāvaccānuvṛttisthairya niścayasya cakāsti tāvajjāgaraḥ / tanmadhye ca niścayānuvṛttinirmūlanāt svapnaḥ , ---- ityavabhāsasāratvāt vastūnāṃ , svapne 'pi dīrghe yatra svapnāntaraṃ sa tadapekṣayā jāgradeva ; jāgradabhimatamapi vā dīrghadīrghaṃ kālāntare niścayānuvṛttinirpdhājjāgradantarāpekṣayā svapna eveti mantavyam //17//
children.translated_text: But where the creation shines as the object of external senses, as common to all perceivers, and as ultimately real — through the continuation of certainty that is free from sublation — from that very [unsublated continuation] the stability of the object [follows]. That creation, for the bound soul, is waking; the subjecthood possessing that domain is the waking state — to that extent. And as long as the stability of the continuation of certainty shines, so long is waking. And within that, dream [occurs] through the uprooting of the continuation of certainty. Thus, since the essence of things is their appearance-nature — even in a dream, when it is long, whatever dream-within-a-dream [occurs], that in comparison to it is waking itself. Or even what is believed to be waking, over a very long period of time, [if] the continuation of certainty is uprooted in a later time — in reference to an inner waking — should be considered dream itself. // 17 //

children.text: āsāṃ tisṛṇāṃ heyatvapradarśanena turyāvasthātaḥ prabhṛtyupādeyatvaṃ sūcayati
children.translated_text: By showing the rejectability of these three [states], he indicates the acceptability [of what lies] from the <s>turya</s> (fourth) state onward:
This triad is to be rejected, since, due to the predominance of <s>prāṇa</s> and such, agency becomes subordinate,
due to the conjunction with pleasure, pain, and such, which consist mostly of the loss and gain of that [agency].

children.text: yatrāyaṃ pramātā tyāgopādānatadicchāprayatnādikaṃ parikleśaṃ paśyati , tadevāsya heyatayā bhāti / sa cāsya sukhaduḥkhayogavaicitryeṇaiva kṛtaḥ , taccaitadavasthātraye saṃbhavati ; yataḥ kartṛtārūpaṃ svātmaviśrāntyananyaunmukhyalakṣaṇamānandaikaghanaṃ yaccinmayaṃ vapuḥ , tadyadā prāṇādimat śūnyapuryaṣṭakadehādibhūmiṣu guṇa tāmabhyeti , tadā tasmin guṇībhūte prāṇādeḥ prādhānyaṃ sphurati / tathā ca tasya cidrūpasya yathāyathā hānistathātathā duḥkhopacayo , yathāyathā kiñcidunmajjanaṃ tathātathā sukhopacayaḥ / tathāhi ---- bubhukṣākāle prāṇasyaivodrekāt duḥkhaṃ , tṛptau tasya nyagbhāvādahantodreke sukhaṃ yuktam / evaṃ śrāntasya mardanāmardane dehaprādhānayāprādhānye mantavye / yastu samāveśatattvajñastasya tatkāle duḥkhānudaya eva / yadāha
children.translated_text: When this perceiver sees the affliction of renunciation, acquisition, desire for that, effort, and such — that alone appears to him as rejectable. And that [affliction] is caused by the variety of the conjunction with pleasure and pain. And that occurs in all three states. For the body of consciousness — whose form is agency, characterized by resting in one's own Self and non-looking-toward-another, which is a solid mass of bliss — when it becomes subordinate in the domains of <s>prāṇa</s> and such, void, <s>puryaṣṭaka</s>, body, and such, then, with it having become subordinate, the predominance of <s>prāṇa</s> and such becomes manifest. And thus, the more the loss of that consciousness-nature, the more the accumulation of pain; the more there is some emergence [of it], the more the accumulation of pleasure. For thus: at the time of hunger, due to the predominance of <s>prāṇa</s> alone, there is pain; at satiation, due to its subordination, and the predominance of the 'I'-awareness, pleasure is reasonable. Similarly, for one who is fatigued, massaging and not massaging should be understood as the predominance and non-predominance of the body. But for one who knows the truth of <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption), at that time there is simply no arising of pain. As stated:
{Even one who is weak, by resorting to that [power], engages in activity;
and one who is extremely hungry can conceal the hunger. //} (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 48)

children.text: iti / evaṃ prāṇādeḥ prādhānye kartṛtāyā guṇabhāve sukhaduḥkhavaicitryaśatayogaḥ prayāsabhūmiḥ , --- iti jāgratsvapnasuṣupte prāṇādiprādhānyaṃ kartṛtānyambhāvaścāsti , ---- iti tat trayameva heyam / kartṛtāprādhānyonmeṣāttu turyarūpātprabhṛti tatsthairyātmakaturyātītadaśāntamupādeyam , ekarasānandaghanasvabhāvalābhe upāditsā -- jihāsā -- vaivaśya -- pariśrama-- praśamāt , ---- iti tātparyam //18//
children.translated_text: Thus. When <s>prāṇa</s> and such predominate and agency becomes subordinate — the conjunction with hundreds of varieties of pleasure and pain is the ground of exertion. Since in waking, dream, and deep sleep there is the predominance of <s>prāṇa</s> and such and the subordination of agency — all three are rejectable. But from the opening of the predominance of agency — which is the <s>turya</s> (fourth) form — up to the <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth) state, which is the stabilization of that — [everything from there] is acceptable, since with the attainment of the nature of a solid mass of homogeneous bliss, the desire to acquire, the desire to abandon, helplessness, and exertion are pacified. This is the purport. // 18 //

children.text: nanu prāṇādiprādhānyaṃ heyatāyāṃ kāraṇamuktaṃ taccejjāgradāditraya eva tarhi turyādau tadabhāvāt tatsamāveśe vyutthāmānupapattiḥ , ---- iti ślokadvayena śaṅkāṃ pariharati /
children.translated_text: Objection: If the predominance of <s>prāṇa</s> and such is stated as the cause of rejectability, and if that exists only in the triad of waking and such — then, in <s>turya</s> and beyond, due to its absence, the impossibility of emergence (<s>vyutthāna</s>) from absorption into that [state would follow]. He resolves the doubt in two verses:
<s>Prāṇa</s>, consisting of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, [operates] individually in sleep and waking;
the one called <s>samāna</s>, whose nature is the cessation of those two, [operates] in deep sleep — as in the equinoxes.
The one called <s>udāna</s>, which goes to the middle and upward, is the <s>turya</s>-goer, of the nature of fire;
<s>Vyāna</s>, whose essence is the <s>Vijñānākala</s> and <s>Mantreśvara</s>, is the all-pervading, the supreme.
'Prāṇa' —

children.text: iti prāṇāpānarūpā jīvanasvabhāvā yeyaṃ cidrūpasya sthitiḥ , sā tāvatsāmānyaparispandarūpā , dehaprāṇāderacetanasya cetanāyamānatāsaṃpādanātmikā ahamitisvātranryāropasārā satī vikalpaparāmarśamayī saiva prāṇāpānādiviśeṣātmanā pañcarūpatāṃ bhajate / tatra kiñcijjahatī kvacitpatantī ca śvāsaniḥśvāsarūpā krameṇa prāṇatvamapānatvaṃ ca viśeṣaṃ darśyati / tadidaṃ viśeṣadvayaṃ jāgrati tāvat sphuṭameva dehāt prasṛtya viṣeye viśrānteḥ , tato 'pi dehe ; smṛtyādau vābhyantare vedye viśrānteḥ prāṇāpānayoḥ suspaṣṭatvāt / svapne 'pi taddvayamastyeva ; svapato 'pi hi prāṇāpānau nirgamapraveśātmānau sphuṭameva pareṇa lakṣyete / svayameva ca vedya saṃvedanāt tyāgopādānarūpā sthitiḥ saṃvedyata eva , tena prāṇanā prāṇāpānaviśeṣadvayamayī jāgrati , tathā svapne ; suptaṃ svapnaḥ , tadeva tu yadā sutarāṃ puṣṭaṃ bhavati , tadā suṣuptaḥ pramātā , tasyedaṃ sauṣuptaṃ padam / tat dvividhamapi samānākhyarūpaviśeṣaṃ prāṇīyaṃ svīkaroti / savedye tāvatsuṣupte yadyapi prāṇāpānaspando lakṣyate , tathāpi tayormadhye yā viśrāntihṛdayasadane nirindriye pradeśe tadeva mukhyataḥ suṣuptamiti / tatra prāṇāpānayoryaśchedo viśrāntiḥ kaṃcitkālaṃ tadātmā sakalarasādivargasyordhvādharatiryakṣu samānīkaraṇavyāpārātmā , tata eva hṛtpadmavikāsadānādbhuktapītajaraṇakārī samāno dinarātrirūpayoḥ prāṇāpānayoḥ kaṃcitkālaṃ sāmyādvicchedācca viṣuvatkālatulyaḥ / viṣuṃ vyāptiṃ samānīkaraṇamarhati , ---- iti , {tadarham}(pāṣū.5-1-117) iti vatiḥ / upamāne vatereva cāvyavatvam
children.translated_text: this <s>prāṇa</s>, which is of the form of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> and whose nature is vitalization — this condition of the consciousness-nature — has first a general pulsation-form, accomplishing the animation of the insentient body, <s>prāṇa</s>, and such, whose essence is the superimposition of freedom as 'I' upon them, being of the nature of <s>vikalpa</s>-reflective awareness — that very [condition] assumes fivefold form through the specific natures of <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and such. Therein, partially relinquishing and partially falling — in the form of inhalation and exhalation — it shows the specific forms of <s>prāṇa</s>-nature and <s>apāna</s>-nature respectively. This specific pair [is manifest] in waking, to begin with, quite clearly — since having extended from the body, it rests in the object, and from there again in the body; or in memory and such, resting in an internal knowable — hence the clear manifestation of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>. In dream too, this pair exists; for even of one who is sleeping, the outgoing and incoming <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> are clearly observed by another. And since one experiences the knowable oneself, the condition of the form of relinquishing and acquiring is itself experienced. Therefore, the vitalization, consisting of the specific pair of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, [operates] in waking and likewise in dream. 'Supta' (sleep) is dream; and when that very [state] becomes further nourished, then the perceiver is in deep sleep (<s>suṣupta</s>), and this is his <s>sauṣupta</s> (deep sleep) state. That state, in both its forms, accepts the specific form called <s>samāna</s>. In deep sleep with knowable content, although the pulsation of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> is observed, nevertheless the repose that is between them — in the heart-abode, in the region devoid of senses — that alone is primarily deep sleep. Therein, the cessation of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, the repose for some time, whose nature is the operation of equalizing the entire group of flavors and such in the upward, downward, and transverse directions — from that very [equalization], bestowing the opening of the heart-lotus, digesting what has been eaten and drunk — <s>samāna</s> is similar to the equinox-time, since in the day-and-night-form <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, for some time there is equality and cessation. 'Viṣu' means pervasion, equalization — [the equinox] deserves that. The suffix 'vat' [is added] by the rule {tadarham} (<s>Pāṇini</s> 5.1.117). And in an expression of comparison, the indeclinability of 'vat' —
'raised up, [it is] calmed' —

children.text: iti prayogāt ; taddhi nyāyasiddhaṃ na vācanikam / viśeṣaṃ vā dinarātritadūnādhikarvalakṣaṇaṃ suvati prerayatyaviratam , ---- iti śatari viṣuvat / tatra ca viṣuvati vicchidyamānasya prāṇāpānasya saṃskārarūpatayā sadbhāvaḥ , saiva hi vicchedo na tu sarvātmanā nāśo'sti , ---- ityuktamasakṛt / tataśca hānādānayorbījarūpatā suṣupte ; iyati ca sarvaḥ pralayākalāntaḥ paśuvargaḥ /
children.translated_text: from such usage; for that is established by logical principle, not merely by textual authority. Or it impels (<s>suvati</s>) ceaselessly the specific [distinctions] characterized by day and night and their diminished and augmented parts — hence, by the <s>śatṛ</s> suffix, <s>viṣuvat</s> (equinox). And therein, in the equinox, the existence of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> that are being interrupted is in the form of residual impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) — for that very [impression] is the interruption, not an absolute annihilation — this has been stated repeatedly. And therefore, in deep sleep, there is the seed-form of rejection and acceptance; and to this extent, the entire class of bound souls up to and including the <s>pralayākalas</s> [is accounted for].

children.text: yadā tu sā prāṇanāvṛttirvāmadakṣiṇamārgau khilībhāvayantī madhyarūpeṇordhvena pravahati , tadā tatpravahaṇaṃ sakalasya bhedasyābhedasāratādānalakṣaṇaṃ vilāpanamāśyānasyeva sarpiṣo vidadhatī udānavṛttirvijñānākalādārabhya sadāśivāntam , sā ca turyātmikā daśā / māyordhve hi vijñānākalāḥ , ---- iti tataḥprabhṛti bhedagalanaṃ pravartate / vilīne tu bhede sarvavedyarāśirūpatattvabhūtabhuvanavargātmaladehavyāpanarūpeṇa prāṇavṛttirvyānarūpā viśvātmakaparamaśovpcitā turyātītarūpā / prāṇa eva pramātā prāṇāpānarūpaḥ samānarūpa udānarūpo vyānarūpaśca , ---- iti sāmānādhikaraṇyam , vijñānākalaścāsau mantraścāsau vargāpekṣayā , īśaśca sadāśiveśvararūpo yo'sau , ---- iti udānaḥ / etaduktaṃ bhavati , yadyapi turyatadatītayorapyasti prāṇanā ---- anyathā jīvatvasya vyutthānasya cānupapatteḥ ---- tathāpi bhedopasaṃhāreṇābhedaviśrāntipradhānatvādanayordaśayoḥ sukhaduḥkhādivaicitryāyogāt ekaghanasvātmaviśrāntyātmakaparamānandamayatvenopādeyataiva / suṣuptādau tu saṃskārarūpatvāsphuṭavedyollāsasphuṭavedyāvabhāsarūpasya bhedasya vidyamānatvāt asti sukhaduḥkhādivaicitryam , ---- iti heyataiva , ---- iti yuktamuktaṃ

children.translated_text: 'This triad is to be rejected' —

children.text: ityādi / bhagavataśca viśvaśarīrasya prāṇāpānasamānodānavyānarūpataiva sakalagatollāsapraveśapralayākalavijñānākalaādivargaśivarūpatā , ---- ityapyanena darśitam / yathoktam
children.translated_text: and so forth. And of the Blessed One whose body is the universe, the very nature of being in the form of <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>samāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, and <s>vyāna</s> — is the nature of being <s>Śiva</s> in the form of the classes of <s>sakala</s>, whose manifestation is spreading forth, <s>praveśa</s> (entry), <s>pralayākala</s>, <s>vijñānākala</s>, and such — this too has been shown by this. As has been stated:

But when that vital activity, rendering the left and right channels fallow, flows upward in the form of the middle [channel], then that flow — of the nature of dissolving all differentiation into the essence of non-differentiation, like the melting of solidified ghee — is the <s>udāna</s> (ascending vital) function, beginning from the <s>vijñānākalas</s> up to <s>Sadāśiva</s>; and that is the state having the nature of <s>turya</s> (the fourth state). For above <s>Māyā</s> are the <s>vijñānākalas</s> — from that point onward the dissolution of differentiation commences. But when differentiation has been dissolved, the vital function in the form of pervading [all] through the body of impurity (<s>mala</s>) consisting of the entire mass of knowables — the group of principles, worlds, and such — is the <s>vyāna</s> (all-pervading vital) form, identical with <s>Paramaśiva</s> of universal nature, having the nature of the <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth) state. <s>Prāṇa</s> alone is the perceiver: in the form of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, in the form of <s>samāna</s>, in the form of <s>udāna</s>, and in the form of <s>vyāna</s> — this is the co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). And he is a <s>vijñānākala</s>, and he is a <s>Mantra</s>, with reference to class; and the Lord in the form of <s>Sadāśiva-Īśvara</s> — that is the <s>udāna</s>. What is being said is this: although in <s>turya</s> and <s>turyātīta</s> too there is vital activity — otherwise the state of being alive and the return [to ordinary consciousness] would be impossible — nevertheless, since in these two states the predominance lies in the repose in non-differentiation through the withdrawal of differentiation, there being no occasion for the variety of pleasure, pain, and such, they are to be adopted, as they consist of the supreme bliss of repose in one's own Self as a single compact mass. But in deep sleep and such, since differentiation exists in the form of residual impressions, indistinct knowable-manifestation, and distinct knowable-appearance — there is indeed the variety of pleasure, pain, and such — therefore they are to be rejected. Thus it was rightly said:
{'The universe, consisting of thirty-six [principles], is the powers of <s>Śambhu</s> beginning with <s>prāṇa</s> and such.' /}
Thus. // 20 // From the beginning, 171 //

Thus ends the second daily lesson, entitled 'Determination of the Perceiver-Principle' (<s>Pramātṛtattvanirūpaṇa</s>), in the Scripture Section (<s>Āgamādhikāra</s>) of the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s> composed by the venerable master <s>Utpaladeva</s>, accompanied by the commentary called <s>Vimarśinī</s> composed by the venerable master <s>Abhinavagupta</s>. // 2 //
And this Scripture Section, the third [investigation], is hereby complete. // 3 //

children.translated_text: the Self who manifests [this] to devotees — Him, <s>Śiva</s>, we praise! //}

children.text: evaṃ svasaṃvedanopapattyāgamasiddhaṃ maheśvararūpamātmasvarūpaṃ yadadhikāratrayeṇa vitatya nirṇītaṃ tadeva saṃkṣepeṇa śiṣyabuddhiṣu niveśayitumāgamārthagrahaṃ ślokāṣṭādaśakena darśayati

children.translated_text: 'One's own Self alone, of all beings' —
beginning with this,
'demonstrated by <s>Utpala</s>' —

children.text: ityantenaikenāhnikena / tatra ‘lsokena pāramārthikaṃ rūpamuktvā ślokanavakena bandhasvarūpaṃ pramātṛprameyatattvadarśanadiśā , saptakena pratyabhijñātmakaṃ mokṣatattvaṃ , ślokenopasaṃhāraṃ darśayati , ---- iti tātparyam / granthārthastu nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: ending with this, in a single daily lesson. Therein, by one verse [he shows] the ultimate nature; by a group of nine verses, the nature of bondage from the perspective of the perceiver-principle and the knowable-principle; by seven [verses], the <s>mokṣa</s>-principle (liberation-principle) of the nature of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>); and by one verse, the conclusion — this is the purport. The meaning of the text is now determined:

Thus, the essential nature of the Self, which is of the form of <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord), established through the three sections by the justification of self-awareness and scripture — that very thing, in order to instill it in summary form in the intellects of disciples, he displays the grasp of the meaning of scripture through a group of eighteen verses,
One's own Self alone, of all beings, is the one <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord);
of universal form, nourished by the unbroken reflective grasping 'I am this.' //

children.text: iha jaḍāstāvaccetananimagnā eva bhānti ; idamiti hi jaḍaparāmarśo'hamiti saṃvitparāmarśa eva viśrāmyati / tataśca jaḍā nirātmāna iti jantava eva jīvāḥ sātmānaḥ , teṣāṃ ca maheśvara eva svātmā sa eva maheśvaro na tvanyaḥ kaścit / yataḥ saṃvitsvabhāvo'sau , saṃvidaśca na deśena na kālena na svarūpeṇa ko'pi bhedaḥ , kāmaṃ dehaprāṇādayo bhidyantāṃ , te tu jaḍapakṣyāścetananimagnā eva , ---- ityeka eva cidātmā svātantryeṇa svātmani yato vaiśvarūpyaṃ bhāsayati , tato maheśvaro'ntarnītāmidantāṃ kṛtvā parānunmukhasvātmaviśrāntirūpāhaṃvimarśaparipūrṇaḥ , ata eva sarvajñasarvakartṛtve nāsya yatnopapādye , vicitrabuddhikarmendriyaviṣaye hi yathā jñātṛtvakartṛtve ekasyaivātmanastayendriyasthānīyarudrakṣetrajñasahasraviṣayasya bhāvarāśerjajjñānaṃ karaṇaṃ ca tadekatra cidātmani , ---- iti //1//
children.translated_text: Here, the insentient things shine only as submerged in consciousness; for the insentient reflective grasping 'this' comes to rest only in the consciousness-reflective-grasping 'I.' And therefore, the insentient being without self, the living beings (<s>jantus</s>) — the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) — alone possess a self; and their own Self is <s>Maheśvara</s> alone — He alone is <s>Maheśvara</s>, and no other whatsoever. Since He is of the nature of consciousness, and of consciousness there is no differentiation whatsoever — neither by space, nor by time, nor by essential nature — let the body, vital breath, and such be differentiated [as they may]; they belong to the insentient side and are submerged in consciousness alone. Thus the one consciousness-Self alone, through freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>), manifests in His own Self the universal variety; therefore He is <s>Maheśvara</s>, having internalized the 'this'-ness and being replete with the 'I'-reflective-grasping which is of the form of repose in one's own Self without turning toward another. Therefore, omniscience and omnipotence are not to be established for Him through effort — for just as in the case of the variegated cognitive and action sense-faculties, the knowledge and agency of the single Self alone — pertaining to the mass of entities in the domain of the thousands of <s>Rudra</s>-field-knowers that stand in the place of those sense-faculties — that knowledge and action [reside] in the one consciousness-Self. // 1 //

children.text: nanu yadyeka evāyaṃ maheśvararūpa ātmā kastarhi bandho yadavamocanāyāyamudyamaḥ ? ityāśaṅkyāha
children.translated_text: Objection: If this Self is indeed one, of the form of <s>Maheśvara</s>, then what is bondage, for the liberation from which this effort [of the treatise] is undertaken? Anticipating this, he says:
Therein, in the 'this'-portion of His own creation, through <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and such, in the form of the grasper —
it has been brought to the domain of the reflective grasping of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego); by this [means], that [Self is bound]. //

children.text: tatraivaṃ svātmani maheśvare sthite tasminneva prakāśarūpe svātmadarpaṇe tenaiva parameśvareṇa svātantryāt tāvatsṛṣṭaḥ saṃkocapuraḥsara idaṃbhāgaḥ , tanmadhe yadetadbuddhiprāṇadeharūpamidantayā vedyaṃtadbuddhyādibhinnasya vedyasya prāhakatayā samucitam idaṃbhāvābhibhavāprabhaviṣṇutvāt kṛtakenāpūrṇenāhaṃbhāvena parāmarśena bhāsamānaṃ cakāsti

children.translated_text: 'I am <s>Devadatta</s>; I am <s>Caitra</s>' —
thus. // 2 //

There — thus, <s>Maheśvara</s> abiding in His own Self — in that very luminous mirror of His own Self, by that very <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord) through His freedom, first is created the 'this'-portion preceded by contraction. In the midst of that, this which is of the form of <s>buddhi</s>, <s>prāṇa</s>, and body, being knowable as 'this,' being suited to the grasper-status of the knowable differentiated from <s>buddhi</s> and such — incapable of overcoming the 'this'-nature — shining with a manufactured, incomplete I-sense through reflective grasping, it gleams:

children.text: nanvevamapyastu , tathāpi kasya bandhaḥ ? īśvaravyatirikto hi ko'nyo'sti ? tadetatparihartumāha ----
children.translated_text: Objection: Even granting this, still — whose bondage is it? For who else exists apart from the Lord? To remove this [doubt], he says:
He, consisting of the non-recognition of his own essential nature, is considered to be the many <s>puruṣas</s> (individual souls);
therein, in creation, action and bliss — experience is of the nature of pain and pleasure. //

children.text: satyam , paramārthato na kaścid bandhaḥ kevalaṃsvasmādanuttarāt svātantryāt yadā svātmānaṃ saṃkucitamavabhāsayati sa eva , tadā svasya pūrṇasya rūpasya yadaparijñānaṃ bhāsamānatve 'pyaparāmarśarūpaṃ tadeva kāraṇatvena prakṛtaṃ yasya sa pūrṇatvākhyātimātratattvaḥ

children.translated_text: '<s>puruṣa</s>' (individual soul) —

children.text: ityucyate / ata evānekaḥ tattaddehaprāṇabuddhiviśeṣeṇa saṃkocagrahaṇāt / sa ca pumān bhoktā sambandhanaṃ bhogalakṣaṇamanubhavati / bhogaśca nāma tasya yau kalpitau kriyānandau , kalpitā kriyā duḥkham , rajo hi prakāśāprakāśacāñcalyarūpaṃ duḥkhamucyate ; prakāśarūpaṃ ca sattvaṃ sukham ; tamastvaprakāśarūpo madhye viśramaḥ pralayasthānīyaḥ //3//
children.translated_text: is so called. Therefore [he is] many, due to the apprehension of contraction through the specificity of each body, vital breath, and intellect. And that <s>puruṣa</s> is an experiencer (<s>bhoktā</s>) — he undergoes the connection called experience (<s>bhoga</s>). And experience means the constructed action and bliss that belong to him: constructed action is pain — for <s>rajas</s>, being of the form of the restlessness of luminosity and non-luminosity, is called pain; and <s>sattva</s>, being of the form of luminosity, is pleasure; and <s>tamas</s>, being of the form of non-luminosity, is the intermediate repose, standing in the place of dissolution. // 3 //

True — in ultimate reality there is no bondage whatsoever. But merely through His own unsurpassed freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>), when He manifests His own Self as contracted — He Himself, at that time: the non-recognition of His own full nature, which though appearing is of the form of non-reflective-grasping — that very thing being set forth as the cause — he whose principle is merely the non-manifestation of fullness

children.text: nanu sṛṣṭāvityanena kiṃ vyavacchedyaṃ kiṃ ca saṃgrāhyam ? ityāha ----
children.translated_text: Objection: By [the phrase] 'in creation,' what is to be excluded and what is to be included? To this he says:

children.text: svāṅgarūpeṣu bhāveṣu patyurjñānaṃ kriyā ca yā /
children.translated_text: When entities are of the nature of one's own limbs, the knowledge and action that belong to the Lord —

children.text: māyātṛtīye te eva paśoḥ sattvaṃ rajastamaḥ //
children.translated_text: in the <s>Māyā</s>-domain, the third [level], those very [knowledge and action] are, for the bound soul, <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. //

children.text: viśvarūpasya bhagavataḥ svarūpabhūta eva viśvatra yaḥ prakāśo yaśca vimarśaḥ , te tāvajjñānakriye svarūpadvayaparāmarśa eva viśrāntam ahamidamitisadāśiveśvaraparamārthaṃ sā bhagavato māyāśaktiḥ , tā etāstisraḥ śaktayo bhagavati naisargikyo'sṛṣṭāḥ / svarūpāparijñāne tu bhinneṣu bhāveṣu jñānaṃ kriyā , śuddhameva bhinnatvaṃ prakāśavimarśaśūnyam , ---- iti paśoḥ prakāśaḥ prakāśāprakāśāvaprakāśaśca iti krameṇa sukhaduḥkhamohalakṣaṇāni prakāśakriyāniyamaśīlāni sattvarajastamāṃsi //4//
children.translated_text: Of the Blessed One whose form is the universe, the luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>) and reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) that exist in the universal [domain] as belonging to His own essential nature — those, being knowledge and action, resting in the reflective grasping of the dual essential nature 'I am this' — in the ultimate reality of <s>Sadāśiva</s>-<s>Īśvara</s> — that is the Blessed One's <s>Māyā-śakti</s>; these three powers are innate in the Blessed One, uncreated. But when there is non-recognition of one's own essential nature, in differentiated entities, knowledge [and] action — pure differentiation, devoid of luminosity and reflective awareness — thus, for the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), luminosity, luminosity-and-non-luminosity, and non-luminosity — these are, in sequence, <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, characterized by pleasure, pain, and delusion respectively, having the nature of regulation of luminosity and action. // 4 //

children.text: nanu caivaṃ sati yathā parmeśvarasya jñānakriyāmāyā avyatirekaṇyaḥ śaktayaḥ , ---- ityucyante , tadvat paśoḥ sattvarajastamā/msi prasajyante , vyatiriktāni ca tāni puṃsttvād gaṇyante , tadetat katham ? iti saṃśayaṃ śamayati
children.translated_text: Objection: If this is so, then just as the Supreme Lord's knowledge, action, and <s>Māyā</s> are called inseparable powers, in the same way, for the bound soul, <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> would follow [as inseparable] — and yet they are counted as separate from <s>puruṣa</s>! How is this? He resolves this doubt:
Abiding in differentiation, the status of being powers is not attributed
to these <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), which undergo transformation into instruments and effects. //

children.text: satyam evaṃ syāt yadi bhedagraha na bhavet , bhedastvayaṃ vicāryate / tatra ca saṃkucitacinmātrasvabhāvaḥ puruṣo , nāsya naisargikaṃ bhāvaviṣayaṃ prakāśanādi rūpaṃ sarvadā tatprasaṅgāt , api tvanyasaṃbandhakṛtam / tataśca tasmāt paśoḥ śaktimattvena śaṅkyamānād bhedena yata etāni sattvādīni , tataḥ śaktayo vyatirekamuktāḥ ---- iti nocyante kiṃ tūpakaraṇatvāt

children.translated_text: '<s>guṇas</s>' (qualities) —

children.text: ityucyante / nanu puruṣāt kimiti te bhedenocyante ? , ucyate , iha sukhaduḥkhamohapariṇāmarūpametatkaraṇatrayodaśakaṃ kāryadaśakaṃ ca sukhādisvabhāvatvenānubhūyate , ---- iti sukhaduḥkhamohāḥ karaṇakāryavargatādātmyavṛttayo yadi puruṣavyāpi tādātmyaṃ bhajeran tarhi puruṣaḥ kāryakaraṇaparyantasṛṣṭimayaḥ saṃpannaḥ , pariṇāmaśca dūṣitaḥ ---- iti svātantryaśaktyā puruṣo viśvarūpaḥ , ---- ityāyātam / tathā ca na kaścit puruṣa īśvara eva , tasmāt apratyabhijñānamayapuruṣasvarūpavicāre sattvādayo bhinnā eva , ---- iti sthitam //5//
children.translated_text: they are called. Objection: Why are they said to be different from <s>puruṣa</s>? Reply: Here, this which is of the form of the transformation of pleasure, pain, and delusion — the thirteen instruments and the ten effects — is experienced as being of the nature of pleasure and such. Therefore, if pleasure, pain, and delusion — which operate in identity with the class of instruments and effects — were to adopt identity pervading <s>puruṣa</s>, then <s>puruṣa</s> would be constituted as consisting of creation extending to effects and instruments, and [his] transformation would be vitiated — thus [it would follow that] through the power of freedom, <s>puruṣa</s> is of universal form — and this outcome [is what the opponent gets]. And thus, no <s>puruṣa</s> [would be different from] the Lord Himself. Therefore, when examining the essential nature of <s>puruṣa</s> as consisting of non-recognition, <s>sattva</s> and such are indeed different — this is established. // 5 //

True — it would be so if there were no apprehension of differentiation. But this very differentiation is being examined. Therein, <s>puruṣa</s> is of the nature of contracted consciousness alone — his nature of illuminating objects and such is not innate to him at all times, since the unwanted consequence [of constant manifestation] would follow; rather, it is produced through connection with something else. And therefore, since these — <s>sattva</s> and such — exist in differentiation from that bound soul who is suspected of being a possessor of powers, they are said to be powers that are separate — they are not called [powers], but rather, because of being subsidiary instruments,

children.text: nanu jñānādīni kathaṃ sattvādirūpāṇi paśuṃ prati ? ityāha
children.translated_text: Objection: How are knowledge and such of the form of <s>sattva</s> and such for the bound soul? To this he says:
Existence-bliss and action belong to the Lord; the absence of that too is that for the bound soul;
what is of the nature of both is <s>rajas</s> — that [is] pain; the cohesive [mixture] is of the nature of <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>. //

children.text: iha tāvat paritviśvasyāvabhāsavaicitryalakṣaṇeṇa sṛṣṭyādinā pālayitā svaprakāśasvabhāvaḥ , tasya viśvapateryā sattā bhavanakartṛtā sphurattārūpā pūrvaṃ vyākhyātā {sā sphurattā mahāsattā}(Ipv_1,5.14) ityatra , saiva prakāśasya vimarśāvyatirekāt vimarśātmakacamatkārarūpāsatī kriyāśaktirucyate , paraunmukhyatyāgena svātmaviśrāntirūpatvācca saiva ānandaḥ , tadevaṃ bhagavataścidātmatayaiveyadrūpatā / paśostu sattā tadabhāvaśca ānandaśca tadabhāvaśca saṃkucitatadrūpatvāt , tena yo'sau sattānandabhāgastatprakāśasukhavṛtti sattvam , yastadabhāvastadāvaraṇamoharūpaṃ tamaḥ , ete ca te sattvatamasī nīlānīlavat parasparaparihāreṇa yadyapi vartete kāryakāraṇatvavat tayāpi ekaparāmarśagocarīkāryadharmyapekṣayā citrapataṅgasaṃgatanīlānīlātmakarūpanyāyenānyonyamiśratayāpi bhātaḥ , ato yo'yaṃ

children.translated_text: 'of the nature of both' —

children.text: miśrasvabhāvaḥ tadrajoguṇaḥ , ata eva prakāśāprakāśasvarūpayoḥ sattvatamasoratra śleṣeṇāvasthānam iti duḥkhatvam ; priyaputrāderekaghana eva hi prakāśaḥ sukham ; ekaghana evāprakāśo mohaḥ / yastu kathañcitprakāśo yathā savyādhikadeharūpatayānabhimatayā , kathañciccāprakāśo yathā gatagadakalyāṇadharmayogitayābhimatayā tadeva duḥkhatvam ; ayameva ca pūrvāparībhāvasāraḥ kriyāparamārthaḥ / atrānubhayarūpatvaṃ tu nāsti , pratītau kasyāṃcit kalpitākalpitarūpāyāmāmananupraveśāt tasya / tathā hi ---- nīlaṃ tāvadakalpitarūpāyāṃ dhiyi bhāti ; nīlābhāvastu tuccho 'pi kalpanākalpita ābhāsamānatvāt tāvadvyavahāraparamārthaḥ , tadubhayavyābhiśraṇāttu nīlānīlaṃ bhātu nāma , yattvanubhayarūpaṃ tannīlapratītyā tāvadakalpitayā na viṣayīkṛtaṃ cet tat kalpitāmanīladhiyamanudhāvet , atha tāṃ kalpitāṃ dhiyaṃ nāviśatyakalpitayā viṣayīkṛtaṃ nīlameva syāt , ---- iti na paśoścaturtho'sti guṇaḥ / apiśabdaścārye , paśoḥ sā sattā sattvam , tadabhāvastamaḥ , dvayātmā rajaśca , ---- iti saṃbandhaḥ //6//
children.translated_text: Of a mixed nature is <s>rajas</s> (activity). For this very reason, since luminosity and non-luminosity — <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s> — abide here through adhesion, it has the nature of suffering. For an exclusive concentration of luminosity, such as in a beloved son, is pleasure; an exclusive concentration of non-luminosity is delusion. But what is somewhat luminous — as in a body with disease, being undesirable in form — and somewhat non-luminous — as in [a body that], having attained the recovery and auspicious state, is desirable — that very thing is suffering. And this is the essence of becoming-prior-and-posterior, the ultimate reality of action. And there is no nature of neither-of-the-two here, because in no cognition, whether constructed or unconstructed, does it fail to enter. For thus: blue, to begin with, appears in unconstructed cognition. But the absence of blue, even though empty, being a constructed appearance, is to that extent a practical reality of convention. Through the intermixture of both, let 'blue-non-blue' appear — but what is of neither-nature, if not made an object by the unconstructed cognition of blue, then it would follow the constructed cognition of non-blue. And if it does not enter even that constructed cognition, then what has been made an object by the unconstructed [cognition] would be blue alone. Therefore, for the bound soul there is no fourth <s>guṇa</s>. The word 'api' is in the sense of emphasis. For the bound soul, existence is <s>sattva</s>, the absence of that is <s>tamas</s>, and what is of dual nature is <s>rajas</s> — this is the connection. //6//

Here, first: the protector of the universe through the creation and such characterized by the variety of the manifestation of appearances, whose essential nature is self-luminous — His, the Lord of the universe's, existence (<s>sattā</s>) — the effulgent (<s>sphurattā</s>) nature of being-the-creator — was previously explained as {that effulgence is the great existence} (<s>Īpv</s> 1,5.14). That itself, due to the non-difference of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) from luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>), being of the form of the aesthetic relish (<s>camatkāra</s>) which is reflective awareness, is called the power of action (<s>kriyā-śakti</s>); and through abandoning the turning toward another, being of the form of repose in one's own Self, that itself is bliss (<s>ānanda</s>). Thus, for the Blessed One, this nature [obtains] precisely through being of the consciousness-Self. But for the bound soul, existence and the absence thereof, bliss and the absence thereof — due to his being a contracted form of that. Therefore, that which is the portion of existence-and-bliss — that is <s>sattva</s>, operating as luminosity and pleasure; that which is the absence thereof — that is <s>tamas</s>, of the form of obscuration and delusion. And these, <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>, like blue and non-blue, though they exist in mutual exclusion, like cause and effect — nevertheless, with reference to a substrate brought into the scope of a single reflective grasping, they also appear as mixed with one another, by the principle of blue-and-non-blue-natured form conjoined like a variegated moth. Therefore, that which is

children.text: evaṃ tāvat patipaśurūpaṃ pramātṛtattvaṃ saṃkṣepeṇa nirṇītam ; atha prameyatattvaṃ nirṇetuṃ patyau tāvat

children.translated_text: 'this is the nature of the knowable' —
to determine this, he says:
Thus, the nature of the perceiver-principle as lord and bound soul has been briefly determined. Now, in order to determine the nature of the knowable — first in the Lord:
Even those [appearances] that are the domains of non-conventional 'this'-reflective awareness, belonging to the Lord —
they are mixed and differentiated, and thus appear in a variegated manner.

children.text: ihābhāsā eva tāvadarthāḥ , ---- ityuktam , te ca parāmarśaikyena kadācinmiśrīkriyante yadā viśeṣarūpatā , kadācidamiśrā eva parāmṛśyante yadā samānyarūpatā , te ete ubhayātmāno'pyarthā asāmāyikenākalpitenedaṃbhāvena sahajaparāmarśarūpeṇāṅgulinirdeśādiprakhyena gocarīkāryāḥ prabhorapi na kevalaṃ sadyojātabālāderyāvadīśvarasyāpi ,

children.translated_text: 'thus' —

children.text: tena sāmānyaviśeṣaprakāreṇa citratayāvabhāsante / citratvaṃ hi tayoḥ ---- yanmiśratvamamiśratvaṃ ca yugapadekāhantāviśrāntaṃ bhāti , ---- iti īśvaradaśāyāṃ bhāvollāsanāntarīyakatvena saṃvitsaṃkocarūpaṃ niṣedhyānuparaktanañarthamātrarūpaṃ śūnyaṃ saṃvitprakāśenaiva prakāśamānamahantāniṣedharūpāmasāmāyikīmidantāmullāsayati //7//
children.translated_text: in the manner of universal and particular, they appear in a variegated way. The variegatedness of these two consists in this: that mixedness and unmixedness appear simultaneously, resting in a single I-awareness. Thus, at the level of the Lord, as necessarily entailed by the efflorescence of entities, the void — which is of the nature of the contraction of consciousness, whose form is merely the meaning of negation colored by what is to be negated — being illuminated by the very light of consciousness, manifests a non-conventional 'this'-ness of the nature of the negation of I-awareness. //7//

Here, appearances alone are objects — as has been stated. And they are sometimes mixed through the unity of reflective grasping — when there is the form of the particular; and sometimes unmixed, reflectively grasped [separately] — when there is the form of the universal. These objects of both natures, even for the Lord, are to be made objects through the non-conventional, unconstructed 'this'-ness — a natural reflective awareness of the nature of pointing with the finger and such — not only for a newborn child and such, but even up to the <s>Īśvara</s> [level],

children.text: evaṃ tāvadīśvararūpasya patyuritthaṃ prameyatattvaṃ , paramaśive tu bhagavati prameyakathaiva kathamuttiṣṭhati , prameyakathotthāpakatvameva bhagavataḥ sadāśiveśvaratvam ; ato 'dhunā paśuṃ prati kīdṛk prameyasya vṛttāntaḥ , ---- iti sandehamapohati ślokatrayeṇa ----
children.translated_text: Thus, the nature of the knowable for the Lord who is of the nature of <s>Īśvara</s> [has been stated]. But in the Supreme <s>Śiva</s>, how does any discourse about the knowable arise? The very raising of the discourse about the knowable is the Lord's <s>Sadāśiva</s>-<s>Īśvara</s> nature. Therefore, now the question is: with respect to the bound soul, what is the state of affairs of the knowable? He dispels the doubt in three verses:
But for the individual self, those objects whose appearances are differentiated are to be constructed,
through the respective distinct designations, in the domain of memory, imaginative extrapolation, and such.
His creation, which is uncommon and depends on the Lord's creation —
this too is truly by the Lord's power, through ignorance, being of His nature,
through the activity of conceptual construction, which is of the nature of the vital breath,
agitated for obstructing one's own resting in Self, and characterized by the variety of this and that letter.

Objection: If those very things that are not conceptualized are conceptualized when they are conceptualized, what is the difference in the knowable between its lord-nature and bound-soul-nature? Reply: 'Tasya' (his): the creation by the bound soul of those objects already created by the Lord revolves upon [the Lord's creation]. Therefore, being dependent on the Lord's creation, it is uncommon — fixed for each individual perceiver. For example:

children.translated_text: Objection: If so, what is the difference for the bound and the liberated with respect to the knowable? Reply:
The liberated one considers the common knowable as non-different from his own Self,
like <s>Maheśvara</s>; but the bound one, as if absolutely different.

children.text: śrīmatsadāśiveśvarapadādārabhya krimiparyantapramātṛvargādhiṣṭhātṛ yadahamitirūpaṃ tadevātmatayābhiniviśate muktaḥ , tataśca viśvasyāpi prameyaṃ mamāpi , mama prameyaṃ viśvasyāpi , prameyaṃ cedaṃ mamaivāṅgabhūtaṃ prameyāntaramapi tathā , ---- ityanena krameṇa prameyaṃ prasparataśca pramātṛvargāccāvyāvṛttam , ---- ityekarasābhedaviśrāntitattvamasya sarvaṃ parāmarśapadamupaiti / baddhasya tu sarvametadviparītam , ---- ityekarasabhedadaviśrānta eṣāsau //13//
children.translated_text: The liberated one enters as his own Self that which shines as 'I,' which presides over the group of perceivers from the illustrious <s>Sadāśiva</s>-<s>Īśvara</s> level down to a worm. Thus, everything attains the ground of reflective grasping as the principle of resting in non-difference as a single essence. But for the bound one, all this is the reverse. Thus, this [knowable] rests in difference as a single essence. //13//

children.text: nanu sadāśivedśvarabhuvi jīvanmuktipade baddharūpapaśupramātṛviṣaye ca prameyavṛttāntaḥ parīkṣitaḥ , paramaśive tu kathamasau ? ityāśaṅkyāha ----
children.translated_text: Objection: The state of the knowable has been examined at the <s>Sadāśiva</s>-<s>Īśvara</s> level, at the stage of <s>jīvanmukti</s>, and in the domain of the bound-soul perceiver. But how is it in the Supreme <s>Śiva</s>? Anticipating this, he says:
But in every way, filled with the flood of infinite principles dissolved within,
<s>Śiva</s> is a dense mass of consciousness and bliss, whose body is the supreme imperishable.

children.text: na khalu bhagavati śrīparamaśive prameyakayā kācidasti , tattvaughasya sarvathā tatra cidrūpatāmātraviśrāntatvena līnatvāt , tataśca sāvasthā saṃvitsvabhāvena svātmaviśrāntyānandena akṛtrimanaisargikaparāmarśātmakasvātmacamatkāralakṣaṇemaikadhanā avicchinnatadrūpā paramākṣareṇa vigrahavatī bhagavato viśvamayasyānavacchinnānuttaradhāmno nityaśuddhasya galitaprameyakathā sarvottīrṇā vyapadiśyate //14//
children.translated_text: Indeed, in the Supreme <s>Śiva</s>, there is no discourse about the knowable whatsoever — since the flood of principles, in every way, rests there solely in the form of consciousness, and is thus dissolved. And therefore, that state, by its nature as consciousness, by the bliss of resting in its own Self, by the marvel of its own Self whose nature is the unartificial, natural reflective awareness, is a single dense mass, of unbroken such-nature, embodied in the supreme imperishable — [the state] of the Blessed One who is of the nature of the universe, whose abode is unlimited and unsurpassed, who is eternally pure, in whom the discourse of the knowable has been dissolved, who transcends everything — thus it is designated. //14//

That very [approach] has here been brought to full clarity through the removal of the blemish-suspicion of opposing doctrines. Since this meaning is established by scripture, teacher, and one's own experience — therefore, settling the reflective awareness (<s>parāmarśa</s>) upon the domain of the object of knowledge, having realized in oneself the sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) characterized as universal agency, when one reflects upon it with firmness — then, by the mere force of that reflective awareness, one is at once a <s>jīvanmukta</s> (liberated while living), the Blessed Lord <s>Śiva</s> Himself. As stated by our supreme master:
{When <s>Śiva</s>-hood, which abides in everything, is known through firm ascertainment,

Objection: Purposeful activity whose essence is repose in the perceiver has not been observed without recognition, [but] when that [recognition] is present, it has been observed — where has this been established? Anticipating this, he says:

Objection: If the entity called the Self is just that [always], then there would be no difference between its recognition and non-recognition — for surely there is no insistence upon a seed [requiring] non-recognition? Similarly, the Self of the world, [though] the Lord of the universe, whose qualities are thus unregarded,

children.text: yadā nāyakaguṇasaṃśravaṇapravṛddhānurāgā kāminī taddarśanameva paramupādeyamākāṅkṣantī divāniśamavaśahṛdayā devatopayācitāni dūtīsaṃpreṣaṇāni madalekhadvārakātmāvasthānivedanāni kurvāṇā virahakṣāmībhavadgātralatikā tiṣṭhati , tadā tadupayācitavaśāt aśaṅkitameva savidhavartini priyatame'valokite taistairutkarṣaviśeṣaiḥ parāmarśapadavīmagacchadbhirjanasādhāraṇatāmāpādite saṃpannamapi priyatamāvalokanaṃ na hṛdayaṃ pūrṇīkaroti ; tathā svātmani viśveśvare satataṃ nirbhāsamāne'pi tannirbhāsanaṃ na hṛḍayasya pūrṇatāmādhatte ; yataḥ sopyātmā viśvajñatvakartṛtvādyapratihatasvaśaktilakṣaṇapāramaiśvaryotkarṣayogena na parāmṛṣṭaḥ ---- iti bhāsamānaghaṭāditulyavṛttānto jātaḥ / yadā tu dūtīvacanādvā tallakṣaṇābhijñānādvopāyāntarādvā tānutkarṣān hṛdayaṅgamīkaraṇenāmṛśati , tadā tatkṣaṇamadbhutaphullanyāyenaiva tāvat kāmapi pūrṇatāmabhyeti , paribhogābhyāsarase tu viśrāntyantarāṇyapi labhate ; tadvadātmani guruvacanājjñānakriyālakṣaṇaśaktyabhijñānādervā yadā pāramaiśvaryotkarṣahṛdayaṅgamībhāvo jāyate , tadā tatlakṣaṇameva pūrṇatātmikā jīvanmuktiḥ ; samāveśābhyāsarase tu vibhūtilābhaḥ ---- iti tasya pratyabhijñaiva parāparasiddhipradāyinī bhavati //17//
children.translated_text: When a young woman (<s>kāminī</s>), whose love has been nourished by hearing of the hero's qualities, longing for his very sight as supremely desirable, day and night with a heart beyond her control — making entreaties to deities, dispatching messengers, communicating her own condition through love-letters — stands with her body-creeper wasting away from separation; then, when by the power of those entreaties, the beloved, standing unexpectedly in her vicinity, is seen — but [seen as] rendered common among ordinary people by those very special excellences reaching the path of reflective awareness — even though the sight of the beloved has been accomplished, it does not fill the heart. Similarly, even though the Self, the Lord of the universe, constantly shines, that shining does not bring fullness to the heart; because that Self too, with the supreme excellence of sovereignty (<s>pārameśvarya</s>) characterized by unrestricted powers such as omniscience and omnipotence — has not been reflectively grasped — and thus has become equal in status to a manifest pot and such. But when, through the words of a messenger, or through recognition of his distinguishing marks, or through some other means, she reflectively grasps those excellences by taking them to heart — then, at that very instant, by the principle of sudden astonishing blossoming, she attains a certain fullness at once; and with the ripening of the practice of enjoyment, she also attains intermediate states of repose. Similarly, regarding the Self, when through the words of the teacher, or through recognition of the powers characterized as knowledge and action, and such, the taking-to-heart of the supreme excellence of sovereignty arises — then that itself is the fullness-natured <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living); and with the ripening of the practice of <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption), there is the attainment of [supernatural] glories (<s>vibhūtis</s>). Thus, the recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) of Him alone is the bestower of the supreme-and-proximate attainments. // 17 //

children.text: sarvopakārakaṃ mahāphalamidaṃ śāstraṃ prasiddhānvayayogena nāmadheyaprasiddhyā ca tadutkarṣasmaraṇadvārajanitasaṃbhāvanāpratyayalakṣaṇapravartakasaṃvedanayā janaṃ praavrtayituṃ piturnāmnā copasaṃhāraṃ darśayati
children.translated_text: Showing the conclusion of this treatise, which is of great fruit and beneficial to all, with his father's name — through the means of inciting people by the prompting cognition characterized by the presumption (<s>saṃbhāvanā</s>) born from the memory of his eminence through the fame of lineage and the fame of name — he says:
For the effortless attainment of anyone, by the son of <s>Udayākara</s>,
this Recognition of the Lord (<s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s>) has been set forth by <s>Utpala</s>. //

children.text: yasya kasyacijjantoriti nātra jātyādyapekṣā kācit ---- iti sarvopakāritvamuktam / ayatnena siddhiḥ parāpararūpā yathā syāt ---- iti mahāphalattvam / udayākaraputraḥ śrīmānutpaladevo'smatparamagururidaṃ śāstramakārṣīt ---- iti tatprasiddyā janaḥ pravartate ---- iti pravartanādvāreṇa so'nugṛhīto bhavati ---- ityubhayanāmanirdeśaḥ / iyamiti hṛdayaṅgamatāmupapattiśatairānītā / iti śivam //18// āditaḥ 190//
children.translated_text: 'Of any being whatsoever' — thus there is no requirement of caste or such here — this states its universal beneficence. 'Effortless attainment' of the supreme-and-proximate form — this [states] its great fruitfulness. The son of <s>Udayākara</s>, the glorious <s>Utpaladeva</s>, our supreme guru, composed this treatise — thus by his fame people are incited — thus through the door of incitement he becomes the bestower of grace — hence the indication of both names. 'This' — [indicates] that which has been brought to the heart through hundreds of proofs. Thus, may there be auspiciousness! // 18 // From the beginning, 190 [verses]. //
{This brief and unbroken commentary (<s>vṛtti</s>) on the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>,
which is a reflective investigation of the meaning of the <s>sūtras</s>, has been composed by <s>Abhinavagupta</s>. //}
{The meanings of sentences, valid means of knowledge, categories, principles, and true scriptural meanings — from no [source] other than one's own treatise do they attain application to the Self.

children.text: bhaumān rasāñjalamayāṃśca na sasyapuṣṭau muktvārkamekamiha yojayituṃ kṣamo'nyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Who other than the sun alone is capable of harnessing the earthly and aqueous essences for the nourishment of crops?
One who, without knowing himself, wishes to discriminate other [things] —

children.text: tena bhautena kiṃ vācyaṃ praśne'sminko bhavāniti //}
children.translated_text: what is to be said to that fool when the question is 'Who are you?' //}

Thus, in the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s> composed by the venerable master <s>Utpaladeva</s>, accompanied by the commentary called <s>Vimarśinī</s> composed by the venerable master <s>Abhinavagupta</s> — [this is] the <s>Tattvasaṅgrahādhikāra</s> (Section on the Summary of Principles). The glorious <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s> is complete. //
